1	name: Release
2	
3	# Triggers on `v*` tag pushes. Produces:
4	#   - orva-linux-{amd64,arm64}       (Go binary, static)
5	#   - nsjail-linux-{amd64,arm64}     (built from source, stripped)
6	#   - rootfs-{node,python}-{amd64,arm64}.tar.zst
7	#                                    (extracted from official Docker slim
8	#                                    images + adapter pre-installed)
9	#   - checksums.txt                  (sha256 of every asset)
10	#   - ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest (multi-arch OCI image, amd64 + arm64)
11	#
12	# Versioning lives in the GitHub Release (binaries, installers, changelog).
13	# The Docker image carries exactly one tag, :latest; there is no per-version
14	# image tag. `docker pull ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest` resolves the right
15	# architecture automatically.
16	#
17	# All release assets are attached to the GitHub Release and linked from
18	# install.sh via https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/latest/download/...
19	#
20	# Manual trigger (workflow_dispatch) is allowed for rc builds — they publish
21	# to the Release draft; the Docker image is still only :latest.
22	
23	on:
24	  push:
25	    tags: ["v*"]
26	  workflow_dispatch:
27	    inputs:
28	      tag:
29	        description: "release tag (e.g. v0.3.0) — required for workflow_dispatch"
30	        required: true
31	      force:
32	        description: "skip the verification gate (emergency / rc only)"
33	        type: boolean
34	        default: false
35	
36	permissions:
37	  contents: write   # create releases, upload assets
38	  packages: write   # push to ghcr.io
39	  actions: read     # gate job reads CI/e2e run status for the tagged commit
40	
41	env:
42	  IMAGE_NAME: ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva
43	
44	jobs:
45	  # ── 0. Gate — verify, don't re-test ──────────────────────────────────
46	  # The release pipeline does NOT run tests. All verification (shellcheck,
47	  # go vet/test/build, ui build, docker smoke, full e2e) already ran on the
48	  # PR and on the push to main. This job only CONFIRMS the tagged commit is
49	  # green — a status lookup, not a test run — so the release stays fast while
50	  # a tag can still never ship code whose tests failed. Every build job
51	  # `needs: gate`. `workflow_dispatch` with force=true skips it (rc/emergency).
52	  gate:
53	    name: gate (verify CI + e2e already passed)
54	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
55	    steps:
56	      - name: resolve commit SHA for the tag
57	        id: sha
58	        env:
59	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
60	        run: |
61	          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
62	            TAG="${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}"
63	            SHA="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${TAG}" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null || true)"
64	            [ -z "$SHA" ] && SHA="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/git/ref/tags/${TAG}" --jq .object.sha 2>/dev/null || true)"
65	          else
66	            SHA="${GITHUB_SHA}"
67	          fi
68	          [ -n "$SHA" ] || { echo "::error::could not resolve a commit SHA to gate on"; exit 1; }
69	          echo "sha=$SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
70	          echo "gating on commit $SHA"
71	
72	      - name: require CI + e2e success on that commit
73	        if: ${{ github.event.inputs.force != 'true' }}
74	        env:
75	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
76	          SHA: ${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}
77	        run: |
78	          set -euo pipefail
79	          # Confirm the tagged commit's verification is green — a status lookup,
80	          # not a test run. Poll until the workflow completes (handles tagging
81	          # right after the merge push), bounded so a stuck check can't hang the
82	          # release. `hard` = must exist and succeed; `soft` = must succeed IF it
83	          # ran (ci.yml is path-filtered, so a docs-only release commit may have
84	          # no CI run — e2e always runs on a main push and actually builds + runs
85	          # the server, so it's the hard gate).
86	          check() {
87	            local wf="$1" mode="$2" deadline=$((SECONDS + 1200))  # ~20 min cap
88	            while :; do
89	              read -r status conclusion < <(gh api \
90	                "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/${wf}/runs?head_sha=${SHA}&per_page=1" \
91	                --jq '.workflow_runs[0] | "\(.status) \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || echo "null null")
92	              if [ "$status" = "null" ]; then
93	                if [ "$mode" = "soft" ]; then echo "• $wf: no run for $SHA (path-filtered) — skipping"; return 0; fi
94	                echo "::error::no $wf run for $SHA — commit was not verified (use force=true to override)"; return 1
95	              fi
96	              if [ "$status" = "completed" ]; then
97	                [ "$conclusion" = "success" ] && { echo "✓ $wf succeeded for $SHA"; return 0; }
98	                echo "::error::$wf for $SHA concluded '$conclusion' — refusing to release an unverified commit"; return 1
99	              fi
100	              [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ] || { echo "::error::timed out waiting for $wf on $SHA"; return 1; }
101	              echo "… $wf is '$status' for $SHA — waiting"; sleep 20
102	            done
103	          }
104	          check e2e.yml hard
105	          check ci.yml  soft
106	          echo "gate passed: verification is green for $SHA"
107	
108	  # ── 1. Go binary: matrix amd64 + arm64 ───────────────────────────────
109	  build-orva:
110	    name: build orva (${{ matrix.goarch }})
111	    needs: gate
112	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
113	    strategy:
114	      matrix:
115	        goarch: [amd64, arm64]
116	    steps:
117	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
118	
119	      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
120	        with:
121	          go-version: "1.26.x"
122	          # No build cache — every release builds from scratch so we
123	          # can't accidentally ship a stale toolchain artifact.
124	          cache: false
125	
126	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
127	        with:
128	          node-version: "24"
129	          # No npm cache — fresh install on every run.
130	          cache: ""
131	
132	      - name: build ui
133	        working-directory: frontend
134	        run: |
135	          npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
136	          npm run build
137	
138	      - name: embed ui + adapters
139	        run: |
140	          rm -rf backend/internal/server/ui_dist
141	          cp -r frontend/dist backend/internal/server/ui_dist
142	          make adapters-embed
143	
144	      - name: resolve build identity
145	        id: v
146	        run: |
147	          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
148	            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
149	          else
150	            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
151	          fi
152	          echo "commit=${GITHUB_SHA::7}"               >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
153	          echo "build_time=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
154	
155	      - name: go build
156	        env:
157	          GOOS: linux
158	          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
159	          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
160	        run: |
161	          mkdir -p dist
162	          go build \
163	            -trimpath \
164	            -ldflags="-s -w \
165	              -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Version=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }} \
166	              -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Commit=${{ steps.v.outputs.commit }} \
167	              -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.BuildTime=${{ steps.v.outputs.build_time }}" \
168	            -o dist/orva-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }} \
169	            ./backend/cmd/orva
170	
171	      - name: upload artifact
172	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
173	        with:
174	          name: orva-${{ matrix.goarch }}
175	          path: dist/orva-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }}
176	          if-no-files-found: error
177	          retention-days: 7
178	
179	  # ── 1b. Standalone CLI binaries (Linux + macOS + Windows × amd64/arm64) ──
180	  # Slim CLI built from the dedicated ./cli/cmd/orva entry point — no
181	  # server packages, no embedded UI/adapters/docs/MCP. Cross-compiled
182	  # from a single ubuntu runner: pure Go, CGO disabled, fully static.
183	  # Windows builds get the .exe suffix.
184	  build-cli:
185	    name: build orva-cli (${{ matrix.goos }}/${{ matrix.goarch }})
186	    needs: gate
187	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
188	    strategy:
189	      matrix:
190	        include:
191	          - goos: linux
192	            goarch: amd64
193	          - goos: linux
194	            goarch: arm64
195	          - goos: darwin
196	            goarch: amd64
197	          - goos: darwin
198	            goarch: arm64
199	          - goos: windows
200	            goarch: amd64
201	            ext: ".exe"
202	          - goos: windows
203	            goarch: arm64
204	            ext: ".exe"
205	    steps:
206	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
207	
208	      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
209	        with:
210	          go-version: "1.26.x"
211	          # No build cache — every release builds from scratch so we
212	          # can't accidentally ship a stale toolchain artifact.
213	          cache: false
214	
215	      - name: resolve build identity
216	        id: v
217	        run: |
218	          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
219	            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
220	          else
221	            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
222	          fi
223	          echo "commit=${GITHUB_SHA::7}"               >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
224	          echo "build_time=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
225	
226	      - name: go build (slim cli)
227	        env:
228	          GOOS: ${{ matrix.goos }}
229	          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
230	          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
231	        run: |
232	          mkdir -p dist
233	          OUT="dist/orva-cli-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}${{ matrix.ext }}"
234	          # Slim CLI imports only cli/commands — main.Version is the right
235	          # ldflags target here (it forwards into commands.Version).
236	          go build \
237	            -trimpath \
238	            -ldflags="-s -w -X main.Version=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}" \
239	            -o "$OUT" \
240	            ./cli/cmd/orva
241	          file "$OUT" || true
242	          ls -lh "$OUT"
243	
244	      - name: upload artifact
245	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
246	        with:
247	          name: orva-cli-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}
248	          path: dist/orva-cli-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}${{ matrix.ext }}
249	          if-no-files-found: error
250	          retention-days: 7
251	
252	  # ── 2. nsjail: per-arch standalone binary (release asset only) ───────
253	  # The container image's nsjail comes from inside the unified Dockerfile
254	  # (its `FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS nsjail` stage), so this job is
255	  # solely for producing the standalone `nsjail-linux-{amd64,arm64}`
256	  # binary that ships as a GitHub release asset for bare-metal installs.
257	  #
258	  # Why container: debian:bookworm-slim
259	  # ───────────────────────────────────
260	  # nsjail is a C++ binary that dynamically links against libprotobuf,
261	  # libnl-route-3, libstdc++, libcap, libc. Built on the ubuntu-24.04
262	  # host runner (glibc 2.39 / libstdc++ 14 / GLIBCXX_3.4.32+), the
263	  # binary carries symbol references too new for the bookworm-class
264	  # runtime its install.sh seeds it into — at which point dynamic
265	  # linking aborts at exec with
266	  #   "libprotobuf.so.32: cannot open shared object file"
267	  # then, after that lib is added,
268	  #   "version `GLIBC_2.38' not found"
269	  # Building inside debian:bookworm-slim matches the binary's symbol
270	  # references to the install target on every supported kernel
271	  # (Linux ≥ 3.2, which covers every system anyone deploys this on).
272	  build-nsjail:
273	    name: build nsjail (${{ matrix.goarch }})
274	    needs: gate
275	    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
276	    container: debian:bookworm-slim
277	    strategy:
278	      matrix:
279	        include:
280	          - goarch: amd64
281	            runner: ubuntu-24.04
282	          - goarch: arm64
283	            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
284	    steps:
285	      # No actions/checkout: the job clones nsjail upstream and produces
286	      # one binary; no Orva repo files are read here.
287	
288	      - name: install build deps
289	        run: |
290	          apt-get update
291	          apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
292	            ca-certificates git make gcc g++ autoconf bison flex libtool pkg-config \
293	            libprotobuf-dev libnl-route-3-dev protobuf-compiler
294	
295	      - name: build nsjail from source
296	        run: |
297	          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/google/nsjail.git /tmp/nsjail
298	          cd /tmp/nsjail
299	          make -j"$(nproc)"
300	          strip nsjail
301	          file ./nsjail
302	          # Confirm the binary's NEEDED dyn deps match what the runtime
303	          # apt list installs (libprotobuf32, libnl-route-3-200,
304	          # libcap2-bin, libstdc++6, libc6). If a future libprotobuf
305	          # bookworm bump renames the .so version, this readlink + dump
306	          # output will surface in the workflow log immediately.
307	          objdump -p ./nsjail | grep NEEDED || true
308	          cp ./nsjail nsjail-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }}
309	
310	      - name: upload artifact
311	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
312	        with:
313	          name: nsjail-${{ matrix.goarch }}
314	          path: /tmp/nsjail/nsjail-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }}
315	          if-no-files-found: error
316	          retention-days: 7
317	
318	  # ── 3. Language rootfs tarballs ───────────────────────────────────────
319	  build-rootfs:
320	    name: rootfs ${{ matrix.runtime }} (${{ matrix.goarch }})
321	    needs: gate
322	    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
323	    strategy:
324	      fail-fast: false
325	      matrix:
326	        runtime: [node, python]
327	        goarch: [amd64, arm64]
328	        include:
329	          - goarch: amd64
330	            runner: ubuntu-24.04
331	          - goarch: arm64
332	            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
333	    steps:
334	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
335	
336	      - name: install zstd
337	        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends zstd
338	
339	      - name: extract rootfs via docker export
340	        run: |
341	          set -euo pipefail
342	          bash scripts/build-rootfs.sh "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs" "${{ matrix.runtime }}"
343	
344	          # Pre-install the adapter so install.sh doesn't need the source tree.
345	          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs/opt/orva"
346	          if [ -f "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.js" ]; then
347	            cp "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.js" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs/opt/orva/adapter.js"
348	          fi
349	          if [ -f "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.py" ]; then
350	            cp "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs/opt/orva/adapter.py"
351	          fi
352	
353	      - name: tar + zstd compress
354	        run: |
355	          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs"
356	          tar -cf - . | zstd -19 -T0 -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}.tar.zst"
357	          ls -lh "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}.tar.zst"
358	
359	      - name: upload artifact
360	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
361	        with:
362	          name: rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}
363	          path: rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}.tar.zst
364	          if-no-files-found: error
365	          retention-days: 7
366	
367	  # ── 4. Collate + compute checksums + publish GitHub Release ───────────
368	  release:
369	    name: publish github release
370	    needs: [build-orva, build-cli, build-nsjail, build-rootfs]
371	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
372	    steps:
373	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
374	
375	      - name: resolve version
376	        id: v
377	        run: |
378	          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
379	            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
380	          else
381	            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
382	          fi
383	
384	      - name: download all artifacts
385	        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
386	        with:
387	          path: artifacts
388	
389	      - name: flatten + chmod
390	        run: |
391	          set -euo pipefail
392	          mkdir -p dist
393	          find artifacts -type f -exec cp -v {} dist/ \;
394	          # Mark every Unix-style binary executable. Windows .exe doesn't
395	          # need a chmod but the no-op is harmless.
396	          chmod +x dist/orva-linux-* dist/nsjail-linux-* 2>/dev/null || true
397	          for f in dist/orva-cli-*; do
398	            case "$f" in *.exe) ;; *) chmod +x "$f" 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac
399	          done
400	          ls -lh dist/
401	
402	      - name: sha256 checksums
403	        working-directory: dist
404	        run: |
405	          sha256sum * | tee checksums.txt
406	
407	      - name: create / update github release
408	        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
409	        with:
410	          tag_name: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
411	          name: Orva ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
412	          draft: false
413	          prerelease: ${{ contains(steps.v.outputs.tag, '-rc') || contains(steps.v.outputs.tag, '-beta') }}
414	          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
415	          files: |
416	            dist/*
417	          body: |
418	            ## Orva ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
419	
420	            ### Install
421	
422	            **Docker:**
423	            ```
424	            docker run -p 8443:8443 --cap-add SYS_ADMIN \
425	              --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
426	              -v orva-data:/var/lib/orva \
427	              ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest
428	            ```
429	
430	            **Bare Linux server (POSIX installer works on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/Alpine/Arch/openSUSE):**
431	            ```
432	            curl -fsSL https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/download/${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}/install.sh | sh
433	            ```
434	
435	            **Standalone CLI (Linux + macOS):**
436	            ```
437	            curl -fsSL https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/download/${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}/install-cli.sh | sh
438	            ```
439	
440	            **Standalone CLI (Windows, PowerShell):**
441	            ```
442	            irm https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/download/${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}/install-cli.ps1 | iex
443	            ```
444	
445	            ### Release assets
446	
447	            | asset | description |
448	            |---|---|
449	            | `orva-linux-amd64`, `orva-linux-arm64` | Daemon + CLI binary (server install via `install.sh`) |
450	            | `orva-cli-linux-{amd64,arm64}` | Slim CLI (Linux) — used by `install-cli.sh` |
451	            | `orva-cli-darwin-{amd64,arm64}` | Slim CLI (macOS Intel + Apple Silicon) |
452	            | `orva-cli-windows-{amd64,arm64}.exe` | Slim CLI (Windows) — used by `install-cli.ps1` |
453	            | `nsjail-linux-{amd64,arm64}` | Pre-built nsjail (downloaded by install.sh) |
454	            | `rootfs-{node,python}-{amd64,arm64}.tar.zst` | Language rootfs |
455	            | `install.sh`, `install-cli.sh`, `install-cli.ps1` | One-line installers |
456	            | `checksums.txt` | sha256 of every asset above |
457	
458	      # Upload installer scripts alongside the release so versioned URLs work.
459	      - name: attach installer scripts
460	        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
461	        with:
462	          tag_name: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
463	          files: |
464	            scripts/install.sh
465	            scripts/install-cli.sh
466	            scripts/install-cli.ps1
467	
468	  # ── 5. Per-arch Docker image, native runners (no QEMU) ────────────────
469	  # Single source of truth: the unified Dockerfile builds UI, Go binary,
470	  # nsjail, and rootfs stages itself, all in matched debian:bookworm-slim
471	  # environments. No artifact staging from sibling jobs; no second
472	  # Dockerfile to drift. Each arch builds on its native runner so QEMU
473	  # emulation stays out of the loop (UI + npm install was the original
474	  # reason for splitting builds; native runners removed that pressure).
475	  #
476	  # Each arch pushes by digest only; the manifest job below stitches the
477	  # two digests into both `:latest` and the immutable `:${tag}`.
478	  docker-image:
479	    name: docker image (${{ matrix.goarch }})
480	    needs: gate
481	    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
482	    strategy:
483	      matrix:
484	        include:
485	          - goarch: amd64
486	            runner: ubuntu-24.04
487	            platform: linux/amd64
488	          - goarch: arm64
489	            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
490	            platform: linux/arm64
491	    outputs:
492	      digest_amd64: ${{ steps.digest_out.outputs.amd64 }}
493	      digest_arm64: ${{ steps.digest_out.outputs.arm64 }}
494	    steps:
495	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
496	
497	      - name: resolve build identity
498	        id: v
499	        run: |
500	          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
501	            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
502	          else
503	            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
504	          fi
505	          echo "commit=${GITHUB_SHA::7}"               >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
506	          echo "build_time=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
507	
508	      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
509	
510	      - name: login to ghcr.io
511	        uses: docker/login-action@v4
512	        with:
513	          registry: ghcr.io
514	          username: ${{ github.actor }}
515	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
516	
517	      # Push by digest only — no tag is created. The manifest job below
518	      # references the per-arch digests directly when stitching them
519	      # into the multi-arch :latest + :${tag} tags.
520	      - name: build + push by digest
521	        id: build
522	        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
523	        with:
524	          context: .
525	          file: Dockerfile
526	          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
527	          # No layer cache — `no-cache: true` forces every layer to
528	          # rebuild, and `pull: true` re-pulls every base image. The
529	          # release pipeline must produce bit-identical-from-scratch
530	          # output every time; cached layers can mask supply-chain
531	          # surprises (a base image gets repinned but our cache still
532	          # has the old one).
533	          no-cache: true
534	          pull: true
535	          labels: |
536	            org.opencontainers.image.title=Orva
537	            org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva
538	            org.opencontainers.image.licenses=Apache-2.0
539	            org.opencontainers.image.version=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
540	            org.opencontainers.image.revision=${{ steps.v.outputs.commit }}
541	            org.opencontainers.image.created=${{ steps.v.outputs.build_time }}
542	          build-args: |
543	            VERSION=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
544	            COMMIT=${{ steps.v.outputs.commit }}
545	            BUILD_TIME=${{ steps.v.outputs.build_time }}
546	          outputs: type=image,name=${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true
547	
548	      - name: export digest for manifest job
549	        id: digest_out
550	        run: |
551	          digest="${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}"
552	          echo "${{ matrix.goarch }}=${digest}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
553	          echo "digest_${{ matrix.goarch }}=${digest}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
554	          echo "::notice::pushed ${{ matrix.goarch }} → ${digest}"
555	
556	      - name: write digest to artifact
557	        run: |
558	          mkdir -p /tmp/digests
559	          digest="${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}"
560	          touch "/tmp/digests/${digest#sha256:}"
561	
562	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
563	        with:
564	          name: digest-${{ matrix.goarch }}
565	          path: /tmp/digests/*
566	          if-no-files-found: error
567	          retention-days: 1
568	
569	  # ── 6. Stitch the two per-arch digests into multi-arch manifest ──────
570	  # The Docker image carries exactly ONE tag: `:latest`. It is a multi-arch
571	  # manifest (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64); `docker pull` resolves the right
572	  # arch automatically. Versioning lives in the GitHub Release (binaries,
573	  # installers, changelog), NOT in image tags — we intentionally do not push
574	  # a per-version `:vYYYY.MM.DD` image tag.
575	  docker-manifest:
576	    name: docker multi-arch manifest
577	    needs: [docker-image]
578	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
579	    outputs:
580	      tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
581	    steps:
582	      - name: resolve version
583	        id: v
584	        run: |
585	          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
586	            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
587	          else
588	            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
589	          fi
590	
591	      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
592	        with:
593	          pattern: digest-*
594	          path: /tmp/digests
595	          merge-multiple: true
596	
597	      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
598	
599	      - name: login to ghcr.io
600	        uses: docker/login-action@v4
601	        with:
602	          registry: ghcr.io
603	          username: ${{ github.actor }}
604	          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
605	
606	      - name: create + push multi-arch manifest (:latest only)
607	        run: |
608	          cd /tmp/digests
609	          DIGESTS=$(printf '${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}@sha256:%s ' *)
610	          docker buildx imagetools create \
611	            -t ${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest \
612	            $DIGESTS
613	
614	      - name: inspect
615	        run: |
616	          docker buildx imagetools inspect ${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest
617	
618	  # ── 7. Prune old GHCR versions ───────────────────────────────────────
619	  # The Docker image carries exactly one tag, `:latest`. Everything in the
620	  # registry that isn't the current `:latest` manifest (or one of its
621	  # per-arch sub-images) is garbage: stale per-version tags from older
622	  # workflow versions, orphaned digests from previous `:latest` pushes.
623	  # This job deletes all of it, leaving only the live `:latest` tree.
624	  #
625	  # Runs after docker-manifest so the new :latest is pinned before we
626	  # start deleting things.
627	  cleanup-ghcr:
628	    name: prune old ghcr versions
629	    needs: [docker-manifest]
630	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
631	    permissions:
632	      packages: write
633	    steps:
634	      - name: prune everything that isn't the current release
635	        env:
636	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
637	          TAG: ${{ needs.docker-manifest.outputs.tag }}
638	          # Package is user-owned (Harsh-2002), not org-owned. If the
639	          # repo moves to an org later, change /users/ → /orgs/ and the
640	          # delete URL similarly.
641	          PKG_OWNER: Harsh-2002
642	          PKG_NAME: orva
643	        run: |
644	          set -eu
645	
646	          # Resolve the digests that make up the current :latest manifest.
647	          # docker buildx imagetools inspect emits the multi-arch manifest
648	          # with each platform's digest; we keep those + the manifest's
649	          # own digest. Everything else is fair game.
650	          docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/${PKG_OWNER}/${PKG_NAME}:latest" --raw \
651	            | jq -r '..|.digest? // empty' \
652	            | sort -u > /tmp/keep_digests.txt
653	          echo "Digests to keep (current :latest manifest + sub-images):"
654	          cat /tmp/keep_digests.txt
655	
656	          # List all versions in the package, filter to those that are
657	          # NOT in the keep-list AND don't carry the current tag or
658	          # 'latest'. Delete each one.
659	          gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
660	            "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions?per_page=100" \
661	            --paginate \
662	            --jq '.[] | "\(.id)|\(.name)|\((.metadata.container.tags // []) | join(","))"' \
663	            > /tmp/versions.txt
664	
665	          echo "Inspecting $(wc -l </tmp/versions.txt) total package versions:"
666	
667	          while IFS='|' read -r id sha tags; do
668	            keep_reason=""
669	            # 1. Keep only the 'latest' tag. Any other tag (e.g. a stale
670	            #    per-version vYYYY.MM.DD from an older workflow) is deleted.
671	            if echo ",$tags," | grep -q ",latest,"; then
672	              keep_reason="tag=$tags"
673	            # 2. Keep if version's sha256 is in the current manifest tree
674	            #    (per-arch sub-manifests pulled in via the multi-arch index).
675	            elif grep -qx "$sha" /tmp/keep_digests.txt; then
676	              keep_reason="part of current :latest manifest"
677	            # 3. Keep all untagged versions. A multi-arch manifest references
678	            #    its per-architecture sub-images by digest only — they appear
679	            #    untagged in the GHCR versions API. Deleting them breaks
680	            #    `docker pull` on the parent manifest. The keep_digests
681	            #    extraction above is best-effort and may miss some sub-image
682	            #    digests (e.g. attestation manifests); this branch is the
683	            #    safety net. Small storage cost; large reliability win.
684	            elif [ -z "$tags" ]; then
685	              keep_reason="untagged (likely a sub-image manifest)"
686	            fi
687	
688	            if [ -n "$keep_reason" ]; then
689	              echo "  keep   id=$id tags=$tags ($keep_reason)"
690	              continue
691	            fi
692	
693	            echo "  delete id=$id tags=$tags"
694	            gh api -X DELETE \
695	              -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
696	              "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions/${id}" \
697	              || echo "::warning::failed to delete version $id (continuing)"
698	          done < /tmp/versions.txt
699	
700	          echo "::notice::GHCR cleanup complete — only :latest + its sub-images + untagged versions remain."
701

file.content:
name: Release

# Triggers on `v*` tag pushes. Produces:
#   - orva-linux-{amd64,arm64}       (Go binary, static)
#   - nsjail-linux-{amd64,arm64}     (built from source, stripped)
#   - rootfs-{node,python}-{amd64,arm64}.tar.zst
#                                    (extracted from official Docker slim
#                                    images + adapter pre-installed)
#   - checksums.txt                  (sha256 of every asset)
#   - ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest (multi-arch OCI image, amd64 + arm64)
#
# Versioning lives in the GitHub Release (binaries, installers, changelog).
# The Docker image carries exactly one tag, :latest; there is no per-version
# image tag. `docker pull ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest` resolves the right
# architecture automatically.
#
# All release assets are attached to the GitHub Release and linked from
# install.sh via https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/latest/download/...
#
# Manual trigger (workflow_dispatch) is allowed for rc builds — they publish
# to the Release draft; the Docker image is still only :latest.

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "release tag (e.g. v0.3.0) — required for workflow_dispatch"
        required: true
      force:
        description: "skip the verification gate (emergency / rc only)"
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: write   # create releases, upload assets
  packages: write   # push to ghcr.io
  actions: read     # gate job reads CI/e2e run status for the tagged commit

env:
  IMAGE_NAME: ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva

jobs:
  # ── 0. Gate — verify, don't re-test ──────────────────────────────────
  # The release pipeline does NOT run tests. All verification (shellcheck,
  # go vet/test/build, ui build, docker smoke, full e2e) already ran on the
  # PR and on the push to main. This job only CONFIRMS the tagged commit is
  # green — a status lookup, not a test run — so the release stays fast while
  # a tag can still never ship code whose tests failed. Every build job
  # `needs: gate`. `workflow_dispatch` with force=true skips it (rc/emergency).
  gate:
    name: gate (verify CI + e2e already passed)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - name: resolve commit SHA for the tag
        id: sha
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            TAG="${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}"
            SHA="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${TAG}" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [ -z "$SHA" ] && SHA="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/git/ref/tags/${TAG}" --jq .object.sha 2>/dev/null || true)"
          else
            SHA="${GITHUB_SHA}"
          fi
          [ -n "$SHA" ] || { echo "::error::could not resolve a commit SHA to gate on"; exit 1; }
          echo "sha=$SHA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "gating on commit $SHA"

      - name: require CI + e2e success on that commit
        if: ${{ github.event.inputs.force != 'true' }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SHA: ${{ steps.sha.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Confirm the tagged commit's verification is green — a status lookup,
          # not a test run. Poll until the workflow completes (handles tagging
          # right after the merge push), bounded so a stuck check can't hang the
          # release. `hard` = must exist and succeed; `soft` = must succeed IF it
          # ran (ci.yml is path-filtered, so a docs-only release commit may have
          # no CI run — e2e always runs on a main push and actually builds + runs
          # the server, so it's the hard gate).
          check() {
            local wf="$1" mode="$2" deadline=$((SECONDS + 1200))  # ~20 min cap
            while :; do
              read -r status conclusion < <(gh api \
                "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/${wf}/runs?head_sha=${SHA}&per_page=1" \
                --jq '.workflow_runs[0] | "\(.status) \(.conclusion)"' 2>/dev/null || echo "null null")
              if [ "$status" = "null" ]; then
                if [ "$mode" = "soft" ]; then echo "• $wf: no run for $SHA (path-filtered) — skipping"; return 0; fi
                echo "::error::no $wf run for $SHA — commit was not verified (use force=true to override)"; return 1
              fi
              if [ "$status" = "completed" ]; then
                [ "$conclusion" = "success" ] && { echo "✓ $wf succeeded for $SHA"; return 0; }
                echo "::error::$wf for $SHA concluded '$conclusion' — refusing to release an unverified commit"; return 1
              fi
              [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ] || { echo "::error::timed out waiting for $wf on $SHA"; return 1; }
              echo "… $wf is '$status' for $SHA — waiting"; sleep 20
            done
          }
          check e2e.yml hard
          check ci.yml  soft
          echo "gate passed: verification is green for $SHA"

  # ── 1. Go binary: matrix amd64 + arm64 ───────────────────────────────
  build-orva:
    name: build orva (${{ matrix.goarch }})
    needs: gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        goarch: [amd64, arm64]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: "1.26.x"
          # No build cache — every release builds from scratch so we
          # can't accidentally ship a stale toolchain artifact.
          cache: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          # No npm cache — fresh install on every run.
          cache: ""

      - name: build ui
        working-directory: frontend
        run: |
          npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run build

      - name: embed ui + adapters
        run: |
          rm -rf backend/internal/server/ui_dist
          cp -r frontend/dist backend/internal/server/ui_dist
          make adapters-embed

      - name: resolve build identity
        id: v
        run: |
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "commit=${GITHUB_SHA::7}"               >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "build_time=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: go build
        env:
          GOOS: linux
          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          go build \
            -trimpath \
            -ldflags="-s -w \
              -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Version=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }} \
              -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Commit=${{ steps.v.outputs.commit }} \
              -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.BuildTime=${{ steps.v.outputs.build_time }}" \
            -o dist/orva-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }} \
            ./backend/cmd/orva

      - name: upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: orva-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          path: dist/orva-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  # ── 1b. Standalone CLI binaries (Linux + macOS + Windows × amd64/arm64) ──
  # Slim CLI built from the dedicated ./cli/cmd/orva entry point — no
  # server packages, no embedded UI/adapters/docs/MCP. Cross-compiled
  # from a single ubuntu runner: pure Go, CGO disabled, fully static.
  # Windows builds get the .exe suffix.
  build-cli:
    name: build orva-cli (${{ matrix.goos }}/${{ matrix.goarch }})
    needs: gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - goos: linux
            goarch: amd64
          - goos: linux
            goarch: arm64
          - goos: darwin
            goarch: amd64
          - goos: darwin
            goarch: arm64
          - goos: windows
            goarch: amd64
            ext: ".exe"
          - goos: windows
            goarch: arm64
            ext: ".exe"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: "1.26.x"
          # No build cache — every release builds from scratch so we
          # can't accidentally ship a stale toolchain artifact.
          cache: false

      - name: resolve build identity
        id: v
        run: |
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "commit=${GITHUB_SHA::7}"               >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "build_time=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: go build (slim cli)
        env:
          GOOS: ${{ matrix.goos }}
          GOARCH: ${{ matrix.goarch }}
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          OUT="dist/orva-cli-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}${{ matrix.ext }}"
          # Slim CLI imports only cli/commands — main.Version is the right
          # ldflags target here (it forwards into commands.Version).
          go build \
            -trimpath \
            -ldflags="-s -w -X main.Version=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}" \
            -o "$OUT" \
            ./cli/cmd/orva
          file "$OUT" || true
          ls -lh "$OUT"

      - name: upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: orva-cli-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          path: dist/orva-cli-${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}${{ matrix.ext }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  # ── 2. nsjail: per-arch standalone binary (release asset only) ───────
  # The container image's nsjail comes from inside the unified Dockerfile
  # (its `FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS nsjail` stage), so this job is
  # solely for producing the standalone `nsjail-linux-{amd64,arm64}`
  # binary that ships as a GitHub release asset for bare-metal installs.
  #
  # Why container: debian:bookworm-slim
  # ───────────────────────────────────
  # nsjail is a C++ binary that dynamically links against libprotobuf,
  # libnl-route-3, libstdc++, libcap, libc. Built on the ubuntu-24.04
  # host runner (glibc 2.39 / libstdc++ 14 / GLIBCXX_3.4.32+), the
  # binary carries symbol references too new for the bookworm-class
  # runtime its install.sh seeds it into — at which point dynamic
  # linking aborts at exec with
  #   "libprotobuf.so.32: cannot open shared object file"
  # then, after that lib is added,
  #   "version `GLIBC_2.38' not found"
  # Building inside debian:bookworm-slim matches the binary's symbol
  # references to the install target on every supported kernel
  # (Linux ≥ 3.2, which covers every system anyone deploys this on).
  build-nsjail:
    name: build nsjail (${{ matrix.goarch }})
    needs: gate
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    container: debian:bookworm-slim
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - goarch: amd64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
          - goarch: arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      # No actions/checkout: the job clones nsjail upstream and produces
      # one binary; no Orva repo files are read here.

      - name: install build deps
        run: |
          apt-get update
          apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            ca-certificates git make gcc g++ autoconf bison flex libtool pkg-config \
            libprotobuf-dev libnl-route-3-dev protobuf-compiler

      - name: build nsjail from source
        run: |
          git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/google/nsjail.git /tmp/nsjail
          cd /tmp/nsjail
          make -j"$(nproc)"
          strip nsjail
          file ./nsjail
          # Confirm the binary's NEEDED dyn deps match what the runtime
          # apt list installs (libprotobuf32, libnl-route-3-200,
          # libcap2-bin, libstdc++6, libc6). If a future libprotobuf
          # bookworm bump renames the .so version, this readlink + dump
          # output will surface in the workflow log immediately.
          objdump -p ./nsjail | grep NEEDED || true
          cp ./nsjail nsjail-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }}

      - name: upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: nsjail-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          path: /tmp/nsjail/nsjail-linux-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  # ── 3. Language rootfs tarballs ───────────────────────────────────────
  build-rootfs:
    name: rootfs ${{ matrix.runtime }} (${{ matrix.goarch }})
    needs: gate
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        runtime: [node, python]
        goarch: [amd64, arm64]
        include:
          - goarch: amd64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
          - goarch: arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: install zstd
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends zstd

      - name: extract rootfs via docker export
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bash scripts/build-rootfs.sh "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs" "${{ matrix.runtime }}"

          # Pre-install the adapter so install.sh doesn't need the source tree.
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs/opt/orva"
          if [ -f "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.js" ]; then
            cp "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.js" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs/opt/orva/adapter.js"
          fi
          if [ -f "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.py" ]; then
            cp "backend/runtimes/${{ matrix.runtime }}/adapter.py" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs/opt/orva/adapter.py"
          fi

      - name: tar + zstd compress
        run: |
          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs"
          tar -cf - . | zstd -19 -T0 -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}.tar.zst"
          ls -lh "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}.tar.zst"

      - name: upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          path: rootfs-${{ matrix.runtime }}-${{ matrix.goarch }}.tar.zst
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  # ── 4. Collate + compute checksums + publish GitHub Release ───────────
  release:
    name: publish github release
    needs: [build-orva, build-cli, build-nsjail, build-rootfs]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: resolve version
        id: v
        run: |
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: download all artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: artifacts

      - name: flatten + chmod
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          find artifacts -type f -exec cp -v {} dist/ \;
          # Mark every Unix-style binary executable. Windows .exe doesn't
          # need a chmod but the no-op is harmless.
          chmod +x dist/orva-linux-* dist/nsjail-linux-* 2>/dev/null || true
          for f in dist/orva-cli-*; do
            case "$f" in *.exe) ;; *) chmod +x "$f" 2>/dev/null || true ;; esac
          done
          ls -lh dist/

      - name: sha256 checksums
        working-directory: dist
        run: |
          sha256sum * | tee checksums.txt

      - name: create / update github release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
          name: Orva ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
          draft: false
          prerelease: ${{ contains(steps.v.outputs.tag, '-rc') || contains(steps.v.outputs.tag, '-beta') }}
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          files: |
            dist/*
          body: |
            ## Orva ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}

            ### Install

            **Docker:**
            ```
            docker run -p 8443:8443 --cap-add SYS_ADMIN \
              --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
              -v orva-data:/var/lib/orva \
              ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest
            ```

            **Bare Linux server (POSIX installer works on Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/Alpine/Arch/openSUSE):**
            ```
            curl -fsSL https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/download/${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}/install.sh | sh
            ```

            **Standalone CLI (Linux + macOS):**
            ```
            curl -fsSL https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/download/${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}/install-cli.sh | sh
            ```

            **Standalone CLI (Windows, PowerShell):**
            ```
            irm https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/releases/download/${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}/install-cli.ps1 | iex
            ```

            ### Release assets

            | asset | description |
            |---|---|
            | `orva-linux-amd64`, `orva-linux-arm64` | Daemon + CLI binary (server install via `install.sh`) |
            | `orva-cli-linux-{amd64,arm64}` | Slim CLI (Linux) — used by `install-cli.sh` |
            | `orva-cli-darwin-{amd64,arm64}` | Slim CLI (macOS Intel + Apple Silicon) |
            | `orva-cli-windows-{amd64,arm64}.exe` | Slim CLI (Windows) — used by `install-cli.ps1` |
            | `nsjail-linux-{amd64,arm64}` | Pre-built nsjail (downloaded by install.sh) |
            | `rootfs-{node,python}-{amd64,arm64}.tar.zst` | Language rootfs |
            | `install.sh`, `install-cli.sh`, `install-cli.ps1` | One-line installers |
            | `checksums.txt` | sha256 of every asset above |

      # Upload installer scripts alongside the release so versioned URLs work.
      - name: attach installer scripts
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
          files: |
            scripts/install.sh
            scripts/install-cli.sh
            scripts/install-cli.ps1

  # ── 5. Per-arch Docker image, native runners (no QEMU) ────────────────
  # Single source of truth: the unified Dockerfile builds UI, Go binary,
  # nsjail, and rootfs stages itself, all in matched debian:bookworm-slim
  # environments. No artifact staging from sibling jobs; no second
  # Dockerfile to drift. Each arch builds on its native runner so QEMU
  # emulation stays out of the loop (UI + npm install was the original
  # reason for splitting builds; native runners removed that pressure).
  #
  # Each arch pushes by digest only; the manifest job below stitches the
  # two digests into both `:latest` and the immutable `:${tag}`.
  docker-image:
    name: docker image (${{ matrix.goarch }})
    needs: gate
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - goarch: amd64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
            platform: linux/amd64
          - goarch: arm64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            platform: linux/arm64
    outputs:
      digest_amd64: ${{ steps.digest_out.outputs.amd64 }}
      digest_arm64: ${{ steps.digest_out.outputs.arm64 }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: resolve build identity
        id: v
        run: |
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "commit=${GITHUB_SHA::7}"               >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "build_time=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: login to ghcr.io
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Push by digest only — no tag is created. The manifest job below
      # references the per-arch digests directly when stitching them
      # into the multi-arch :latest + :${tag} tags.
      - name: build + push by digest
        id: build
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
          # No layer cache — `no-cache: true` forces every layer to
          # rebuild, and `pull: true` re-pulls every base image. The
          # release pipeline must produce bit-identical-from-scratch
          # output every time; cached layers can mask supply-chain
          # surprises (a base image gets repinned but our cache still
          # has the old one).
          no-cache: true
          pull: true
          labels: |
            org.opencontainers.image.title=Orva
            org.opencontainers.image.source=https://github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva
            org.opencontainers.image.licenses=Apache-2.0
            org.opencontainers.image.version=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
            org.opencontainers.image.revision=${{ steps.v.outputs.commit }}
            org.opencontainers.image.created=${{ steps.v.outputs.build_time }}
          build-args: |
            VERSION=${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
            COMMIT=${{ steps.v.outputs.commit }}
            BUILD_TIME=${{ steps.v.outputs.build_time }}
          outputs: type=image,name=${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }},push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true

      - name: export digest for manifest job
        id: digest_out
        run: |
          digest="${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}"
          echo "${{ matrix.goarch }}=${digest}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "digest_${{ matrix.goarch }}=${digest}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "::notice::pushed ${{ matrix.goarch }} → ${digest}"

      - name: write digest to artifact
        run: |
          mkdir -p /tmp/digests
          digest="${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}"
          touch "/tmp/digests/${digest#sha256:}"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: digest-${{ matrix.goarch }}
          path: /tmp/digests/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  # ── 6. Stitch the two per-arch digests into multi-arch manifest ──────
  # The Docker image carries exactly ONE tag: `:latest`. It is a multi-arch
  # manifest (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64); `docker pull` resolves the right
  # arch automatically. Versioning lives in the GitHub Release (binaries,
  # installers, changelog), NOT in image tags — we intentionally do not push
  # a per-version `:vYYYY.MM.DD` image tag.
  docker-manifest:
    name: docker multi-arch manifest
    needs: [docker-image]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: resolve version
        id: v
        run: |
          if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            echo "tag=${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "tag=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: digest-*
          path: /tmp/digests
          merge-multiple: true

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: login to ghcr.io
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: create + push multi-arch manifest (:latest only)
        run: |
          cd /tmp/digests
          DIGESTS=$(printf '${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}@sha256:%s ' *)
          docker buildx imagetools create \
            -t ${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest \
            $DIGESTS

      - name: inspect
        run: |
          docker buildx imagetools inspect ${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest

  # ── 7. Prune old GHCR versions ───────────────────────────────────────
  # The Docker image carries exactly one tag, `:latest`. Everything in the
  # registry that isn't the current `:latest` manifest (or one of its
  # per-arch sub-images) is garbage: stale per-version tags from older
  # workflow versions, orphaned digests from previous `:latest` pushes.
  # This job deletes all of it, leaving only the live `:latest` tree.
  #
  # Runs after docker-manifest so the new :latest is pinned before we
  # start deleting things.
  cleanup-ghcr:
    name: prune old ghcr versions
    needs: [docker-manifest]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: prune everything that isn't the current release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAG: ${{ needs.docker-manifest.outputs.tag }}
          # Package is user-owned (Harsh-2002), not org-owned. If the
          # repo moves to an org later, change /users/ → /orgs/ and the
          # delete URL similarly.
          PKG_OWNER: Harsh-2002
          PKG_NAME: orva
        run: |
          set -eu

          # Resolve the digests that make up the current :latest manifest.
          # docker buildx imagetools inspect emits the multi-arch manifest
          # with each platform's digest; we keep those + the manifest's
          # own digest. Everything else is fair game.
          docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/${PKG_OWNER}/${PKG_NAME}:latest" --raw \
            | jq -r '..|.digest? // empty' \
            | sort -u > /tmp/keep_digests.txt
          echo "Digests to keep (current :latest manifest + sub-images):"
          cat /tmp/keep_digests.txt

          # List all versions in the package, filter to those that are
          # NOT in the keep-list AND don't carry the current tag or
          # 'latest'. Delete each one.
          gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
            "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions?per_page=100" \
            --paginate \
            --jq '.[] | "\(.id)|\(.name)|\((.metadata.container.tags // []) | join(","))"' \
            > /tmp/versions.txt

          echo "Inspecting $(wc -l </tmp/versions.txt) total package versions:"

          while IFS='|' read -r id sha tags; do
            keep_reason=""
            # 1. Keep only the 'latest' tag. Any other tag (e.g. a stale
            #    per-version vYYYY.MM.DD from an older workflow) is deleted.
            if echo ",$tags," | grep -q ",latest,"; then
              keep_reason="tag=$tags"
            # 2. Keep if version's sha256 is in the current manifest tree
            #    (per-arch sub-manifests pulled in via the multi-arch index).
            elif grep -qx "$sha" /tmp/keep_digests.txt; then
              keep_reason="part of current :latest manifest"
            # 3. Keep all untagged versions. A multi-arch manifest references
            #    its per-architecture sub-images by digest only — they appear
            #    untagged in the GHCR versions API. Deleting them breaks
            #    `docker pull` on the parent manifest. The keep_digests
            #    extraction above is best-effort and may miss some sub-image
            #    digests (e.g. attestation manifests); this branch is the
            #    safety net. Small storage cost; large reliability win.
            elif [ -z "$tags" ]; then
              keep_reason="untagged (likely a sub-image manifest)"
            fi

            if [ -n "$keep_reason" ]; then
              echo "  keep   id=$id tags=$tags ($keep_reason)"
              continue
            fi

            echo "  delete id=$id tags=$tags"
            gh api -X DELETE \
              -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
              "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions/${id}" \
              || echo "::warning::failed to delete version $id (continuing)"
          done < /tmp/versions.txt

          echo "::notice::GHCR cleanup complete — only :latest + its sub-images + untagged versions remain."

    12	on:

    14	  # they must not run on main-push: during a release cut the old release is
    15	  # already gone and the new one isn't published yet, so "latest" 404s. On
    16	  # release:published they validate the freshly-published artifacts.
    17	  release:

════════════════════════ .github/workflows/cleanup-ghcr.yml ════════════════════════
     1	name: cleanup-ghcr
     2	
     3	# Manual one-shot prune of accumulated old versions in
     4	# ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva. The release workflow's cleanup-ghcr job
     5	# already does this automatically on every tag push — this standalone
     6	# workflow exists so an operator can prune NOW without re-running the
     7	# full ~15-min release pipeline (when, for example, prior releases
     8	# left orphan versions behind before the cleanup job existed).
     9	#
    10	# Trigger from the Actions tab → "cleanup-ghcr" → "Run workflow".
    11	# Optional `tag` input picks which release's manifest to preserve;
    12	# defaults to whatever ghcr's :latest currently points at.
    13	
    14	on:
    15	  workflow_dispatch:
    16	    inputs:
    17	      tag:
    18	        description: "release tag to preserve (default: whatever :latest resolves to)"
    19	        required: false
    20	        default: ""
    21	
    22	permissions:
    23	  packages: write
    24	
    25	jobs:
    26	  prune:
    27	    name: prune old ghcr versions
    28	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    29	    steps:
    30	      - name: resolve target tag
    31	        id: tag
    32	        env:
    33	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    34	          INPUT_TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}
    35	        run: |
    36	          if [ -n "$INPUT_TAG" ]; then
    37	            echo "tag=$INPUT_TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    38	            exit 0
    39	          fi
    40	          # Resolve :latest → digest → find the tag that shares that digest.
    41	          latest_digest=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest --raw \
    42	            | sha256sum | awk '{print "sha256:"$1}')
    43	          # The :latest manifest itself is a multi-arch manifest list. Find
    44	          # which version row in the API has 'latest' in its tags — that
    45	          # row's adjacent tag (vYYYY.MM.DD) is what we preserve.
    46	          tag=$(gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
    47	            "/users/Harsh-2002/packages/container/orva/versions?per_page=100" \
    48	            --paginate \
    49	            --jq '.[] | select(.metadata.container.tags // [] | index("latest")) | .metadata.container.tags[] | select(. != "latest")' \
    50	            | head -n1)
    51	          if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
    52	            echo "::error::could not resolve a non-latest tag from the current :latest manifest"
    53	            exit 1
    54	          fi
    55	          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    56	          echo "::notice::resolved current release tag: $tag"
    57	
    58	      - name: prune everything that isn't $TAG
    59	        env:
    60	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    61	          TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}
    62	          PKG_OWNER: Harsh-2002
    63	          PKG_NAME: orva
    64	        run: |
    65	          set -eu
    66	
    67	          # Same logic as release.yml's cleanup-ghcr job. Resolve the
    68	          # digest tree of the current manifest, then delete anything
    69	          # not in that tree and not tagged with $TAG or 'latest'.
    70	          docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/${PKG_OWNER}/${PKG_NAME}:${TAG}" --raw \
    71	            | jq -r '..|.digest? // empty' \
    72	            | sort -u > /tmp/keep_digests.txt
    73	          echo "Digests to keep:"
    74	          cat /tmp/keep_digests.txt
    75	
    76	          gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
    77	            "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions?per_page=100" \
    78	            --paginate \
    79	            --jq '.[] | "\(.id)|\(.name)|\((.metadata.container.tags // []) | join(","))"' \
    80	            > /tmp/versions.txt
    81	
    82	          total=$(wc -l </tmp/versions.txt)
    83	          deleted=0
    84	          kept=0
    85	          echo "Inspecting $total total package versions:"
    86	
    87	          while IFS='|' read -r id sha tags; do
    88	            keep_reason=""
    89	            # 1. Keep if version carries the current tag or 'latest'.
    90	            if echo ",$tags," | grep -qE ",($TAG|latest),"; then
    91	              keep_reason="tag=$tags"
    92	            # 2. Keep if version's sha is referenced by the current manifest tree.
    93	            elif grep -qx "$sha" /tmp/keep_digests.txt; then
    94	              keep_reason="part of current $TAG manifest"
    95	            # 3. Keep all untagged versions. Multi-arch manifests reference
    96	            #    their per-arch sub-images by digest only — those show up as
    97	            #    untagged in the GHCR versions API. Deleting them breaks
    98	            #    `docker pull` on the parent manifest. The keep_digests
    99	            #    extraction is best-effort; this branch is the safety net.
   100	            elif [ -z "$tags" ]; then
   101	              keep_reason="untagged (likely a sub-image manifest)"
   102	            fi
   103	
   104	            if [ -n "$keep_reason" ]; then
   105	              echo "  keep   id=$id tags=$tags ($keep_reason)"
   106	              kept=$((kept+1))
   107	              continue
   108	            fi
   109	
   110	            echo "  delete id=$id tags=$tags"
   111	            if gh api -X DELETE \
   112	                -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
   113	                "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions/${id}" 2>/tmp/delete-err; then
   114	              deleted=$((deleted+1))
   115	            else
   116	              echo "::warning::failed to delete version $id: $(cat /tmp/delete-err)"
   117	            fi
   118	          done < /tmp/versions.txt
   119	
   120	          echo "::notice::cleanup-ghcr done — kept=$kept, deleted=$deleted, of $total total."
   121	          {
   122	            echo "## cleanup-ghcr summary"
   123	            echo ""
   124	            echo "- preserved tag: \`$TAG\` (+ \`latest\` + sub-images)"
   125	            echo "- kept: $kept versions"
   126	            echo "- deleted: $deleted versions"
   127	            echo "- total inspected: $total"
   128	          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

     1	name: install-e2e
     2	
     3	# Real install + smoke + uninstall across 6 distros, in privileged
     4	# systemd-in-docker containers. The cheap stuff (shellcheck on the
     5	# install scripts themselves) lives in ci.yml — this workflow assumes
     6	# the scripts pass lint and focuses on actually running them.
     7	
     8	# Least-privilege default token (these jobs only read the repo).
     9	permissions:
    10	  contents: read
    11	
    12	on:
    13	  # Runs AFTER a release publishes — these download the released binary, so
    14	  # they must not run on main-push: during a release cut the old release is
    15	  # already gone and the new one isn't published yet, so "latest" 404s. On
    16	  # release:published they validate the freshly-published artifacts.
    17	  release:
    18	    types: [published]
    19	  pull_request:
    20	    paths:
    21	      - "scripts/install.sh"
    22	      - "scripts/uninstall.sh"
    23	      - "test/install/**"
    24	      - ".github/workflows/install-e2e.yml"
    25	  workflow_dispatch: {}
    26	  schedule:
    27	    # Weekly Sunday 03:00 UTC catches rolling-release breakage (Arch).
    28	    - cron: "0 3 * * 0"
    29	
    30	jobs:
    31	  matrix:
    32	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    33	    # Two distros are advisory rather than gating:
    34	    #   arch   — rolling release; pacman mirrors drift between runs and
    35	    #            occasionally serve stale signatures or 404 individual
    36	    #            versions, so a transient mirror flake shouldn't block.
    37	    #   alpine — musl + glibc-built nsjail works via gcompat for the
    38	    #            install + smoke flow, but openrc's reinstall edge case
    39	    #            (uninstall then immediate reinstall + service start)
    40	    #            occasionally races on the GH runner. Smoke flow proves
    41	    #            the core install works; the reinstall round-trip is a
    42	    #            nice-to-have we'll harden later.
    43	    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.distro == 'arch' || matrix.distro == 'alpine321' }}
    44	    strategy:
    45	      fail-fast: false
    46	      matrix:
    47	        distro:
    48	          - ubuntu24
    49	          - debian12
    50	          - alpine321
    51	          - rocky9
    52	          - fedora41
    53	          - arch

    55	      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

    57	      - name: Install jq + curl
    58	        run: |
    59	          sudo apt-get update -qq
    60	          sudo apt-get install -y jq curl

    62	      - name: Run install + smoke + uninstall for ${{ matrix.distro }}
    63	        # ORVA_BROWSER_LEG=0 skips agent-browser in CI (no display).
    64	        # HTTP route spot-checks still run.
    65	        env:
    66	          ORVA_BROWSER_LEG: "0"

     1	name: cleanup-ghcr
     2	
     3	# Manual one-shot prune of accumulated old versions in
     4	# ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva. The release workflow's cleanup-ghcr job
     5	# already does this automatically on every tag push — this standalone
     6	# workflow exists so an operator can prune NOW without re-running the
     7	# full ~15-min release pipeline (when, for example, prior releases
     8	# left orphan versions behind before the cleanup job existed).
     9	#
    10	# Trigger from the Actions tab → "cleanup-ghcr" → "Run workflow".
    11	# Optional `tag` input picks which release's manifest to preserve;
    12	# defaults to whatever ghcr's :latest currently points at.
    13	
    14	on:
    15	  workflow_dispatch:
    16	    inputs:
    17	      tag:
    18	        description: "release tag to preserve (default: whatever :latest resolves to)"
    19	        required: false
    20	        default: ""
    21	
    22	permissions:
    23	  packages: write
    24	
    25	jobs:
    26	  prune:
    27	    name: prune old ghcr versions
    28	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    29	    steps:
    30	      - name: resolve target tag
    31	        id: tag
    32	        env:
    33	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    34	          INPUT_TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag }}
    35	        run: |
    36	          if [ -n "$INPUT_TAG" ]; then
    37	            echo "tag=$INPUT_TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    38	            exit 0
    39	          fi
    40	          # Resolve :latest → digest → find the tag that shares that digest.
    41	          latest_digest=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/harsh-2002/orva:latest --raw \
    42	            | sha256sum | awk '{print "sha256:"$1}')
    43	          # The :latest manifest itself is a multi-arch manifest list. Find
    44	          # which version row in the API has 'latest' in its tags — that
    45	          # row's adjacent tag (vYYYY.MM.DD) is what we preserve.
    46	          tag=$(gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
    47	            "/users/Harsh-2002/packages/container/orva/versions?per_page=100" \
    48	            --paginate \
    49	            --jq '.[] | select(.metadata.container.tags // [] | index("latest")) | .metadata.container.tags[] | select(. != "latest")' \
    50	            | head -n1)
    51	          if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
    52	            echo "::error::could not resolve a non-latest tag from the current :latest manifest"
    53	            exit 1
    54	          fi
    55	          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    56	          echo "::notice::resolved current release tag: $tag"
    57	
    58	      - name: prune everything that isn't $TAG
    59	        env:
    60	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    61	          TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}
    62	          PKG_OWNER: Harsh-2002
    63	          PKG_NAME: orva
    64	        run: |
    65	          set -eu
    66	
    67	          # Same logic as release.yml's cleanup-ghcr job. Resolve the
    68	          # digest tree of the current manifest, then delete anything
    69	          # not in that tree and not tagged with $TAG or 'latest'.
    70	          docker buildx imagetools inspect "ghcr.io/${PKG_OWNER}/${PKG_NAME}:${TAG}" --raw \
    71	            | jq -r '..|.digest? // empty' \
    72	            | sort -u > /tmp/keep_digests.txt
    73	          echo "Digests to keep:"
    74	          cat /tmp/keep_digests.txt
    75	
    76	          gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
    77	            "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions?per_page=100" \
    78	            --paginate \
    79	            --jq '.[] | "\(.id)|\(.name)|\((.metadata.container.tags // []) | join(","))"' \
    80	            > /tmp/versions.txt
    81	
    82	          total=$(wc -l </tmp/versions.txt)
    83	          deleted=0
    84	          kept=0
    85	          echo "Inspecting $total total package versions:"
    86	
    87	          while IFS='|' read -r id sha tags; do
    88	            keep_reason=""
    89	            # 1. Keep if version carries the current tag or 'latest'.
    90	            if echo ",$tags," | grep -qE ",($TAG|latest),"; then
    91	              keep_reason="tag=$tags"
    92	            # 2. Keep if version's sha is referenced by the current manifest tree.
    93	            elif grep -qx "$sha" /tmp/keep_digests.txt; then
    94	              keep_reason="part of current $TAG manifest"
    95	            # 3. Keep all untagged versions. Multi-arch manifests reference
    96	            #    their per-arch sub-images by digest only — those show up as
    97	            #    untagged in the GHCR versions API. Deleting them breaks
    98	            #    `docker pull` on the parent manifest. The keep_digests
    99	            #    extraction is best-effort; this branch is the safety net.
   100	            elif [ -z "$tags" ]; then
   101	              keep_reason="untagged (likely a sub-image manifest)"
   102	            fi
   103	
   104	            if [ -n "$keep_reason" ]; then
   105	              echo "  keep   id=$id tags=$tags ($keep_reason)"
   106	              kept=$((kept+1))
   107	              continue
   108	            fi
   109	
   110	            echo "  delete id=$id tags=$tags"
   111	            if gh api -X DELETE \
   112	                -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
   113	                "/users/${PKG_OWNER}/packages/container/${PKG_NAME}/versions/${id}" 2>/tmp/delete-err; then
   114	              deleted=$((deleted+1))
   115	            else
   116	              echo "::warning::failed to delete version $id: $(cat /tmp/delete-err)"
   117	            fi
   118	          done < /tmp/versions.txt
   119	
   120	          echo "::notice::cleanup-ghcr done — kept=$kept, deleted=$deleted, of $total total."
   121	          {
   122	            echo "## cleanup-ghcr summary"
   123	            echo ""
   124	            echo "- preserved tag: \`$TAG\` (+ \`latest\` + sub-images)"
   125	            echo "- kept: $kept versions"
   126	            echo "- deleted: $deleted versions"
   127	            echo "- total inspected: $total"
   128	          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

1	# Build identity — stamped into the binary via -X ldflags and surfaced
2	# at /api/v1/system/health + Settings → Build info in the dashboard. The
3	# three values flow Makefile → Dockerfile → release.yml so a single
4	# source of truth feeds bare-metal, Docker, and CI builds alike.
5	#
6	# VERSION:    git tag when tagged, otherwise `git describe` (e.g.
7	#             "v2026.05.15-3-g1be3399-dirty"). Default "dev" if no git.
8	# COMMIT:     short SHA of the build's HEAD commit.
9	# BUILD_TIME: wall-clock at build moment (RFC3339 UTC) — useful for
10	#             telling "is this image the one CI just produced?".
11	VERSION    ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
12	COMMIT     ?= $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
13	BUILD_TIME ?= $(shell date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
14	BINARY      = orva
15	BUILD       = build
16	
17	# The version package lives at backend/internal/version. Go's ldflags
18	# fail silently when the target path is wrong — keep these three lines
19	# the only place this string appears so renames stay in sync.
20	LDFLAGS = -s -w \
21	  -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Version=$(VERSION) \
22	  -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Commit=$(COMMIT) \
23	  -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.BuildTime=$(BUILD_TIME)
24	
25	.PHONY: build test lint clean ui embed build-all dev adapters-embed docs-embed cli cli-all
26	
27	# Sync the canonical docs reference markdown into both consumers:
28	# - backend/internal/mcp/reference.md → embedded by the get_orva_docs MCP
29	#   tool via //go:embed
30	# - frontend/public/docs.md → served by Vite at /docs.md so the Docs page's
31	#   "Copy as Markdown" button reads the same bytes
32	# - cli/commands/reference.md → embedded by the `orva docs` command via
33	#   //go:embed so the slim CLI renders the same reference offline
34	# Single source of truth lives at docs/reference.md. Edit it, run
35	# `make docs-embed`, and UI + MCP + CLI serve the new content.
36	docs-embed:
37		@cp docs/reference.md backend/internal/mcp/reference.md
38		@cp docs/reference.md frontend/public/docs.md
39		@cp docs/reference.md cli/commands/reference.md
40	
41	# Copy adapter sources + bundled SDK into backend/cmd/orva/adapters/ so
42	# //go:embed has them at build time. Keeps backend/runtimes/ as the
43	# source-of-truth directory (shared with Dockerfile COPY paths).
44	# Also copies the v0.2 orva SDK module (kv / invoke / jobs).
45	adapters-embed:
46		@rm -rf backend/cmd/orva/adapters
47		@mkdir -p backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python
48		@cp backend/runtimes/node/adapter.js     backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/adapter.js
49		@cp backend/runtimes/python/adapter.py   backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python/adapter.py
50		@cp backend/runtimes/node/orva.js        backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/orva.js
51		@cp backend/runtimes/python/orva.py      backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python/orva.py
52		@# v0.6 SDK: ship .d.ts + package.json so TS handlers get types;
53		@# py.typed marks the Python module as fully typed for static checkers.
54		@cp backend/runtimes/node/orva.d.ts      backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/orva.d.ts
55		@cp backend/runtimes/node/package.json   backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/package.json
56		@cp backend/runtimes/python/py.typed     backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python/py.typed

58	build: adapters-embed docs-embed
59		@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
60		go build -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" -o $(BUILD)/$(BINARY) ./backend/cmd/orva

65	lint:
66		go vet ./...

81	# Standalone CLI binary. Same Go program as the daemon (orva and orva-cli
82	# share `./cmd/orva`), but built without the embedded UI/rootfs assumptions
83	# and named distinctly so release artifacts don't collide with the server.
84	# CGO disabled + -trimpath + stripped symbols → fully static, ships anywhere.
85	# Slim standalone CLI. Built from the dedicated ./cli/cmd/orva entry point
86	# which imports only the cli/commands library — no server packages, no
87	# embedded UI/adapters/docs/MCP. Targets ~6–9 MB vs the ~20 MB server.
88	# CGO disabled + -trimpath + stripped symbols → fully static.
89	cli:
90		@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
91		CGO_ENABLED=0 go build \
92		  -trimpath \
93		  -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" \
94		  -o $(BUILD)/orva ./cli/cmd/orva
