96	# Cross-compile the slim CLI for every release-asset target.
97	# Output naming matches the GitHub release-asset convention so install-cli.sh
98	# (and the README curl recipe) can point straight at /releases/latest/download/.
99	# Windows targets get the .exe suffix.
100	cli-all:
101		@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
102		@for target in linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64; do \
103		  os=$${target%/*}; arch=$${target#*/}; \
104		  ext=""; [ "$$os" = "windows" ] && ext=".exe"; \
105		  echo ">> building orva-cli-$$os-$$arch$$ext"; \

# Build identity — stamped into the binary via -X ldflags and surfaced
# at /api/v1/system/health + Settings → Build info in the dashboard. The
# three values flow Makefile → Dockerfile → release.yml so a single
# source of truth feeds bare-metal, Docker, and CI builds alike.
#
# VERSION:    git tag when tagged, otherwise `git describe` (e.g.
#             "v2026.05.15-3-g1be3399-dirty"). Default "dev" if no git.
# COMMIT:     short SHA of the build's HEAD commit.
# BUILD_TIME: wall-clock at build moment (RFC3339 UTC) — useful for
#             telling "is this image the one CI just produced?".
VERSION    ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
COMMIT     ?= $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
BUILD_TIME ?= $(shell date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
BINARY      = orva
BUILD       = build

# The version package lives at backend/internal/version. Go's ldflags
# fail silently when the target path is wrong — keep these three lines
# the only place this string appears so renames stay in sync.
LDFLAGS = -s -w \
  -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Version=$(VERSION) \
  -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.Commit=$(COMMIT) \
  -X github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/version.BuildTime=$(BUILD_TIME)

.PHONY: build test lint clean ui embed build-all dev adapters-embed docs-embed cli cli-all

# Sync the canonical docs reference markdown into both consumers:
# - backend/internal/mcp/reference.md → embedded by the get_orva_docs MCP
#   tool via //go:embed
# - frontend/public/docs.md → served by Vite at /docs.md so the Docs page's
#   "Copy as Markdown" button reads the same bytes
# - cli/commands/reference.md → embedded by the `orva docs` command via
#   //go:embed so the slim CLI renders the same reference offline
# Single source of truth lives at docs/reference.md. Edit it, run
# `make docs-embed`, and UI + MCP + CLI serve the new content.
docs-embed:
	@cp docs/reference.md backend/internal/mcp/reference.md
	@cp docs/reference.md frontend/public/docs.md
	@cp docs/reference.md cli/commands/reference.md

# Copy adapter sources + bundled SDK into backend/cmd/orva/adapters/ so
# //go:embed has them at build time. Keeps backend/runtimes/ as the
# source-of-truth directory (shared with Dockerfile COPY paths).
# Also copies the v0.2 orva SDK module (kv / invoke / jobs).
adapters-embed:
	@rm -rf backend/cmd/orva/adapters
	@mkdir -p backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python
	@cp backend/runtimes/node/adapter.js     backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/adapter.js
	@cp backend/runtimes/python/adapter.py   backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python/adapter.py
	@cp backend/runtimes/node/orva.js        backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/orva.js
	@cp backend/runtimes/python/orva.py      backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python/orva.py
	@# v0.6 SDK: ship .d.ts + package.json so TS handlers get types;
	@# py.typed marks the Python module as fully typed for static checkers.
	@cp backend/runtimes/node/orva.d.ts      backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/orva.d.ts
	@cp backend/runtimes/node/package.json   backend/cmd/orva/adapters/node/package.json
	@cp backend/runtimes/python/py.typed     backend/cmd/orva/adapters/python/py.typed

build: adapters-embed docs-embed
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	go build -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" -o $(BUILD)/$(BINARY) ./backend/cmd/orva

test:
	go test -count=1 ./...

lint:
	go vet ./...

ui: docs-embed
	cd frontend && npm install && npm run build

embed: ui
	rm -rf backend/internal/server/ui_dist
	cp -r frontend/dist backend/internal/server/ui_dist

build-all: embed build

dev:
	cd frontend && npm run dev &
	go run ./backend/cmd/orva serve

# Standalone CLI binary. Same Go program as the daemon (orva and orva-cli
# share `./cmd/orva`), but built without the embedded UI/rootfs assumptions
# and named distinctly so release artifacts don't collide with the server.
# CGO disabled + -trimpath + stripped symbols → fully static, ships anywhere.
# Slim standalone CLI. Built from the dedicated ./cli/cmd/orva entry point
# which imports only the cli/commands library — no server packages, no
# embedded UI/adapters/docs/MCP. Targets ~6–9 MB vs the ~20 MB server.
# CGO disabled + -trimpath + stripped symbols → fully static.
cli:
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	CGO_ENABLED=0 go build \
	  -trimpath \
	  -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" \
	  -o $(BUILD)/orva ./cli/cmd/orva

# Cross-compile the slim CLI for every release-asset target.
# Output naming matches the GitHub release-asset convention so install-cli.sh
# (and the README curl recipe) can point straight at /releases/latest/download/.
# Windows targets get the .exe suffix.
cli-all:
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD)
	@for target in linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64; do \
	  os=$${target%/*}; arch=$${target#*/}; \
	  ext=""; [ "$$os" = "windows" ] && ext=".exe"; \
	  echo ">> building orva-cli-$$os-$$arch$$ext"; \
	  CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$$os GOARCH=$$arch go build \
	    -trimpath \
	    -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" \
	    -o $(BUILD)/orva-cli-$$os-$$arch$$ext ./cli/cmd/orva || exit 1; \
	done

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)
	rm -rf backend/internal/server/ui_dist
	rm -rf frontend/dist

content.content:
1	# Backend
2	
3	Go 1.26 (bumped from 1.25 — the embedded Bifrost AI gateway requires go ≥1.26; the Dockerfile + all CI workflows pin golang 1.26 in lock-step). Module: `github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva` (rooted at the repo, not at
4	`backend/`). SQLite with no CGO (`modernc.org/sqlite`).
5	
6	The server binary built from `backend/cmd/orva` is the daemon (`orva serve`)
7	plus all CLI subcommands. The CLI subcommands live at `cli/commands/`
8	(package `commands`) — `backend/cmd/orva/main.go` imports
9	`cli/commands` and calls `commands.NewRoot()` then bolts on its own
10	`serve` / `setup` / `init` constructors. Single source of truth for
11	every client subcommand; the slim standalone CLI at `cli/cmd/orva`
12	uses the same library.
13	
14	## Build & Test
15	
16	```bash
17	# From repo root:
18	make build          # → build/orva (server + CLI bundled)
19	make test           # go test ./...
20	make lint           # go vet ./...
21	
22	# Direct invocations (also from repo root, since go.mod is here):
23	go build ./backend/cmd/orva
24	go test ./...
25	go vet ./...
26	```
27	
28	## Package Layout (`internal/`)
29	
30	| Package | Purpose |
31	|---|---|
32	| `config` | Config struct; env var + YAML loading |
33	| `database` | SQLite schema, migrations, all CRUD helpers |
34	| `registry` | In-memory function registry wrapping DB |
35	| `builder` | Deploy pipeline: tarball → `npm install` / `pip install` → optional `tsc` → register |
36	| `pool` | Warm-sandbox pool manager (`pool.Manager`) per function |
37	| `sandbox` | nsjail process lifecycle; `Worker` type with `Dispatch`/`DispatchEx` |
38	| `proxy` | HTTP → sandbox bridge; request capture (A3); streaming write-loop (C1) |
39	| `metrics` | Prometheus-text counters + histograms (no external deps, atomic ops) |
40	| `secrets` | AES-256-GCM encrypted secrets per function |
41	| `scheduler` | Cron runner (`robfig/cron/v3`) |
42	| `mcp` | MCP server (go-sdk); 70 operator-management tools OR channel-mode (one tool per bundled function, invoke-only). Auth accepts API keys, OAuth 2.1 access tokens, OR channel tokens. |
43	| `oauth` | OAuth 2.1 authorization server (RFC 7591 DCR + RFC 8414 metadata + PKCE S256 + RFC 8707 resource indicators + RFC 7009 revocation). Lets claude.ai/ChatGPT add `/mcp` as a custom connector via the browser. Connected apps + sessions managed at `/api/v1/oauth/connected-apps` and `/api/v1/auth/sessions` and surfaced in the dashboard's Settings page. DCR default scope is `read invoke write admin`. |
44	| `auth` | Shared `Principal` type (Kind=api_key / oauth / channel + ID/Label/Perms/Channel). Both REST middleware and MCP auth resolve the inbound bearer to a `*Principal`; downstream code (activity log, MCP tool registration) consumes the Kind directly. |
45	| `trace` | Causal-trace collector + span lifecycle (W3C `traceparent` interop, outlier detection). See `docs/TRACING.md`. |
46	| `urlhint` | Per-request `BaseURL(r)` helper. One source of truth for OAuth issuer URLs, MCP `invoke_url` fields, and audience-bound token validation. |
47	
48	**Agent channels** — bundle N functions under a name + a static bearer token; presenting that token at `/mcp` exposes ONLY those functions as MCP tools (snake_case names, invoke-only). Operator-managed at `/api/v1/channels` (`Channels` page in the dashboard). Token format: `orva_chn_<32 hex>`. Channel tokens are explicitly rejected with 401 at `/api/v1/*` — they have no Orva-management authority.
49	| `firewall` | nftables outbound allow-list per function (lazy `sync.Once` probe) |
50	| `server` | HTTP router + middleware chain + all handlers |
51	| `server/events` | SSE event hub + outbound webhook fanout |
52	| `server/handlers` | One file per resource group; `respond/` sub-package |
53	| `cli` | Shared `Client` + `Config` for CLI subcommands |
54	| `backup` | `SnapshotDB` / `ArchiveTo` / `RestoreFrom` helpers |
55	| `version` | Single source of truth for the version string |
56	| `ai` | In-product AI chat assistant. `Manager` (service layer) wires the SQLite store, the secrets cipher (provider-key encryption), the in-process tool registry, the embedded Bifrost LLM gateway (`ai/llm`), and the agentic loop (`ai/agent`). Served at `/api/v1/ai/*` by `server/ai_handler.go` (SSE for chat/approval). The agent's `defaultSystemPrompt` const lives in `ai/manager.go` — it's a Go **raw string, so it must stay backtick-free** (escape any fenced-code examples by description, not literal ```). |
57	| `ai/llm` | Wraps the embedded Bifrost gateway (`github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core`) behind neutral types + a normalized event stream. `Account` resolves BYO keys from `ai_provider_configs` live. Thinking levels → `ChatReasoning`. |
58	| `ai/agent` | Agentic loop (≈25-iteration budget): stream model turn → emit SSE deltas → detect tool calls → approval-gate writes → in-process dispatch → feed results back. Decoupled from `mcp` (takes tools + a dispatcher). Two independent gates: the per-conversation **approval policy** (`all_writes` / `destructive_only` / `auto`, checked in `approvalNeeded`) and a separate code-enforced `confirm=true` requirement on destructive tools. |
59	
60	The canonical UUIDv7 generator (`ids`) and HTTP client (`client`) live at **repo-root** `internal/ids/` and `internal/client/` — shared with the slim CLI codebase, not under `backend/internal/`.
61	
62	## CLI Commands (`cmd/orva/`)
63	
64	All Cobra subcommands share one binary with the server. `orva serve` starts the daemon; every other command is a CLI client that reads `~/.orva/config.yaml`.
65	
66	Key files: `deploy.go`, `diff.go`, `functions.go`, `invoke.go`, `logs.go`, `cron.go`, `kv.go`, `jobs.go`, `secrets.go`, `webhooks.go`, `routes.go`, `keys.go`, `system.go`, `activity.go`, `completion.go`.
67	
68	## Key Patterns
69	
70	**Handler responses**: always use `respond.JSON(w, status, val)` / `respond.Error(w, status, "SLUG", "message")` from `server/handlers/respond/`.
71	
72	**Invocation funnel**: HTTP, cron, jobs, and F2F calls all go through `Worker.Dispatch()` (sync response) or `Worker.DispatchEx()` (multi-frame streaming). Never invoke nsjail directly from handlers.
73	
74	**Async DB writes**: execution rows use `database.AsyncInsertExecution*` batch writers — no synchronous DB calls on the hot proxy path.
75	
76	**Name resolution**: functions can be referenced by UUID or by name. Use `resolveFnID(db, nameOrID)` from `handlers/functions_helpers.go`.
77	
78	**Streaming wire protocol**: `response_start` → `chunk` (base64 body data) → `response_end` frames over the worker's stdin/stdout pipe. `proxy.Forward()` owns the write-loop.
79	
80	**Shared tool registry (single source of truth)**: every operator tool is declared once via `regAddTool` (`mcp/agent_registry.go`). That call registers the tool with BOTH the external MCP server (`server.go`, unchanged behavior) AND the in-process agent registry (`mcp.BuildAgentRegistry(deps, perms)`, gated to the principal's perms). The internal AI agent dispatches these tools directly as Go calls — no MCP transport, no HTTP. Same name/description/schema/destructive-hint feed both fronts, so they never drift. When adding a tool, use `regAddTool(rc, perm, def, handler)` inside a `register*Tools(rc *regCtx)` function — never bare `mcpsdk.AddTool`.
81	
82	## Middleware Chain
83	
84	`CORS → BodySizeLimit → Auth → RequestID → Logger → Handler`
85	
86	Auth middleware only runs on paths starting with `/api/`. Everything else (`/fn/`, `/metrics`, `/webhook/`, `/mcp`, custom routes) bypasses the API-key check entirely — per-function auth for invocations is enforced inside `InvokeHandler`. Internal SDK paths (`/api/v1/_kv/`, `/api/v1/_internal/`) use the per-process internal token instead of API keys.
87	
88	## Database
89	
90	SQLite WAL mode. All migrations in `internal/database/migrations.go` — additive only. `VACUUM INTO` produces consistent backup snapshots without a write lock.
91	
92	## Gotchas
93	
94	- `backend/cmd/orva/adapters/` is **generated** — edit `backend/runtimes/` instead; `make adapters-embed` syncs them.
95	- `execution_requests` has **no FK** to `executions` (intentionally dropped to fix async insert ordering); manual cascade runs in `DeleteExecution`.
96	- TypeScript deploys: after a successful `tsc`, the function's `Entrypoint` is updated to `dist/handler.js` in the DB. The validator on re-deploy checks for the source `.ts` file, not the compiled output.
97	- Zombie nsjail fix: `cmd.Wait()` is centralized in `Spawn` via `waitDone chan struct{}`; never call `Wait()` on the sandbox `cmd` anywhere else.
98	- **AI conversation editing is destructive-tail:** editing or deleting a chat message (`EditMessage` / `DeleteMessage` in `server/ai_handler.go`, backed by `database.DeleteMessagesFromSeq`) truncates the conversation at that message's `seq` — it deletes that message and every message + tool call after it, then (for edit) re-runs the turn. There is no branching history; the tail is gone. `Regenerate` is the same truncate-then-rerun on the last assistant turn.
99	- **AI turns are one-per-conversation:** the `ai.Manager` holds a keyed try-lock (`tryLockConv`/`unlockConv`) acquired by every mutating entry point (Chat, Resume, RegenerateLast, EditAndResend, DeleteMessageFrom). An overlapping turn on the same conversation is rejected — SSE `error` for streaming paths, `ai.ErrConversationBusy` → 409 for the JSON delete. `database.InsertMessage` assigns `seq` atomically inside the INSERT (`MAX(seq)+1` subquery); never split it back into a SELECT-then-INSERT.
100	- **AI gateway lifecycle:** `ai.Manager.Close()` releases the embedded Bifrost pools and is called from `Server.Shutdown` (via `s.router.ai`). The gateway is built lazily and rebuilt on provider-config change (`invalidateClient`).
101	- **Docs single source:** `docs/reference.md` is the canonical Orva reference markdown (~53 KB). `make docs-embed` syncs it to `backend/internal/mcp/reference.md` (embedded by the `get_orva_docs` MCP tool) and `frontend/public/docs.md` (served at `/docs.md` for the dashboard's Copy as Markdown button). Edit the canonical file then run `make docs-embed`; the Vue Docs page is the rendered version (separate templates) and must be updated alongside if content changes.

# Backend

Go 1.26 (bumped from 1.25 — the embedded Bifrost AI gateway requires go ≥1.26; the Dockerfile + all CI workflows pin golang 1.26 in lock-step). Module: `github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva` (rooted at the repo, not at
`backend/`). SQLite with no CGO (`modernc.org/sqlite`).

The server binary built from `backend/cmd/orva` is the daemon (`orva serve`)
plus all CLI subcommands. The CLI subcommands live at `cli/commands/`
(package `commands`) — `backend/cmd/orva/main.go` imports
`cli/commands` and calls `commands.NewRoot()` then bolts on its own
`serve` / `setup` / `init` constructors. Single source of truth for
every client subcommand; the slim standalone CLI at `cli/cmd/orva`
uses the same library.

## Build & Test

```bash
# From repo root:
make build          # → build/orva (server + CLI bundled)
make test           # go test ./...
make lint           # go vet ./...

# Direct invocations (also from repo root, since go.mod is here):
go build ./backend/cmd/orva
go test ./...
go vet ./...
```

## Package Layout (`internal/`)

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `config` | Config struct; env var + YAML loading |
| `database` | SQLite schema, migrations, all CRUD helpers |
| `registry` | In-memory function registry wrapping DB |
| `builder` | Deploy pipeline: tarball → `npm install` / `pip install` → optional `tsc` → register |
| `pool` | Warm-sandbox pool manager (`pool.Manager`) per function |
| `sandbox` | nsjail process lifecycle; `Worker` type with `Dispatch`/`DispatchEx` |
| `proxy` | HTTP → sandbox bridge; request capture (A3); streaming write-loop (C1) |
| `metrics` | Prometheus-text counters + histograms (no external deps, atomic ops) |
| `secrets` | AES-256-GCM encrypted secrets per function |
| `scheduler` | Cron runner (`robfig/cron/v3`) |
| `mcp` | MCP server (go-sdk); 70 operator-management tools OR channel-mode (one tool per bundled function, invoke-only). Auth accepts API keys, OAuth 2.1 access tokens, OR channel tokens. |
| `oauth` | OAuth 2.1 authorization server (RFC 7591 DCR + RFC 8414 metadata + PKCE S256 + RFC 8707 resource indicators + RFC 7009 revocation). Lets claude.ai/ChatGPT add `/mcp` as a custom connector via the browser. Connected apps + sessions managed at `/api/v1/oauth/connected-apps` and `/api/v1/auth/sessions` and surfaced in the dashboard's Settings page. DCR default scope is `read invoke write admin`. |
| `auth` | Shared `Principal` type (Kind=api_key / oauth / channel + ID/Label/Perms/Channel). Both REST middleware and MCP auth resolve the inbound bearer to a `*Principal`; downstream code (activity log, MCP tool registration) consumes the Kind directly. |
| `trace` | Causal-trace collector + span lifecycle (W3C `traceparent` interop, outlier detection). See `docs/TRACING.md`. |
| `urlhint` | Per-request `BaseURL(r)` helper. One source of truth for OAuth issuer URLs, MCP `invoke_url` fields, and audience-bound token validation. |

**Agent channels** — bundle N functions under a name + a static bearer token; presenting that token at `/mcp` exposes ONLY those functions as MCP tools (snake_case names, invoke-only). Operator-managed at `/api/v1/channels` (`Channels` page in the dashboard). Token format: `orva_chn_<32 hex>`. Channel tokens are explicitly rejected with 401 at `/api/v1/*` — they have no Orva-management authority.
| `firewall` | nftables outbound allow-list per function (lazy `sync.Once` probe) |
| `server` | HTTP router + middleware chain + all handlers |
| `server/events` | SSE event hub + outbound webhook fanout |
| `server/handlers` | One file per resource group; `respond/` sub-package |
| `cli` | Shared `Client` + `Config` for CLI subcommands |
| `backup` | `SnapshotDB` / `ArchiveTo` / `RestoreFrom` helpers |
| `version` | Single source of truth for the version string |
| `ai` | In-product AI chat assistant. `Manager` (service layer) wires the SQLite store, the secrets cipher (provider-key encryption), the in-process tool registry, the embedded Bifrost LLM gateway (`ai/llm`), and the agentic loop (`ai/agent`). Served at `/api/v1/ai/*` by `server/ai_handler.go` (SSE for chat/approval). The agent's `defaultSystemPrompt` const lives in `ai/manager.go` — it's a Go **raw string, so it must stay backtick-free** (escape any fenced-code examples by description, not literal ```). |
| `ai/llm` | Wraps the embedded Bifrost gateway (`github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core`) behind neutral types + a normalized event stream. `Account` resolves BYO keys from `ai_provider_configs` live. Thinking levels → `ChatReasoning`. |
| `ai/agent` | Agentic loop (≈25-iteration budget): stream model turn → emit SSE deltas → detect tool calls → approval-gate writes → in-process dispatch → feed results back. Decoupled from `mcp` (takes tools + a dispatcher). Two independent gates: the per-conversation **approval policy** (`all_writes` / `destructive_only` / `auto`, checked in `approvalNeeded`) and a separate code-enforced `confirm=true` requirement on destructive tools. |

The canonical UUIDv7 generator (`ids`) and HTTP client (`client`) live at **repo-root** `internal/ids/` and `internal/client/` — shared with the slim CLI codebase, not under `backend/internal/`.

## CLI Commands (`cmd/orva/`)

All Cobra subcommands share one binary with the server. `orva serve` starts the daemon; every other command is a CLI client that reads `~/.orva/config.yaml`.

Key files: `deploy.go`, `diff.go`, `functions.go`, `invoke.go`, `logs.go`, `cron.go`, `kv.go`, `jobs.go`, `secrets.go`, `webhooks.go`, `routes.go`, `keys.go`, `system.go`, `activity.go`, `completion.go`.

## Key Patterns

**Handler responses**: always use `respond.JSON(w, status, val)` / `respond.Error(w, status, "SLUG", "message")` from `server/handlers/respond/`.

**Invocation funnel**: HTTP, cron, jobs, and F2F calls all go through `Worker.Dispatch()` (sync response) or `Worker.DispatchEx()` (multi-frame streaming). Never invoke nsjail directly from handlers.

**Async DB writes**: execution rows use `database.AsyncInsertExecution*` batch writers — no synchronous DB calls on the hot proxy path.

**Name resolution**: functions can be referenced by UUID or by name. Use `resolveFnID(db, nameOrID)` from `handlers/functions_helpers.go`.

**Streaming wire protocol**: `response_start` → `chunk` (base64 body data) → `response_end` frames over the worker's stdin/stdout pipe. `proxy.Forward()` owns the write-loop.

**Shared tool registry (single source of truth)**: every operator tool is declared once via `regAddTool` (`mcp/agent_registry.go`). That call registers the tool with BOTH the external MCP server (`server.go`, unchanged behavior) AND the in-process agent registry (`mcp.BuildAgentRegistry(deps, perms)`, gated to the principal's perms). The internal AI agent dispatches these tools directly as Go calls — no MCP transport, no HTTP. Same name/description/schema/destructive-hint feed both fronts, so they never drift. When adding a tool, use `regAddTool(rc, perm, def, handler)` inside a `register*Tools(rc *regCtx)` function — never bare `mcpsdk.AddTool`.

## Middleware Chain

`CORS → BodySizeLimit → Auth → RequestID → Logger → Handler`

Auth middleware only runs on paths starting with `/api/`. Everything else (`/fn/`, `/metrics`, `/webhook/`, `/mcp`, custom routes) bypasses the API-key check entirely — per-function auth for invocations is enforced inside `InvokeHandler`. Internal SDK paths (`/api/v1/_kv/`, `/api/v1/_internal/`) use the per-process internal token instead of API keys.

## Database

SQLite WAL mode. All migrations in `internal/database/migrations.go` — additive only. `VACUUM INTO` produces consistent backup snapshots without a write lock.

## Gotchas

- `backend/cmd/orva/adapters/` is **generated** — edit `backend/runtimes/` instead; `make adapters-embed` syncs them.
- `execution_requests` has **no FK** to `executions` (intentionally dropped to fix async insert ordering); manual cascade runs in `DeleteExecution`.
- TypeScript deploys: after a successful `tsc`, the function's `Entrypoint` is updated to `dist/handler.js` in the DB. The validator on re-deploy checks for the source `.ts` file, not the compiled output.
- Zombie nsjail fix: `cmd.Wait()` is centralized in `Spawn` via `waitDone chan struct{}`; never call `Wait()` on the sandbox `cmd` anywhere else.
- **AI conversation editing is destructive-tail:** editing or deleting a chat message (`EditMessage` / `DeleteMessage` in `server/ai_handler.go`, backed by `database.DeleteMessagesFromSeq`) truncates the conversation at that message's `seq` — it deletes that message and every message + tool call after it, then (for edit) re-runs the turn. There is no branching history; the tail is gone. `Regenerate` is the same truncate-then-rerun on the last assistant turn.
- **AI turns are one-per-conversation:** the `ai.Manager` holds a keyed try-lock (`tryLockConv`/`unlockConv`) acquired by every mutating entry point (Chat, Resume, RegenerateLast, EditAndResend, DeleteMessageFrom). An overlapping turn on the same conversation is rejected — SSE `error` for streaming paths, `ai.ErrConversationBusy` → 409 for the JSON delete. `database.InsertMessage` assigns `seq` atomically inside the INSERT (`MAX(seq)+1` subquery); never split it back into a SELECT-then-INSERT.
- **AI gateway lifecycle:** `ai.Manager.Close()` releases the embedded Bifrost pools and is called from `Server.Shutdown` (via `s.router.ai`). The gateway is built lazily and rebuilt on provider-config change (`invalidateClient`).
- **Docs single source:** `docs/reference.md` is the canonical Orva reference markdown (~53 KB). `make docs-embed` syncs it to `backend/internal/mcp/reference.md` (embedded by the `get_orva_docs` MCP tool) and `frontend/public/docs.md` (served at `/docs.md` for the dashboard's Copy as Markdown button). Edit the canonical file then run `make docs-embed`; the Vue Docs page is the rendered version (separate templates) and must be updated alongside if content changes.

1	# Architecture
2	
3	Orva is a single-binary Go server (`orvad`) that fronts an HTTP API,
4	spawns nsjail-isolated workers per function, and serves a Vue
5	dashboard from the same port. SQLite is the only storage backend.
6	There is no separate control plane and no clustering — one host runs
7	the whole thing.
8	
9	## Component map
10	
11	What runs on the host:
12	
13	```
14	host kernel  (Linux ≥ 5.10, cgroup v2, unprivileged userns)
15	  │
16	  └─ orvad   (single Go process, listens on :8443)
17	       │
18	       ├─ HTTP server     /api  /web  /auth  /events (SSE)  /mcp
19	       ├─ Pool manager    per-function warm workers + KPA autoscaler
20	       ├─ Build queue     extract → install deps → atomic publish
21	       ├─ Event hub       SSE pub/sub for metrics + exec + deploy
22	       ├─ MCP server      operator-management tools (also reused by the AI agent)
23	       ├─ AI assistant    in-product agentic chat: Bifrost LLM gateway +
24	       │                  agentic loop, dispatches MCP tools in-process (SSE)
25	       ├─ GC goroutine    prunes archived versions per system_config
26	       └─ SQLite          orva.db (WAL mode), single file
27	                          │
28	       spawns ▼ (one per cold-start invocation)
29	                          │
30	       ┌──────────────────┴───────────────────┐
31	       │                                      │
32	  nsjail worker                          nsjail worker     ...
33	  ┌────────────────────┐                 ┌────────────────────┐
34	  │ user namespace     │                 │ user namespace     │
35	  │ chroot → rootfs    │                 │ chroot → rootfs    │
36	  │ /code (read-only)  │                 │ /code (read-only)  │
37	  │ tmpfs /tmp         │                 │ tmpfs /tmp         │
38	  │ cgroup v2 limits   │                 │ cgroup v2 limits   │
39	  │ seccomp filter     │                 │ seccomp filter     │
40	  │ user code          │                 │ user code          │
41	  └────────────────────┘                 └────────────────────┘
42	```
43	
44	What's connected to what (data flow inside orvad):
45	
46	```
47	HTTP request  ──▶  HTTP server  ──▶  Pool manager  ──▶  nsjail worker
48	                                          │                  │
49	                                          │              user code
50	                                          │                  │
51	                                          ▼              response
52	                                     Idle/Busy
53	                                     channel pool
54	
55	POST /functions/.../deploy-inline  ──▶  Build queue  ──▶  versions/<hash>/
56	                                                          + current symlink
57	
58	Async writer  ◀──  invocation finished  ──▶  Event hub  ──▶  /events SSE
59	     │                                            │
60	     ▼                                            ▼
61	  SQLite                                    Browser EventSource
62	  (executions table)                        (Dashboard live tiles)
63	
64	All subsystems read/write a single SQLite file (orva.db):
65	  users, sessions, api_keys, functions, deployments, executions,
66	  execution_logs, build_logs, secrets, routes, pool_config, system_config
67	```
68	
69	## Process model
70	
71	Single Go process. No fork, no IPC for control flow — the autoscaler,
72	build queue, GC, and event hub all live as goroutines inside `orvad`.
73	
74	The only out-of-process work is **per-invocation nsjail spawn**:
75	`orvad` calls `nsjail` as a child, hands it the request frame on
76	stdin, reads the response frame from stdout, and reaps the child. The
77	nsjail child re-execs into the language runtime (`node` or `python3`)
78	with the chroot already set up.
79	
80	Per-function pools keep nsjail+adapter processes warm so subsequent
81	invocations skip the ~50ms spawn cost.
82	
83	## Request lifecycle (cold path)
84	
85	```
86	POST /fn/xxx/health
87	     │
88	     ▼ middleware: auth → rate-limit → CORS
89	     │
90	     ▼ InvokeHandler.ServeHTTP
91	     │
92	     ▼ Registry.Get(fnID)               ← in-memory cache, SQLite fallback
93	     │
94	     ▼ poolMgr.Acquire(fnID, ctx)       ← per-fn pool; autoscaler may spawn
95	     │      │
96	     │      ├ idle worker available?    → reuse
97	     │      └ no, total < dynamicMax?   → spawnFn(ctx)
98	     │             │
99	     │             └ sandbox.Spawn(cfg) → fork nsjail → rootfs chroot
100	     │                                                  → exec adapter
101	     ▼ proxy.Forward(worker, req)
102	     │      │
103	     │      ├ JSON-encode request frame
104	     │      ├ write to worker stdin
105	     │      ├ read response frame from worker stdout (with TimeoutMS)
106	     │      └ JSON-decode statusCode/headers/body
107	     │
108	     ▼ writeResponse(w, frame)
109	     │
110	     ▼ async-insert execution row       ← drained_loop in async.go batches writes
111	     │
112	     ▼ events.Hub.Publish("execution")  ← SSE subscribers see it live
113	     │
114	     ▼ poolMgr.Release(worker)          ← worker returns to idle channel
115	                                          (or killed if dynamicMax shrank)
116	```
117	
118	Warm path is identical except `Acquire` returns immediately from the
119	idle channel.
120	
121	## Deploy lifecycle
122	
123	```
124	POST /api/v1/functions/{id}/deploy-inline   {code, dependencies}
125	     │
126	     ▼ FunctionHandler.DeployInline
127	     │
128	     ├ tar+gz the inline code to /tmp/orva-inline-*.tar.gz
129	     │
130	     ▼ DB.InsertDeployment(status="queued", phase=null)
131	     │
132	     ▼ buildQueue.Submit(BuildJob{tarball, deploymentID})
133	     │
134	     ▼ (async) Queue.runJob in worker goroutine
135	     │      │
136	     │      ├ FnLock(fnID)              ← serializes against rollback
137	     │      ├ DB.UpdateDeploymentPhase("extract")
138	     │      ├ Builder.Build(ctx, fn, tarball)
139	     │      │     │
140	     │      │     ├ pre-flight statvfs check        → ErrInsufficientDisk
141	     │      │     ├ hashFile(tarball) → codeHash
142	     │      │     ├ if versions/<hash>/.orva-ready exists → cached short-circuit
143	     │      │     ├ scratch_dir = versions/<hash>.tmp.<rand>
144	     │      │     │     ├ extract tarball
145	     │      │     │     ├ ValidateArchive (reject path-traversal symlinks)
146	     │      │     │     ├ npm install / pip install (HOST-side, not in sandbox)
147	     │      │     │     ├ install adapter wrapper (main.js / main.py)
148	     │      │     │     └ touch .orva-ready
149	     │      │     └ atomic os.Rename(scratch_dir, versions/<hash>)
150	     │      │
151	     │      ├ DB.SetDeploymentCodeHash(deployID, codeHash)
152	     │      ├ Registry.Set(fn) with bumped version + hash
153	     │      ├ ActivateVersion(dataDir, fnID, codeHash)  ← symlink retarget
154	     │      ├ DB.FinishDeployment(succeeded)
155	     │      ├ events.Hub.Publish("deployment", {status:"succeeded", phase:"done"})
156	     │      └ poolMgr.RefreshForDeploy(fnID)  ← drains idle workers
157	     │
158	     ▼ next Acquire → spawnFn reads `current` symlink fresh → new code
159	```
160	
161	Symlink retarget is atomic (rename(2) on a symlink). nsjail binds the
162	symlink path itself (no deref at bind time), but reads-through happen
163	at exec time inside the new namespace, so workers that got their
164	`-R` mount before the swap continue serving the old code until they
165	exit. `RefreshForDeploy` drains the idle channel so the next spawn
166	picks up the new target.
167	
168	## Storage layout
169	
170	```
171	/var/lib/orva/
172	├── orva.db                                    SQLite (WAL mode)
173	├── orva.db-wal
174	├── orva.db-shm
175	├── .admin-key                                 mode 0600, plaintext bootstrap key
176	├── functions/
177	│   └── 019df200-7b00-7e00-9c00-aab1cd2e3f40/
178	│       ├── current → versions/abc1234...     atomic symlink (the active version)
179	│       └── versions/
180	│           ├── abc1234.../                   immutable per-hash dirs
181	│           │   ├── .orva-ready                marker = "this version is complete"
182	│           │   ├── handler.js                 user code
183	│           │   ├── package.json               (if deps were declared)
184	│           │   ├── node_modules/              installed at build time
185	│           │   └── main.js                    Orva's adapter wrapper
186	│           └── def5678.../
187	└── rootfs/
188	    ├── node/                                slim image with /usr/local/bin/node (Node.js 24)
189	    └── python/                              slim image with /usr/local/bin/python3 (Python 3.14)
190	```
191	
192	## Database schema
193	
194	One SQLite file, grouped by subsystem. Core tables:
195	
196	| table | what it stores |
197	|---|---|
198	| `users`              | onboarded admin/operator accounts |
199	| `sessions`           | UI cookie tokens (7-day TTL) |
200	| `api_keys`           | bearer tokens for `/api/v1/*` |
201	| `functions`          | name, runtime, current version + code_hash, status |
202	| `deployments`        | per-build audit trail (queued/building/succeeded/failed; rollback rows are source='rollback') |
203	| `executions` / `execution_requests` / `execution_logs` / `execution_log_entries` | every invocation + its captured request + stderr/stdout |
204	| `build_logs`         | stdout/stderr from `npm install` / `pip install` |
205	| `function_secrets`   | per-function encrypted env vars (AES-256-GCM) |
206	| `routes`             | custom URL → function-id mappings (`/webhooks/stripe`) |
207	| `pool_config`        | per-fn autoscaler tuning (min_warm, max_warm, target_concurrency) |
208	| `system_config`      | global tuning knobs (versions_to_keep, gc_interval_seconds, etc.) |
209	
210	Feature tables added since v0.2:
211	
212	| group | tables |
213	|---|---|
214	| Scheduling & queues  | `cron_schedules`, `jobs` |
215	| KV & fixtures        | `kv_store`, `fixtures` |
216	| Webhooks             | `event_subscriptions`, `webhook_deliveries`, `inbound_webhooks` |
217	| Tracing & activity   | `user_spans`, `activity_log` |
218	| Firewall             | `egress_blocklist` |
219	| Agent channels       | `channels`, `channel_functions` |
220	| OAuth 2.1            | `oauth_clients`, `oauth_authorization_codes`, `oauth_access_tokens` |
221	| AI assistant         | `ai_conversations`, `ai_messages`, `ai_tool_calls`, `ai_provider_configs`, `ai_settings` |
222	
223	Schema lives in [`backend/internal/database/migrations.go`](../backend/internal/database/migrations.go) (~34 tables).
224	Migrations are additive only — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + idempotent ALTER columns run on every boot. AI message/tool-call rows cascade-delete with their `ai_conversations` parent; editing or deleting a chat message truncates the conversation tail by `seq` (see `DeleteMessagesFromSeq`).
225	
226	## Component responsibilities
227	
228	### `backend/internal/server/`
229	
230	The HTTP layer. Routes, middleware, handlers, the SSE event hub.
231	Stateless — every request reaches into the pool manager, registry, or
232	DB for actual work.
233	
234	- `router.go` — `http.ServeMux` wiring, middleware chain
235	- `server.go` — `New()` constructs all subsystems and their cross-references
236	- `middleware.go` — request-id, body-size cap, CORS, logger
237	- `middleware_auth.go` — session cookie + API-key dispatch
238	- `events/` — SSE pub/sub broker (`hub.go`, `handler.go`)
239	- `handlers/` — one file per concern (functions, invoke, secrets, routes, etc.)
240	- `handlers/respond/` — error envelope helpers + `Retry-After` injection
241	
242	### `backend/internal/pool/`
243	
244	Warm worker pools, one per function, autoscaled.
245	
246	- `pool.go` — `Manager` owns a `sync.Map[fnID]*functionPool`
247	- `function_pool.go` — per-fn idle channel + acquire/release/sweep
248	- `autoscaler.go` — Knative-KPA-style: 60s stable + 6s panic windows, `dynamicMax` derived from CPU + memory budget
249	- `hostmem.go` — global memory budget tracker (refuses spawns past 80% reservation)
250	
251	### `backend/internal/sandbox/`
252	
253	nsjail invocation, per-spawn config, host-wide concurrency limiter.
254	
255	- `sandbox.go` — builds the nsjail argv (chroot, mounts, cgroup, seccomp)
256	- `worker.go` — JSON frame protocol over stdin/stdout, expiry tracking
257	- `seccomp.go` — Kafel policy (`default`, `strict`, `permissive`)
258	- `limiter.go` — host-wide `MaxConcurrent` semaphore with `TryAcquire`
259	
260	### `backend/internal/builder/`
261	
262	Build queue + version archive + GC + first-boot migration.
263	
264	- `queue.go` — bounded channel + `runtime.NumCPU()` worker goroutines
265	- `builder.go` — extract → validate → install deps → atomic publish
266	- `activate.go` — symlink retarget for both deploy and rollback

272	
273	SQLite access. No ORM — explicit queries, prepared statements where
274	hot.
275	
276	- `migrations.go` — schema + idempotent ALTER loop
277	- `async.go` — batched-flush writer for executions (50-job batches or 50ms tick)
278	- One file per resource: `functions.go`, `deployments.go`, `secrets.go`, etc.

281	
282	The bridge between HTTP and a sandbox worker.

284	- `proxy.go` — encodes request as JSON frame, writes to worker stdin, reads response frame, propagates timeouts and errors

288	In-memory function cache backed by SQLite. Hot path reads (every
289	invocation) avoid a DB round-trip.

292	
293	Encrypts/decrypts per-function env vars. Master key is derived from
294	the data dir's existence; rotation is a future project.

297	
298	In-memory ring buffer over the last ~8k invocations. Computes p50,
299	p95, p99 server-side so the dashboard doesn't recompute on every
300	poll.
301	
302	### `backend/internal/ai/`
303	
304	The in-product AI chat assistant — an agentic loop that operates the
305	instance end-to-end through the same tools the MCP server exposes, with
306	BYO provider keys. Served at `/api/v1/ai/*` (SSE for chat + approval).
307	
308	- `manager.go` — service layer: wires the SQLite chat store, the
309	  secrets cipher (provider-key encryption at rest), the in-process tool
310	  registry, the LLM gateway, and the agentic loop. Holds the agent's
311	  `defaultSystemPrompt` (a Go raw string — must stay backtick-free).
312	- `llm/` — wraps the **embedded Bifrost gateway**
313	  (`github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core`) behind neutral types + a
314	  normalized event stream. `Account` resolves BYO keys from
315	  `ai_provider_configs` at request time; thinking levels map to
316	  `ChatReasoning`. (The Bifrost dependency is why the module requires
317	  Go ≥1.26.)

329	the external MCP server — one source of truth, gated to the principal's
330	perms, so the two fronts never drift. Served by

332	`AI` sidebar section (`frontend/src/views/AI.vue`).

335	the `admin` permission; conversations are a shared operator space (not
336	isolated per credential). The manager serializes turns with a
337	per-conversation try-lock (overlapping turns are rejected, not
338	interleaved), `ai_messages.seq` is assigned atomically inside the

342

344	exec's into; it reads request frames from stdin, calls the user's

347	- `node/adapter.js` — also used for node

351	
352	Vue 3 + Pinia + Vite. Single-page dashboard served from `/web/` by the

369	  The AI chat is the exception: it streams over `fetch` +
370	  `ReadableStream` (the chat POST carries a body, so `EventSource`
371	  won't do)

373	## Concurrency model
374	
375	Goroutines do almost everything. Critical concurrency primitives:
376	
377	- **Pool manager**: per-fn `sync.Map` lookup. Each function pool has a
378	  `chan *Worker` (buffered) for idle workers — Go channels handle the
379	  acquire/release synchronization.
380	- **Per-fn lock** (`Manager.FunctionLock`): serializes deploy and
381	  rollback on the same function. Different functions are independent.
382	- **Async writer**: single goroutine drains a `chan writeJob` and
383	  batches DB inserts. Replaces the old goroutine-per-call pattern that
384	  burned CPU at sustained 500+ req/s.
385	- **Autoscaler**: one goroutine per `Manager`, ticks every second,
386	  evaluates each function's pool against its EWMA stable + panic
387	  windows.
388	- **Reaper**: one goroutine per pool, sweeps idle workers past TTL.
389	- **GC**: one goroutine, prunes archived version dirs every 5 minutes.
390	- **Build queue**: `runtime.NumCPU()` worker goroutines drain a job
391	  channel.
392	- **Event hub**: subscribers each have a 32-deep buffered channel.
393	  Producers drop events for slow consumers rather than block.
394	
395	## Why these choices
396	
397	**Why a single binary?** Operational simplicity. One process to
398	upgrade, one log to tail, one volume to back up. We give up the option
399	of horizontal scaling — but the target is a self-hosted, single-host
400	deployment, where horizontal scaling is over-engineering.
401	
402	**Why SQLite?** The target is single-host. Postgres would force
403	operators to run two services and manage credentials between them. The
404	write rate is bounded by invocation throughput (one row per
405	invocation), and the async writer batches commits. SQLite in WAL mode
406	handles thousands of writes per second on commodity hardware.
407	
408	**Why nsjail per invocation?** Hardware isolation requires either
409	process-level (nsjail / gvisor / kata) or VM-level (firecracker)
410	sandboxing. nsjail is the cheapest — single fork + namespace setup,
411	no VM boot. Per-invocation isolation means a function compromise
412	cannot affect another function or the host. Warm pools amortize the
413	spawn cost.
414	
415	**Why Knative-style autoscaling?** Two-window EWMA (stable +
416	panic) handles bursty traffic gracefully. Stable smooths out transient
417	spikes; panic responds within seconds when sustained load arrives.
418	Combined with per-fn `dynamicMax` capped on CPU + memory budget, the
419	host stays healthy during traffic floods.
420	
421	**Why content-addressed deploys?** Identical redeploys are a no-op
422	(same hash → cached version dir). Rollback is a symlink retarget.
423	Garbage collection is "delete versions not in the keep window." The
424	alternative — re-extract and re-install on every redeploy — is
425	slower and provides no rollback story.
426	
427	## Reading order for new contributors

429	1. `backend/cmd/orva/serve.go` — entrypoint; see how everything wires up

# Architecture

Orva is a single-binary Go server (`orvad`) that fronts an HTTP API,
spawns nsjail-isolated workers per function, and serves a Vue
dashboard from the same port. SQLite is the only storage backend.
There is no separate control plane and no clustering — one host runs
the whole thing.

## Component map

What runs on the host:

```
host kernel  (Linux ≥ 5.10, cgroup v2, unprivileged userns)
  │
  └─ orvad   (single Go process, listens on :8443)
       │
       ├─ HTTP server     /api  /web  /auth  /events (SSE)  /mcp
       ├─ Pool manager    per-function warm workers + KPA autoscaler
       ├─ Build queue     extract → install deps → atomic publish
       ├─ Event hub       SSE pub/sub for metrics + exec + deploy
       ├─ MCP server      operator-management tools (also reused by the AI agent)
       ├─ AI assistant    in-product agentic chat: Bifrost LLM gateway +
       │                  agentic loop, dispatches MCP tools in-process (SSE)
       ├─ GC goroutine    prunes archived versions per system_config
       └─ SQLite          orva.db (WAL mode), single file
                          │
       spawns ▼ (one per cold-start invocation)
                          │
       ┌──────────────────┴───────────────────┐
       │                                      │
  nsjail worker                          nsjail worker     ...
  ┌────────────────────┐                 ┌────────────────────┐
  │ user namespace     │                 │ user namespace     │
  │ chroot → rootfs    │                 │ chroot → rootfs    │
  │ /code (read-only)  │                 │ /code (read-only)  │
  │ tmpfs /tmp         │                 │ tmpfs /tmp         │
  │ cgroup v2 limits   │                 │ cgroup v2 limits   │
  │ seccomp filter     │                 │ seccomp filter     │
  │ user code          │                 │ user code          │
  └────────────────────┘                 └────────────────────┘
```

What's connected to what (data flow inside orvad):

```
HTTP request  ──▶  HTTP server  ──▶  Pool manager  ──▶  nsjail worker
                                          │                  │
                                          │              user code
                                          │                  │
                                          ▼              response
                                     Idle/Busy
                                     channel pool

POST /functions/.../deploy-inline  ──▶  Build queue  ──▶  versions/<hash>/
                                                          + current symlink

Async writer  ◀──  invocation finished  ──▶  Event hub  ──▶  /events SSE
     │                                            │
     ▼                                            ▼
  SQLite                                    Browser EventSource
  (executions table)                        (Dashboard live tiles)

All subsystems read/write a single SQLite file (orva.db):
  users, sessions, api_keys, functions, deployments, executions,
  execution_logs, build_logs, secrets, routes, pool_config, system_config
```

## Process model

Single Go process. No fork, no IPC for control flow — the autoscaler,
build queue, GC, and event hub all live as goroutines inside `orvad`.

The only out-of-process work is **per-invocation nsjail spawn**:
`orvad` calls `nsjail` as a child, hands it the request frame on
stdin, reads the response frame from stdout, and reaps the child. The
nsjail child re-execs into the language runtime (`node` or `python3`)
with the chroot already set up.

Per-function pools keep nsjail+adapter processes warm so subsequent
invocations skip the ~50ms spawn cost.

## Request lifecycle (cold path)

```
POST /fn/xxx/health
     │
     ▼ middleware: auth → rate-limit → CORS
     │
     ▼ InvokeHandler.ServeHTTP
     │
     ▼ Registry.Get(fnID)               ← in-memory cache, SQLite fallback
     │
     ▼ poolMgr.Acquire(fnID, ctx)       ← per-fn pool; autoscaler may spawn
     │      │
     │      ├ idle worker available?    → reuse
     │      └ no, total < dynamicMax?   → spawnFn(ctx)
     │             │
     │             └ sandbox.Spawn(cfg) → fork nsjail → rootfs chroot
     │                                                  → exec adapter
     ▼ proxy.Forward(worker, req)
     │      │
     │      ├ JSON-encode request frame
     │      ├ write to worker stdin
     │      ├ read response frame from worker stdout (with TimeoutMS)
     │      └ JSON-decode statusCode/headers/body
     │
     ▼ writeResponse(w, frame)
     │
     ▼ async-insert execution row       ← drained_loop in async.go batches writes
     │
     ▼ events.Hub.Publish("execution")  ← SSE subscribers see it live
     │
     ▼ poolMgr.Release(worker)          ← worker returns to idle channel
                                          (or killed if dynamicMax shrank)
```

Warm path is identical except `Acquire` returns immediately from the
idle channel.

## Deploy lifecycle

```
POST /api/v1/functions/{id}/deploy-inline   {code, dependencies}
     │
     ▼ FunctionHandler.DeployInline
     │
     ├ tar+gz the inline code to /tmp/orva-inline-*.tar.gz
     │
     ▼ DB.InsertDeployment(status="queued", phase=null)
     │
     ▼ buildQueue.Submit(BuildJob{tarball, deploymentID})
     │
     ▼ (async) Queue.runJob in worker goroutine
     │      │
     │      ├ FnLock(fnID)              ← serializes against rollback
     │      ├ DB.UpdateDeploymentPhase("extract")
     │      ├ Builder.Build(ctx, fn, tarball)
     │      │     │
     │      │     ├ pre-flight statvfs check        → ErrInsufficientDisk
     │      │     ├ hashFile(tarball) → codeHash
     │      │     ├ if versions/<hash>/.orva-ready exists → cached short-circuit
     │      │     ├ scratch_dir = versions/<hash>.tmp.<rand>
     │      │     │     ├ extract tarball
     │      │     │     ├ ValidateArchive (reject path-traversal symlinks)
     │      │     │     ├ npm install / pip install (HOST-side, not in sandbox)
     │      │     │     ├ install adapter wrapper (main.js / main.py)
     │      │     │     └ touch .orva-ready
     │      │     └ atomic os.Rename(scratch_dir, versions/<hash>)
     │      │
     │      ├ DB.SetDeploymentCodeHash(deployID, codeHash)
     │      ├ Registry.Set(fn) with bumped version + hash
     │      ├ ActivateVersion(dataDir, fnID, codeHash)  ← symlink retarget
     │      ├ DB.FinishDeployment(succeeded)
     │      ├ events.Hub.Publish("deployment", {status:"succeeded", phase:"done"})
     │      └ poolMgr.RefreshForDeploy(fnID)  ← drains idle workers
     │
     ▼ next Acquire → spawnFn reads `current` symlink fresh → new code
```

Symlink retarget is atomic (rename(2) on a symlink). nsjail binds the
symlink path itself (no deref at bind time), but reads-through happen
at exec time inside the new namespace, so workers that got their
`-R` mount before the swap continue serving the old code until they
exit. `RefreshForDeploy` drains the idle channel so the next spawn
picks up the new target.

## Storage layout

```
/var/lib/orva/
├── orva.db                                    SQLite (WAL mode)
├── orva.db-wal
├── orva.db-shm
├── .admin-key                                 mode 0600, plaintext bootstrap key
├── functions/
│   └── 019df200-7b00-7e00-9c00-aab1cd2e3f40/
│       ├── current → versions/abc1234...     atomic symlink (the active version)
│       └── versions/
│           ├── abc1234.../                   immutable per-hash dirs
│           │   ├── .orva-ready                marker = "this version is complete"
│           │   ├── handler.js                 user code
│           │   ├── package.json               (if deps were declared)
│           │   ├── node_modules/              installed at build time
│           │   └── main.js                    Orva's adapter wrapper
│           └── def5678.../
└── rootfs/
    ├── node/                                slim image with /usr/local/bin/node (Node.js 24)
    └── python/                              slim image with /usr/local/bin/python3 (Python 3.14)
```

## Database schema

One SQLite file, grouped by subsystem. Core tables:

| table | what it stores |
|---|---|
| `users`              | onboarded admin/operator accounts |
| `sessions`           | UI cookie tokens (7-day TTL) |
| `api_keys`           | bearer tokens for `/api/v1/*` |
| `functions`          | name, runtime, current version + code_hash, status |
| `deployments`        | per-build audit trail (queued/building/succeeded/failed; rollback rows are source='rollback') |
| `executions` / `execution_requests` / `execution_logs` / `execution_log_entries` | every invocation + its captured request + stderr/stdout |
| `build_logs`         | stdout/stderr from `npm install` / `pip install` |
| `function_secrets`   | per-function encrypted env vars (AES-256-GCM) |
| `routes`             | custom URL → function-id mappings (`/webhooks/stripe`) |
| `pool_config`        | per-fn autoscaler tuning (min_warm, max_warm, target_concurrency) |
| `system_config`      | global tuning knobs (versions_to_keep, gc_interval_seconds, etc.) |

Feature tables added since v0.2:

| group | tables |
|---|---|
| Scheduling & queues  | `cron_schedules`, `jobs` |
| KV & fixtures        | `kv_store`, `fixtures` |
| Webhooks             | `event_subscriptions`, `webhook_deliveries`, `inbound_webhooks` |
| Tracing & activity   | `user_spans`, `activity_log` |
| Firewall             | `egress_blocklist` |
| Agent channels       | `channels`, `channel_functions` |
| OAuth 2.1            | `oauth_clients`, `oauth_authorization_codes`, `oauth_access_tokens` |
| AI assistant         | `ai_conversations`, `ai_messages`, `ai_tool_calls`, `ai_provider_configs`, `ai_settings` |

Schema lives in [`backend/internal/database/migrations.go`](../backend/internal/database/migrations.go) (~34 tables).
Migrations are additive only — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + idempotent ALTER columns run on every boot. AI message/tool-call rows cascade-delete with their `ai_conversations` parent; editing or deleting a chat message truncates the conversation tail by `seq` (see `DeleteMessagesFromSeq`).

  `chan *Worker` (buffered) for idle workers — Go channels handle the
  acquire/release synchronization.
- **Per-fn lock** (`Manager.FunctionLock`): serializes deploy and
  rollback on the same function. Different functions are independent.
- **Async writer**: single goroutine drains a `chan writeJob` and
  batches DB inserts. Replaces the old goroutine-per-call pattern that
  burned CPU at sustained 500+ req/s.
- **Autoscaler**: one goroutine per `Manager`, ticks every second,
  evaluates each function's pool against its EWMA stable + panic
  windows.
- **Reaper**: one goroutine per pool, sweeps idle workers past TTL.
- **GC**: one goroutine, prunes archived version dirs every 5 minutes.
- **Build queue**: `runtime.NumCPU()` worker goroutines drain a job
  channel.
- **Event hub**: subscribers each have a 32-deep buffered channel.
  Producers drop events for slow consumers rather than block.

## Why these choices

**Why a single binary?** Operational simplicity. One process to
upgrade, one log to tail, one volume to back up. We give up the option
of horizontal scaling — but the target is a self-hosted, single-host
deployment, where horizontal scaling is over-engineering.

**Why SQLite?** The target is single-host. Postgres would force
operators to run two services and manage credentials between them. The
write rate is bounded by invocation throughput (one row per
invocation), and the async writer batches commits. SQLite in WAL mode
handles thousands of writes per second on commodity hardware.

**Why nsjail per invocation?** Hardware isolation requires either
process-level (nsjail / gvisor / kata) or VM-level (firecracker)
sandboxing. nsjail is the cheapest — single fork + namespace setup,
no VM boot. Per-invocation isolation means a function compromise
cannot affect another function or the host. Warm pools amortize the
spawn cost.

**Why Knative-style autoscaling?** Two-window EWMA (stable +
panic) handles bursty traffic gracefully. Stable smooths out transient
spikes; panic responds within seconds when sustained load arrives.
Combined with per-fn `dynamicMax` capped on CPU + memory budget, the
host stays healthy during traffic floods.

**Why content-addressed deploys?** Identical redeploys are a no-op
(same hash → cached version dir). Rollback is a symlink retarget.
Garbage collection is "delete versions not in the keep window." The
alternative — re-extract and re-install on every redeploy — is
slower and provides no rollback story.

## Reading order for new contributors

1. `backend/cmd/orva/serve.go` — entrypoint; see how everything wires up
2. `backend/internal/server/server.go::New` — main constructor
3. `backend/internal/server/handlers/invoke.go` — hot path (HTTP → pool → sandbox)
4. `backend/internal/pool/pool.go::Manager` + `function_pool.go::acquire` — the warm-pool dance
5. `backend/internal/builder/builder.go::Build` + `activate.go::ActivateVersion` — deploy + rollback
6. `frontend/src/stores/events.js` + `frontend/src/views/Dashboard.vue` — SSE consumption

# docs/

Human-maintained reference documentation. Keep these in sync when changing API shapes, config keys, runtime behavior, or operational procedures.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `API.md` | Full REST API reference — every endpoint, request/response shapes, error codes |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | System design, component diagram, request lifecycle |
| `CAPACITY.md` | Sizing guide, pool tuning, resource limits per runtime |
| `CLI.md` | `orva` CLI reference — every subcommand, flags, examples |
| `CONFIG.md` | All configuration keys, environment variables, and defaults |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Dev environment setup, PR process, code style conventions |
| `DEPLOYMENT.md` | Docker, bare-metal, reverse proxy setup, TLS termination |
| `ERRORS.md` | Error slug catalog — `SLUG → HTTP status → human meaning` |
| `GVISOR.md` | gVisor (`runsc`) runtime evaluation — incompatibility writeup |
| `KATA.md` | Kata Containers runtime evaluation — supported configurations + measured cost |
| `OPERATIONS.md` | Day-2 ops: backup/restore, VACUUM, log rotation, upgrades |
| `RUNTIMES.md` | Per-runtime handler contract, streaming (generators/async iterables), TypeScript |
| `SECURITY.md` | Threat model, nsjail sandbox isolation, network firewall (nftables) |
| `SUPPORT.md` | Support matrix — distros, kernels, container runtimes |
| `TRACING.md` | Causal trace model, propagation, W3C interop, outlier detection |
| `reference.md` | **Canonical** Orva reference (~53 KB GFM markdown) — single source of truth shipped to the dashboard's Copy-as-Markdown button (via `frontend/public/docs.md`) and the `get_orva_docs` MCP tool (via `backend/internal/mcp/reference.md`). `make docs-embed` syncs both copies. Uses `{{ORIGIN}}` placeholders that consumers substitute at runtime. |

## Update Triggers

- New REST endpoint → update `API.md`
- New CLI subcommand or flag → update `CLI.md`
- New config key → update `CONFIG.md`
- New error slug → update `ERRORS.md`
- Runtime behavior change → update `RUNTIMES.md`
- Backup/restore or vacuum changes → update `OPERATIONS.md`
- Security boundary change → update `SECURITY.md`
- New container-runtime evaluation → add `<NAME>.md` (mirror `KATA.md` / `GVISOR.md`) + update `SUPPORT.md` and the README runtime-support table

23	var ErrWorkerExited = errors.New("worker exited unexpectedly")
24	
25	// Worker is a long-lived nsjail+adapter process held by the pool. It
26	// serializes one request at a time — callers hold exclusive access for the
27	// duration of a Dispatch. Stdout is the length-prefixed protocol stream;
28	// stderr is drained in the background into a ring buffer.
29	type Worker struct {
30		Cmd     *exec.Cmd
31		stdin   io.WriteCloser
32		stdout  io.ReadCloser
33		stderr  io.ReadCloser
34		Spawned time.Time
35		Served  atomic.Int64

38		// cgroup after its jailed child's PID, which isn't known until after fork).
39		// AcquireUsec and AcquireAt are stamped by the pool before handing the
40		// worker to a caller and read at release for per-function EWMA metrics.
41		cgroupPathMu sync.Mutex
42		CgroupPath   string
43		AcquireUsec  int64
44		AcquireAt    time.Time

55		// process. Quit() / Kill() use this to synchronize their grace timers
56		// without ever calling cmd.Wait() themselves — that prevents the
57		// "Wait was already called" race we used to hit when a Quit grace
58		// expired and the escalation path called Kill() concurrently.
59		//

173		}()
174	
175		return w, nil
176	}
177	
178	// Dispatch writes a request frame and reads the response frame. Returns
179	// (respBody, stderrSnapshot, err). On context cancellation or protocol
180	// error the worker is marked dead and must not be reused.
181	//
182	// Backwards-compatible non-streaming wrapper around DispatchEx. For
183	// streaming responses (v0.4 C1) callers should prefer DispatchEx so they
184	// can drive chunk frames out to the HTTP client incrementally.
185	func (w *Worker) Dispatch(ctx context.Context, eventJSON []byte) ([]byte, []byte, error) {
186		res, err := w.DispatchEx(ctx, eventJSON)
187		if err != nil {
188			var stderr []byte
189			if res != nil {
190				stderr = res.Stderr()
191			}
192			return nil, stderr, err
193		}
194		if res.Streaming {
195			// Caller used the back-compat path on a streaming handler. Drain
196			// chunks into a buffer so the existing single-write path still
197			// works; this is the path tests + non-HTTP callers take.
198			var buf []byte
199			for {
200				kind, data, err := res.NextFrame(ctx)
201				if err != nil {
202					return nil, res.Stderr(), err
203				}
204				if kind == "end" {
205					break
206				}
207				if kind == "chunk" {
208					buf = append(buf, data...)
209				}
210			}
211			envelope, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
212				"statusCode": res.StatusCode,
213				"headers":    res.Headers,
214				"body":       string(buf),
215			})
216			return envelope, res.Stderr(), nil
217		}
218		envelope, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
219			"statusCode": res.StatusCode,
220			"headers":    res.Headers,
221			"body":       res.Body,
222		})
223		return envelope, res.Stderr(), nil
224	}
225	
226	// DispatchResult is returned from DispatchEx. Two shapes:
227	//
228	//   - Streaming=false: StatusCode/Headers/Body fully populated; the call
229	//     completed with the historical single-frame "response" path. Callers
230	//     just write the envelope and move on.
231	//   - Streaming=true:  StatusCode/Headers populated from "response_start";
232	//     Body is empty. Caller MUST loop on NextFrame until kind == "end".
233	//     During the loop the Worker holds w.mu — Release should run only
234	//     after the loop terminates.
235	//
236	// Stderr() is safe to call at any point; it returns the bytes written to
237	// the worker's stderr ring buffer since dispatch began. Most callers wait
238	// until after the loop completes so they capture the full snapshot.
239	type DispatchResult struct {
240		Streaming  bool
241		StatusCode int
242		Headers    map[string]string
243		Body       string
244	
245		w         *Worker
246		errBefore int64
247		finished  bool
248		// readErr is sticky — once the underlying pipe surfaces an error, all
249		// subsequent NextFrame calls return it.
250		readErr error
251		// finishHook is called exactly once when the streaming loop reaches a
252		// terminal state (end / error / ctx-cancel). Used by DispatchEx to
253		// release the worker mutex it held across the stream.
254		finishHook func()
255	}
256	
257	// finalize runs the finishHook (if set) exactly once. Idempotent.
258	func (r *DispatchResult) finalize() {
259		if r.finishHook != nil {
260			hook := r.finishHook
261			r.finishHook = nil
262			hook()
263		}
264	}
265	
266	// NextFrame reads the next frame from a streaming response. Returns:
267	//
268	//	kind="chunk", data=<bytes>   — one chunk of body bytes
269	//	kind="end",   data=nil       — terminator; loop should exit
270	//	kind="",      err=...        — protocol error; worker is dead
271	//
272	// An empty chunk (data length 0) is a heartbeat from the adapter and is
273	// surfaced as kind="chunk", data=nil. Callers can choose to forward an
274	// empty Write+Flush (keeps proxies/LBs alive) or skip it.
275	func (r *DispatchResult) NextFrame(ctx context.Context) (kind string, data []byte, err error) {
276		if r.finished {
277			r.finalize()
278			return "end", nil, nil
279		}
280		if r.readErr != nil {
281			r.finalize()
282			return "", nil, r.readErr
283		}
284	
285		// Read the next frame from worker stdout, with ctx cancellation.
286		type framePayload struct {
287			payload []byte
288			err     error
289		}
290		ch := make(chan framePayload, 1)
291		go func() {
292			p, err := readFrame(r.w.stdout)
293			ch <- framePayload{p, err}
294		}()
295		select {
296		case fp := <-ch:
297			if fp.err != nil {
298				r.w.markDead()
299				r.readErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: read chunk frame: %v", ErrWorkerExited, fp.err)
300				r.finalize()
301				return "", nil, r.readErr
302			}
303			var f frameResponse
304			if err := json.Unmarshal(fp.payload, &f); err != nil {
305				r.w.markDead()
306				r.readErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid chunk frame: %v", ErrWorkerExited, err)
307				r.finalize()
308				return "", nil, r.readErr
309			}
310			switch f.Type {
311			case "chunk":
312				// Body bytes are base64 to keep the JSON transport binary-safe.
313				if f.Data == "" {
314					return "chunk", nil, nil
315				}
316				dec, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(f.Data)
317				if err != nil {
318					r.w.markDead()
319					r.readErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid chunk data: %v", ErrWorkerExited, err)
320					r.finalize()
321					return "", nil, r.readErr
322				}
323				return "chunk", dec, nil
324			case "response_end":
325				r.finished = true
326				r.w.Served.Add(1)
327				r.finalize()
328				return "end", nil, nil
329			case "error":
330				// Adapter surfaced an error mid-stream. Always treat as fatal
331				// because the response head was already written — there is no
332				// clean way to convert this into a 5xx envelope at this point.
333				r.w.markDead()
334				r.readErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: adapter mid-stream error: %s", ErrWorkerExited, f.Message)
335				r.finalize()
336				return "", nil, r.readErr
337			default:
338				r.w.markDead()
339				r.readErr = fmt.Errorf("%w: unexpected stream frame type %q", ErrWorkerExited, f.Type)
340				r.finalize()
341				return "", nil, r.readErr
342			}
343		case <-ctx.Done():
344			r.w.markDead()
345			r.readErr = ctx.Err()
346			r.finalize()
347			return "", nil, r.readErr
348		}
349	}
350	
351	// Stderr returns the bytes written to the worker's stderr since dispatch
352	// began. Callers typically defer this until after the streaming loop has
353	// drained so the snapshot covers the full handler invocation.
354	func (r *DispatchResult) Stderr() []byte {
355		if r == nil || r.w == nil {
356			return nil
357		}
358		return r.w.errBuf.Snapshot(r.errBefore)
359	}
360	
361	// DispatchEx writes a request frame, reads the FIRST response frame, and
362	// dispatches by frame type:
363	//
364	//   - "response"        → DispatchResult{Streaming:false} populated end-to-end
365	//   - "response_start"  → DispatchResult{Streaming:true}; caller drives
366	//     NextFrame until kind=="end"
367	//
368	// On protocol errors the worker is marked dead. Worker.mu is held until
369	// the streaming caller finishes the loop (DispatchEx releases it inside
370	// NextFrame's terminal cases via finished=true; non-streaming returns
371	// release the lock immediately). This matches the contract that one
372	// Worker handles one request at a time.
373	//
374	// NOTE: holding w.mu across the streaming loop is fine because the pool
375	// guarantees a single goroutine owns each Worker, and Release happens
376	// after the proxy's Forward unwinds.
377	func (w *Worker) DispatchEx(ctx context.Context, eventJSON []byte) (*DispatchResult, error) {
378		if w.dead.Load() {
379			return nil, errors.New("worker dead")
380		}
381		w.mu.Lock()
382		// We can't unconditionally defer Unlock here because streaming holds
383		// the lock until NextFrame finishes. Both terminal paths (non-stream
384		// + stream-end + error) take responsibility for unlocking.
385		unlocked := false
386		unlock := func() {
387			if !unlocked {
388				unlocked = true
389				w.mu.Unlock()
390			}
391		}
392	
393		if w.dead.Load() {
394			unlock()
395			return nil, errors.New("worker dead")
396		}
397	
398		errBefore := w.errBuf.Len()
399	
400		// Compose the request frame: {"type":"request","event":<raw>}.
401		reqFrame, _ := json.Marshal(frameRequest{Type: "request", Event: json.RawMessage(eventJSON)})
402	
403		// Wire write must complete or we bail.
404		writeErrCh := make(chan error, 1)
405		go func() {
406			writeErrCh <- writeFrame(w.stdin, reqFrame)
407		}()
408	
409		// Read FIRST response frame on another goroutine so ctx cancel can
410		// break us out.
411		respCh := make(chan []byte, 1)
412		readErrCh := make(chan error, 1)
413		go func() {
414			payload, err := readFrame(w.stdout)
415			if err != nil {
416				readErrCh <- err
417				return
418			}
419			respCh <- payload
420		}()
421	
422		select {
423		case err := <-writeErrCh:
424			if err != nil {
425				w.markDead()
426				unlock()
427				return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore},
428					fmt.Errorf("%w: write frame: %v", ErrWorkerExited, err)
429			}
430		case <-ctx.Done():
431			w.markDead()
432			unlock()
433			return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore}, ctx.Err()
434		}
435	
436		select {
437		case payload := <-respCh:
438			var resp frameResponse
439			if err := json.Unmarshal(payload, &resp); err != nil {
440				w.markDead()
441				unlock()
442				return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore},
443					fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid response frame: %v", ErrWorkerExited, err)
444			}
445			if resp.Type == "error" {
446				if resp.Fatal {
447					w.markDead()
448					unlock()
449					return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore},
450						fmt.Errorf("%w: adapter fatal: %s", ErrWorkerExited, resp.Message)
451				}
452				// Non-fatal adapter error: handler threw but VM is healthy. Do
453				// NOT mark dead; do NOT classify as ErrWorkerExited.
454				unlock()
455				return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore},
456					fmt.Errorf("adapter: %s", resp.Message)
457			}
458			if resp.Type == "response" {
459				// Non-streaming back-compat path: full response in one frame.
460				w.Served.Add(1)
461				unlock()
462				return &DispatchResult{
463					Streaming:  false,
464					StatusCode: resp.StatusCode,
465					Headers:    resp.Headers,
466					Body:       resp.Body,
467					w:          w,
468					errBefore:  errBefore,
469					finished:   true,
470				}, nil
471			}
472			if resp.Type == "response_start" {
473				// Streaming: keep the lock — the caller drives NextFrame and
474				// unlocks via the wrapper below when finished.
475				r := &DispatchResult{
476					Streaming:  true,
477					StatusCode: resp.StatusCode,
478					Headers:    resp.Headers,
479					w:          w,
480					errBefore:  errBefore,
481				}
482				// Wrap NextFrame so the worker unlocks on terminal kinds. We
483				// achieve this by replacing the helper closure ... but Go
484				// doesn't let us mutate a method, so instead we install the
485				// unlock as a finalizer triggered on every NextFrame return
486				// path that flips finished=true OR sets readErr.
487				//
488				// Simpler: use a tiny goroutine-free finishHook that the
489				// NextFrame body checks. We attach via a new field.
490				r.finishHook = unlock
491				return r, nil
492			}
493			w.markDead()
494			unlock()
495			return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore},
496				fmt.Errorf("%w: unexpected frame type %q", ErrWorkerExited, resp.Type)
497		case err := <-readErrCh:
498			w.markDead()
499			unlock()
500			return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore},
501				fmt.Errorf("%w: read frame: %v", ErrWorkerExited, err)
502		case <-ctx.Done():
503			w.markDead()
504			unlock()
505			return &DispatchResult{w: w, errBefore: errBefore}, ctx.Err()
506		}
507	}
508	
509	// Quit sends a clean shutdown frame, waits grace, then SIGTERMs, then SIGKILLs.
510	//
511	// All synchronization with the underlying process happens via w.waitDone,
512	// which the single Wait() goroutine launched in Spawn closes once the PID
513	// has been reaped. Quit MUST NOT call cmd.Wait() itself — doing so races
514	// with the Spawn-side Wait and yields "Wait was already called" errors,
515	// which would silently leave nsjail unreaped.
516	func (w *Worker) Quit(grace time.Duration) error {
517		if w.dead.Load() {
518			return w.Kill()
519		}
520		quitFrame, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"type": "quit"})
521		_ = writeFrame(w.stdin, quitFrame)
522		_ = w.stdin.Close()
523	
524		select {
525		case <-w.waitDone:
526			w.markDead()
527			return nil
528		case <-time.After(grace):
529		}
530	
531		// Grace expired — escalate.
532		if w.Cmd.Process != nil {
533			_ = w.Cmd.Process.Signal(syscall.SIGTERM)
534		}
535		select {
536		case <-w.waitDone:
537		case <-time.After(grace):
538			_ = w.Kill()
539			// Wait briefly for the Spawn-side reaper to finish so the caller
540			// returning from Quit can rely on the process being gone. Bounded
541			// so a wedged kernel can't hang shutdown forever.
542			select {
543			case <-w.waitDone:
544			case <-time.After(grace):
545			}
546		}
547		w.markDead()
548		return nil
549	}
550	
551	// Kill is an immediate SIGKILL of the worker's process group.
552	//
553	// Reaping is owned by the single Wait() goroutine launched in Spawn — we
554	// must NOT call cmd.Wait() here. Calling Wait() twice on the same
555	// *exec.Cmd is a documented race that can leave nsjail unreaped (the
556	// loser sees "Wait was already called" and returns without reaping).
557	// Pre-fix this was the path that produced <defunct> nsjail entries after
558	// streaming-client disconnects: markDead → pool kill → duplicate Wait.
559	func (w *Worker) Kill() error {
560		w.markDead()
561		if w.Cmd == nil || w.Cmd.Process == nil {
562			return nil
563		}
564		// Signal the whole process group (Setpgid=true at Spawn).
565		_ = syscall.Kill(-w.Cmd.Process.Pid, syscall.SIGKILL)
566		_ = w.Cmd.Process.Kill()
567		// The Spawn-side reaper goroutine will pick up the SIGKILL exit and
568		// close waitDone. Caller does not block on it — w.Kill returns as soon
569		// as the signal is delivered.
570		return nil
571	}
572	
573	// IsDead reports whether the worker has been marked unusable.
574	func (w *Worker) IsDead() bool { return w.dead.Load() }
575	
576	// GetCgroupPath returns the resolved cgroup path (thread-safe).
577	func (w *Worker) GetCgroupPath() string {
578		w.cgroupPathMu.Lock()
579		defer w.cgroupPathMu.Unlock()
580		return w.CgroupPath
581	}
582	
583	// IsExpired reports whether the worker should be retired based on age or
584	// use count. Either zero disables that check.
585	func (w *Worker) IsExpired(ttl time.Duration, maxUses int64) bool {
586		if ttl > 0 && time.Since(w.Spawned) > ttl {
587			return true
588		}
589		if maxUses > 0 && w.Served.Load() >= maxUses {
590			return true
591		}
592		return false
593	}
594	
595	func (w *Worker) markDead() {
596		w.dead.Store(true)
597		// Close stdin so a blocked read on the adapter side unblocks and exits.
598		_ = w.stdin.Close()
599	}
600	
601	// ── Framing helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
602	
603	func writeFrame(w io.Writer, payload []byte) error {
604		var hdr [4]byte
605		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[:], uint32(len(payload)))
606		if _, err := w.Write(hdr[:]); err != nil {
607			return err
608		}
609		if _, err := w.Write(payload); err != nil {
610			return err
611		}
612		return nil
613	}
614	
615	func readFrame(r io.Reader) ([]byte, error) {
616		var hdr [4]byte
617		if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, hdr[:]); err != nil {
618			return nil, err
619		}
620		n := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(hdr[:])
621		if n == 0 {
622			return []byte("{}"), nil
623		}
624		if n > 64*1024*1024 { // sanity cap — 64 MB per frame
625			return nil, fmt.Errorf("frame too large: %d bytes", n)
626		}
627		buf := make([]byte, n)
628		if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf); err != nil {
629			return nil, err
630		}
631		return buf, nil
632	}
633	
634	// ── Stderr ring buffer ────────────────────────────────────────────────
635	
636	// ringBuffer is a fixed-size, write-only ring used to capture the last N
637	// bytes of stderr per worker. Reads are via Snapshot(from).
638	type ringBuffer struct {
639		mu      sync.Mutex
640		buf     []byte
641		size    int
642		written int64 // total bytes ever written
643	}
644	
645	func newRingBuffer(size int) *ringBuffer {
646		return &ringBuffer{buf: make([]byte, size), size: size}
647	}
648	
649	func (r *ringBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
650		r.mu.Lock()
651		defer r.mu.Unlock()
652		for _, b := range p {
653			r.buf[int(r.written)%r.size] = b
654			r.written++
655		}
656		return len(p), nil
657	}
658	
659	// Len returns the cumulative byte count (monotonically increasing).
660	func (r *ringBuffer) Len() int64 {
661		r.mu.Lock()
662		defer r.mu.Unlock()
663		return r.written
664	}
665	
666	// Snapshot returns the bytes written since the 'from' marker. If the
667	// buffer wrapped past that point, the oldest overwritten bytes are lost.
668	func (r *ringBuffer) Snapshot(from int64) []byte {
669		r.mu.Lock()
670		defer r.mu.Unlock()
671		if r.written <= from {
672			return nil
673		}
674		want := int(r.written - from)
675		if want > r.size {
676			want = r.size
677		}
678		start := int(r.written-int64(want)) % r.size
679		out := make([]byte, want)
680		if start+want <= r.size {
681			copy(out, r.buf[start:start+want])
682		} else {
683			n := copy(out, r.buf[start:])
684			copy(out[n:], r.buf[:want-n])
685		}
686		return out
687	}
