478		// Both URLs return the same RFC 8414 document; the OIDC variant
479		// adds subject_types_supported / id_token_signing_alg_values_supported
480		// so ChatGPT's discovery probe validates without a fallback round-trip.
481		r.mux.HandleFunc("GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server", handlers.OAuthAuthServerMetadataHandler)
482		r.mux.HandleFunc("GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp", handlers.OAuthAuthServerMetadataHandler)
483		r.mux.HandleFunc("GET /.well-known/openid-configuration", handlers.OpenIDConfigurationHandler)
484		r.mux.HandleFunc("GET /.well-known/openid-configuration/mcp", handlers.OpenIDConfigurationHandler)
485		// OAuth 2.1 endpoints — DCR (RFC 7591), authorize (consent SSR),
486		// token (authorization_code + refresh_token grants), revoke (RFC 7009).
487		// Lets claude.ai / ChatGPT add /mcp as a custom channel via OAuth
488		// without the operator pasting a bearer token.
489		oauthHandler := &oauth.Handler{
490			DB:            r.db,
491			SecureCookies: r.cfg.Security.SecureCookies,
492		}
493		r.mux.HandleFunc("POST /register", oauthHandler.Register)
494		r.mux.HandleFunc("GET /oauth/authorize", oauthHandler.AuthorizeGET)
495		r.mux.HandleFunc("POST /oauth/authorize", oauthHandler.AuthorizePOST)
496		r.mux.HandleFunc("POST /oauth/token", oauthHandler.Token)
497		r.mux.HandleFunc("POST /oauth/revoke", oauthHandler.Revoke)
498	
499		// UI routes — serve the Vue SPA at /web/. No credentials are injected;
500		// the UI uses /auth/onboard + /auth/login to establish a session.
501		r.mux.Handle("/web/", uiHandler())
502		r.mux.HandleFunc("GET /{$}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
503			http.Redirect(w, req, "/web/", http.StatusFound)
504		})
505	
506		// Catch-all for user-defined custom routes. Go's ServeMux sends any
507		// path that doesn't match a more specific pattern to "/", so we use
508		// this handler to look up /webhooks/stripe-style routes (exact or
509		// /prefix/*) in the `routes` table and dispatch to the invoke handler.
510		r.mux.HandleFunc("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
511			if isReservedPath(req.URL.Path) {
512				http.NotFound(w, req)
513				return
514			}
515			route, _, err := r.db.MatchRoute(req.URL.Path)
516			if err != nil || route == nil {
517				http.NotFound(w, req)
518				return
519			}
520			invokeHandler.ServeHTTP(w, req)
521		})
522	}

524	// buildMiddlewareChain builds the full middleware chain:
525	// CORS -> BodySize -> Auth -> RequestID -> Logger -> Handler
526	func (r *Router) buildMiddlewareChain() {
527		maxBody := r.cfg.Server.MaxBodyBytes
528		if maxBody <= 0 {
529			maxBody = 6 * 1024 * 1024 // 6MB default
530		}
531	
532		origins := r.cfg.Security.CORSOrigins
533		if len(origins) == 0 {
534			origins = []string{"*"}
535		}
536	
537		// Build chain from inside out: Handler -> Logger -> RequestID -> Auth -> BodySize -> CORS
538		chain := loggerMiddleware(r.db, r.eventHub, r.mux)
539		chain = requestIDMiddleware(chain)
540		chain = authMiddleware(r.db, &r.keyCache, chain)
541		chain = bodySizeMiddleware(maxBody, chain)
542		chain = corsMiddleware(origins, chain)
543	
544		r.handler = chain
545	}

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"net/http"
6		"os"
7		"strings"
8		"sync"
9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/database"
12		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/internal/ids"
13		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/metrics"
14		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/proxy"
15		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/registry"
16		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/sandbox"
17		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/secrets"
18		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/server/handlers/respond"
19		"github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva/backend/internal/trace"
20	)
21	
22	// InvokeHandler handles function invocation requests.
23	type InvokeHandler struct {
24		Registry       *registry.Registry
25		Proxy          *proxy.Proxy
26		DB             *database.Database
27		Metrics        *metrics.Metrics
28		Secrets        *secrets.Manager
29		DataDir        string
30		DefaultSeccomp string // Global default seccomp policy name
31	
32		// PublishEvent is fired after every invocation so the SSE event hub can
33		// stream execution rows to live UI clients (Dashboard recent invocations
34		// + InvocationsLog). Best-effort; non-blocking. Wired in server.New from
35		// events.Hub.Publish.
36		PublishEvent func(eventType string, data any)
37	
38		// rateLimiter is initialized lazily on first request so existing tests
39		// that build the handler with zero-value fields keep working. Keyed by
40		// (fn_id, client_ip).
41		rateLimiterOnce sync.Once
42		rateLimiter     *rateLimiter
43	}
44	
45	// ServeHTTP is the hot path for function invocation. It accepts two path
46	// shapes:
47	//   - /fn/{id}/... — direct invoke (id is the short form without "fn_" prefix)
48	//   - any custom route previously registered via /api/v1/routes that maps
49	//     a user-chosen path (e.g. /webhooks/stripe) to a function_id
50	func (h *InvokeHandler) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
51		reqID := r.Header.Get("X-Request-ID")
52	
53		var fnID string
54		// Prefix we should strip from the incoming request path before handing
55		// it to the sandboxed function. For /fn/{id} this is handled inside
56		// proxy.Forward; for custom routes we compute the strip here based on
57		// whether the match was exact or a `/prefix/*` match.
58		var stripPrefix string
59	
60		// Check custom routes first. MatchRoute tries exact match, then the
61		// longest `/prefix/*` match.
62		if route, matched, err := h.DB.MatchRoute(r.URL.Path); err == nil && route != nil {
63			if route.Methods != "*" && route.Methods != "" {
64				allowed := false
65				for _, m := range strings.Split(route.Methods, ",") {
66					if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(m), r.Method) {
67						allowed = true
68						break
69					}
70				}
71				if !allowed {
72					respond.Error(w, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED",
73						"method not allowed for this route", reqID)
74					return
75				}
76			}
77			fnID = route.FunctionID
78			// For exact-match routes the function sees "/" as its path. For
79			// prefix routes it sees the sub-path after the prefix so its
80			// internal router (FastAPI/Express/etc.) can dispatch.
81			if strings.HasSuffix(route.Path, "/*") {
82				stripPrefix = matched // e.g. "/shortener/"
83			} else {
84				stripPrefix = matched // full path → function sees "/"
85			}
86		} else {
87			// Fall back to /fn/{id} extraction.
88			fnID = extractFnID(r.URL.Path)
89		}
90	
91		if fnID == "" {
92			respond.Error(w, http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", "no function for this path", reqID)
93			return
94		}
95	
96		// Registry lookup.
97		fn, err := h.Registry.Get(fnID)
98		if err != nil {
99			respond.Error(w, http.StatusNotFound, "NOT_FOUND", "function not found", reqID)
100			return
101		}
102	
103		// Status gate:
104		// - "active": proceed normally.
105		// - "building" AND a prior code directory exists: serve with the old
106		//   code (zero-downtime redeploy). This is the Heroku/Vercel model.
107		// - "building" with no prior code, or any other non-active status:
108		//   respond 503 with Retry-After so clients can poll.
109		if fn.Status != "active" {
110			if fn.Status == "building" && hasPriorCode(h.DataDir, fn.ID) {
111				// Fall through — the warm pool still has workers bound to the
112				// old code dir. Fresh deploys won't hit this branch because
113				// there's no prior code yet.
114			} else {
115				status := http.StatusConflict
116				code := "NOT_ACTIVE"
117				msg := fmt.Sprintf("function status is %q, must be active", fn.Status)
118				if fn.Status == "building" {
119					status = http.StatusServiceUnavailable
120					code = "BUILDING"
121					msg = "deployment in progress"
122					w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "5")
123				}
124				respond.Error(w, status, code, msg, reqID)
125				return
126			}
127		}
128	
129		// Per-function auth gate. auth_mode='none' (default) is a no-op and
130		// keeps the public-by-default contract; 'platform_key' and 'signed' are
131		// opt-in. authorizeInvoke writes the error response itself on failure.
132		if code := h.authorizeInvoke(w, r, fn); code != "" {
133			return
134		}
135	
136		// Per-function rate limit. perMin == 0 short-circuits inside Allow.
137		if fn.RateLimitPerMin > 0 {
138			h.rateLimiterOnce.Do(func() { h.rateLimiter = newRateLimiter() })
139			if !h.rateLimiter.Allow(fn.ID, clientIP(r), fn.RateLimitPerMin) {
140				w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "60")
141				respond.Error(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "RATE_LIMITED",
142					fmt.Sprintf("rate limit exceeded (%d req/min per IP)", fn.RateLimitPerMin), reqID)
143				return
144			}
145		}
146	
147		// Generate execution ID — UUIDv7 so executions sort by creation
148		// time naturally (the highest-volume table benefits most from
149		// time-clustered B-tree inserts).
150		execID := ids.New()
151	
152		// HTTP-rooted span. Trace ID was set by requestIDMiddleware; we add
153		// the span ID for this execution and stamp the trigger label.
154		traceID := trace.TraceID(r.Context())
155		parentSpan := trace.ParentSpanID(r.Context()) // empty for true HTTP roots; non-empty if an external W3C parent was honored
156		spanID := trace.NewSpanID()
157		traceCtx := trace.WithSpanID(r.Context(), spanID)
158		traceCtx = trace.WithTrigger(traceCtx, "http")
159		r = r.WithContext(traceCtx)
160	
161		// Track active requests.
162		h.Metrics.ActiveRequests.Add(1)
163		defer h.Metrics.ActiveRequests.Add(-1)
164	
165		start := time.Now()
166	
167		// Set context timeout from function config.
168		timeoutMS := fn.TimeoutMS
169		if timeoutMS <= 0 {
170			timeoutMS = 30000
171		}
172	
173		// Resolve the code directory for this function.
174		// The deploy handler stores code at DataDir/functions/<fn_id>/code/
175		codeDir := h.DataDir + "/functions/" + fn.ID + "/code"
176	
177		// Determine language.
178		lang := sandbox.Language(fn.Runtime)
179	
180		// Build seccomp policy for this function.
181		seccompPolicy := sandbox.BuildSeccompPolicy(h.DefaultSeccomp, nil, nil)
182	
183		// Build env: function's env_vars plus decrypted secrets. Secrets win on
184		// key collision (so an operator can override a public env var).
185		env := map[string]string{}

295			"function_id":   fn.ID,

299			"duration_ms":   durationMS,

301			"cold_start":    coldStart,
302			"started_at":    now.Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
303			"finished_at":   now.Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
304		})
305	}
306	
307	// hasPriorCode returns true if the function has a built code directory from
308	// a previous successful deploy. Used during redeploys so live traffic keeps
309	// hitting the old code until the new build succeeds.
310	func hasPriorCode(dataDir, fnID string) bool {
311		if dataDir == "" {
312			return false
313		}
314		st, err := os.Stat(dataDir + "/functions/" + fnID + "/code")
315		return err == nil && st.IsDir()
316	}
317	
318	// extractFnID pulls the function ID from paths like /fn/{id} or
319	// /fn/{id}/sub/path. With UUIDv7 IDs, the URL form and the DB form are
320	// identical — no prefix-stripping or re-adding.
321	func extractFnID(path string) string {
322		const prefix = "/fn/"
323		if !strings.HasPrefix(path, prefix) {
324			return ""
325		}
326		remainder := strings.TrimPrefix(path, prefix)
327		if idx := strings.Index(remainder, "/"); idx >= 0 {
328			return remainder[:idx]
329		}
330		return remainder
331	}

    10	// at `versions/<codeHash>`. The two-step symlink + rename pattern avoids
    11	// the empty-window that os.RemoveAll(current) + os.Symlink would create:
    12	// rename(2) on a symlink is atomic on Linux ext4/xfs.
    13	//
    14	// The link target is a relative path ("versions/<hash>") so the same
    15	// symlink resolves correctly if the data directory is moved or if the
    16	// container's mountpoint changes. nsjail does not deref symlinks at the
    17	// bind-mount source — `-R cfg.CodeDir:/code` binds the symlink path
    18	// itself — but the spawn closure resolves the link fresh on each Spawn,
    19	// so RefreshForDeploy draining workers is sufficient for the next spawn
    20	// to pick up the new target.
    21	func ActivateVersion(dataDir, fnID, codeHash string) error {
    22		if codeHash == "" {
    23			return fmt.Errorf("activate: empty code hash")
    24		}
    25		// codeHash becomes part of a filesystem path (versions/<hash>); it is
    26		// always a sha256 hex digest. Reject anything else defensively so a
    27		// traversal value can never reach the symlink target.
    28		if !isHexHash(codeHash) {
    29			return fmt.Errorf("activate: invalid code hash %q", codeHash)
    30		}
    31		fnDir := filepath.Join(dataDir, "functions", fnID)
    32		target := filepath.Join("versions", codeHash) // relative; see comment above
    33	
    34		tmp := filepath.Join(fnDir, "current.tmp."+randSuffix())
    35		if err := os.Symlink(target, tmp); err != nil {
    36			return fmt.Errorf("activate: symlink: %w", err)
    37		}
    38		current := filepath.Join(fnDir, "current")
    39		if err := os.Rename(tmp, current); err != nil {
    40			// Best-effort cleanup of the tmp link so we don't leave debris.
    41			_ = os.Remove(tmp)
    42			return fmt.Errorf("activate: atomic rename: %w", err)
    43		}
    44		return nil
    45	}
    46	
    47	// isHexHash reports whether s is a 64-char lowercase-hex sha256 digest.
    48	func isHexHash(s string) bool {
    49		if len(s) != 64 {
    50			return false
    51		}
    52		for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
    53			c := s[i]
    54			if !((c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f')) {
    55				return false
    56			}

    58		return true
    59	}

    62	// the hash it points at, or "" if the symlink is missing or malformed.
    63	// Used by GC to know which version not to delete.
    64	func ResolveActiveHash(dataDir, fnID string) string {

    73		}
    74		return hash

set -e
IMAGE_ROOTFS=/opt/orva/rootfs
VOLUME_ROOTFS=/var/lib/orva/rootfs
RUNTIMES="node python"
for rt in $RUNTIMES; do
  if [ ! -d "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/usr" ]; then
    echo ">> seeding $VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt from image"
    mkdir -p "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt"
    cp -a "$IMAGE_ROOTFS/$rt/." "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/"
  fi
done
rt=node
mkdir -p "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva"
cp "$IMAGE_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/adapter.js" "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/adapter.js"
if [ -d "$IMAGE_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/node_modules/orva" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/node_modules/orva"
  cp -a "$IMAGE_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/node_modules/orva/." "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/node_modules/orva/"
fi
rt=python
mkdir -p "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva"
cp "$IMAGE_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/adapter.py" "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/adapter.py"
if [ -f "$IMAGE_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/orva.py" ]; then
  cp "$IMAGE_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/orva.py" "$VOLUME_ROOTFS/$rt/opt/orva/orva.py"
fi
mkdir -p /var/lib/orva/functions
if [ ! -e /dev/net/tun ]; then
  mkdir -p /dev/net 2>/dev/null || true
  if mknod /dev/net/tun c 10 200 2>/dev/null; then
    chmod 0666 /dev/net/tun
    echo ">> created /dev/net/tun for egress sandboxes"
  else
    echo ">> WARN: could not create /dev/net/tun — egress functions will fail to spawn"
    echo "         (re-run docker with --device /dev/net/tun if you need egress)"
  fi
fi
touch /var/lib/orva/.setup-complete
setup_nsjail_cgroups() {
  ORVA_CG=/sys/fs/cgroup/orva-sandboxes
  if ! mkdir -p "$ORVA_CG" 2>/dev/null || [ ! -f "$ORVA_CG/cgroup.procs" ]; then
    echo ">> WARN: cannot create cgroup at $ORVA_CG — nsjail CPU/memory limits disabled"
    echo "         (requires cgroup: host and - /sys/fs/cgroup:/sys/fs/cgroup:rw)"
    return
  fi
  if echo "+memory +cpu +pids" > "$ORVA_CG/cgroup.subtree_control" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo ">> nsjail cgroup delegation ready: $ORVA_CG"
    export ORVA_CGROUPV2_MOUNT="$ORVA_CG"
  else
    echo ">> WARN: $ORVA_CG/cgroup.subtree_control write failed — cgroup limits disabled"
    rmdir "$ORVA_CG" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
}
setup_nsjail_cgroups || true
write_cli_config() (
    keyfile=/var/lib/orva/.admin-key
    cfg_dir=/root/.orva
    cfg_path="$cfg_dir/config.yaml"
    i=0
    while [ ! -s "$keyfile" ] && [ "$i" -lt 60 ]; do
        sleep 1
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    [ -s "$keyfile" ] || { echo ">> WARN: bootstrap key not seen within 60s; CLI config not written" >&2; return; }
    api_key=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$keyfile")
    [ -n "$api_key" ] || return
    mkdir -p "$cfg_dir"
    chmod 700 "$cfg_dir"
    umask 077
    cat > "$cfg_path" <<EOF
endpoint: http://localhost:8443
api_key: $api_key

# Security model

This document explains how Orva isolates user-supplied code from the host
and from other functions. It is descriptive, not prescriptive — every
claim below is grounded in a specific file/line that you can audit.

## Threat model

Orva is **single-tenant**: one operator, many functions, possibly many
end-users hitting those functions. The platform's security goals,
ordered by importance:

1. A function cannot read or write **another function's data**
2. A function cannot read or write the **host filesystem** outside its
   own `/code` mount and its private `/tmp`
3. A function cannot **escalate to host root**, even though it appears to
   run as UID 0 inside its sandbox (more on this below)
4. A function cannot **exhaust host resources** beyond its declared
   memory / CPU / pid limits
5. A function cannot make **arbitrary network calls** when network mode
   is `none` (default — isolated net namespace, loopback only). Functions
   that need outbound HTTPS opt in by setting `network_mode: egress`

Orva is **not** designed to defend against:
- A malicious operator running on the same host (they own the keys)
- A kernel-level zero-day (no seccomp filter is bulletproof against
  kernel exploits — see `nsjail` upstream's stance)
- Side-channel attacks (Spectre / Rowhammer / cache timing) — these are
  out of scope for any container-grade isolation

## What's between user code and the host

```
host kernel
  └─ docker container "orva"             ← UID 0 inside container; needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN
      └─ orvad (Go server)                  to construct sandboxes
          └─ nsjail process                ← unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) drops effective caps
              └─ user namespace
                  ├─ chroot to runtime rootfs (read-only)
                  ├─ /code bind-mount     ← read-only, function-private
                  ├─ tmpfs /tmp           ← private, wiped on worker exit
                  ├─ cgroup v2: memory + CPU + pids
                  ├─ seccomp filter       ← ~150 syscalls blocked
                  └─ user code (node / python)
```

The gap between layers is enforced by the Linux kernel, not by Orva
code. Orva configures the boundaries and trusts the kernel to keep
them.

## What "running as root inside the sandbox" actually means

User code sees `getuid() == 0`. **It is NOT root on the host.**

The mechanism is `CLONE_NEWUSER` + UID mapping. nsjail's `-Mo` flag
(`internal/sandbox/sandbox.go:154`) creates a new user namespace where
inside-UID 0 is mapped to host-UID 65534 (`nobody`). All capability
checks happen against the user-namespace's UID, but actions that cross
the namespace boundary (writing to a file owned by host-root,
mounting a filesystem outside the chroot, sending a signal to a host
PID) are denied because the function has zero effective capabilities
**outside** its namespace.

Verify it yourself:

```bash
# Deploy a fn that introspects /proc/self/status
KEY=$(docker exec orva cat /var/lib/orva/.admin-key)

curl -X POST -H "X-Orva-API-Key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  http://localhost:8443/api/v1/functions \
  -d '{"name":"whoami","runtime":"node","memory_mb":128,"cpus":1}'

FID=$(curl -s -H "X-Orva-API-Key: $KEY" http://localhost:8443/api/v1/functions \
  | jq -r '.functions[] | select(.name=="whoami") | .id')

curl -X POST -H "X-Orva-API-Key: $KEY" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  http://localhost:8443/api/v1/functions/$FID/deploy-inline \
  -d '{"code":"const fs=require(\"fs\");module.exports=async()=>{return fs.readFileSync(\"/proc/self/status\",\"utf8\").split(\"\\n\").filter(l=>l.startsWith(\"Cap\")||l.startsWith(\"Uid\"));}"}'

curl -X POST -H "X-Orva-API-Key: $KEY" \
  http://localhost:8443/fn/${FID} -d '{}'
```

Expected output (the meaningful lines):

```
Uid: 0  0  0  0
Gid: 0  0  0  0
CapInh: 0000000000000000      ← 0: no inheritable caps
CapPrm: 0000000000000000      ← 0: no permitted caps
CapEff: 0000000000000000      ← 0: no effective caps
CapBnd: 0000000000000000      ← 0: nothing in the bounding set
CapAmb: 0000000000000000      ← 0: nothing ambient
```

UID 0 with **all 64 capability bits cleared**. The function can do
nothing root-on-the-host could do.

## Filesystem isolation

Configured at `internal/sandbox/sandbox.go:154-160`:

```go
"-Mo",                          // mount mode: ownership-mapped userns
"--chroot", rootfs,             // pivot_root into the runtime's rootfs
"-R", cfg.CodeDir + ":/code",   // read-only bind mount of the function's code
"-T", "/tmp",                   // private tmpfs at /tmp
```

- The runtime rootfs (`/var/lib/orva/rootfs/<runtime>/`) is the only
  filesystem visible. It contains the language runtime + standard libs.
- `/code` is a read-only bind mount of the function's code directory
  (`<dataDir>/functions/<id>/current` → symlink to `versions/<hash>/`).
  Read-only means the function cannot write back to its own code dir,
  which prevents persistent compromise of the deployment artifact.
- `/tmp` is a fresh tmpfs per spawn — wiped when the worker exits or is
  reaped. Functions can write here freely; nothing escapes.
- No other host paths are visible. The procfs, sysfs, and cgroup
  filesystems are masked by the chroot.

The 10 subsystem readers are still running (this box has 2 cores, so the fan-out is serialized 2-at-a-time). Here's my first pass from reading the code directly — I'll follow with the deep per-subsystem map when the fan-out lands.

---

# Orva — what it is

A **self-hosted Function-as-a-Service platform** for homelabs and on-prem boxes. You write a JavaScript/TypeScript/Python function, hit deploy, and Orva runs it in an nsjail sandbox behind an HTTP endpoint. It's the Lambda/Cloudflare-Workers loop on hardware you own — no cloud account, no per-invocation billing.

- **Apache-2.0**, ~195 commits since 2026-04-28, two contributors (Harsh-2002 + Anurag Vishwakarma), latest tag `v2026.08.05`.
- Self-described as **not production-ready for customer-facing work** — homelab/side-project/internal-tools grade.
- Target user is documented explicitly in `PRODUCT.md`: *one* technical operator, single host, dark-only dashboard, "operator-grade, calm, technical." No multi-tenancy, by design.

The thing that makes it unusual for a hobby FaaS: it ships a **72-tool MCP server** and an **in-product agentic AI assistant** that can operate the whole instance.

---

## Repo shape

Single Go module (`github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva`) rooted at the repo, not at `backend/`:

| Path | What | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `backend/` | Go server — 221 `.go` files, all subsystems | 276 files |
| `cli/` | Slim standalone CLI (`cli/commands/` is the **single source of truth** for subcommands; the server imports it) | 39 files |
| `internal/` | Shared by both binaries: `ids/` (UUIDv7), `client/` (HTTP + `~/.orva/config.yaml`) | 4 files |
| `frontend/` | Vue 3 + Vite + Pinia + Tailwind v4 + CodeMirror 6 dashboard | 97 files |
| `docs/` | 16 reference docs, `reference.md` is canonical | 27 files |
| `test/` | Shell suites + a Python e2e harness (`test/e2e/run.py`, 22 test modules) | 81 files |
| `scripts/` | `install.sh` (1085 lines), `install-cli.{sh,ps1}`, `entrypoint.sh`, `build-rootfs.sh` | 6 files |

**Server and CLI are the same program.** `orva serve` is the daemon; every other subcommand is a client. `backend/cmd/orva/main.go` calls `commands.NewRoot()` then bolts on `serve`/`setup`/`init`. The slim CLI (`cli/cmd/orva`) imports only `cli/commands` — no server packages, no embedded UI — which is why it's ~9 MB vs ~70 MB.

---

## How an invocation actually works

I traced this through the real code rather than the docs:

```
HTTP  →  corsMiddleware → bodySize → auth → requestID → logger → mux
      →  InvokeHandler.ServeHTTP        (handlers/invoke.go)
         ├ MatchRoute() custom-route lookup, else /fn/{id}
         ├ Registry.Get(fnID)           in-memory, SQLite-backed
         ├ status gate / per-fn auth_mode / per-fn rate limit
         ├ trace span stamped (W3C traceparent honored)
         └ Proxy.Forward(...)
              └ pool.Acquire(fnID)      warm worker, or spawnFn()
                   └ sandbox.Spawn()    exec nsjail → chroot → adapter
      →  4-byte big-endian length prefix + JSON frame over the worker's stdin
      ←  "response" | "response_start" + "chunk"(base64) … + "response_end"
      →  AsyncInsertExecutionFinal()    batched writer, off the hot path
      →  eventHub.Publish("execution")  → SSE → dashboard live tiles
```

Details worth knowing:

- **The wire protocol is length-prefixed JSON over stdin/stdout**, not a socket or HTTP. `writeFrame`/`readFrame` in `sandbox/worker.go:603-632`, 64 MB frame cap.
- **Streaming** is a real feature: `DispatchEx` returns `Streaming:true` on a `response_start` frame and the caller pumps `NextFrame` until `end`. Body bytes are base64 so NULs survive the JSON transport.
- **nsjail argv** (`sandbox.go:176`): `-Mo --chroot <rootfs> -R <codeDir>:/code -T /tmp --rlimit_as max -Q`, plus `--use_cgroupv2` + `--cgroup_mem_max` (1.5× declared memory) + `--cgroup_pids_max` + `--cgroup_cpu_ms_per_sec` **only if** a writable cgroup v2 delegate exists. `--time_limit` is deliberately dropped — Go-side context timeouts give ms resolution.
- **Zombie-reaping is centralized**: exactly one `cmd.Wait()` goroutine per worker, started in `Spawn`, signalling via `waitDone`. `Quit`/`Kill` never call `Wait()`. This is a scar from a real v0.4 bug.
- **Egress is opt-in**: default is an isolated net namespace with loopback only. `network_mode: egress` adds nsjail `--user_net` plus bind-mounts of a firewall-managed `/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/hosts`.
- **Autoscaler is Knative-KPA-shaped**: 60s stable window + 6s panic window, 1s tick, `dynamicMax` bounded by CPU *and* a host memory budget (`hostmem.go` refuses spawns past ~80% reservation).

**Deploys are content-addressed.** `versions/<sha256>/` dirs are immutable; `current` is a symlink retargeted by an atomic `rename(2)` (`builder/activate.go`). Identical redeploy = cache hit via `.orva-ready`. Rollback = symlink retarget. GC = delete versions outside the keep window. `npm install`/`pip install`/`tsc` run **host-side**, not in the sandbox.

---

## GitHub Actions — six workflows

The policy is **"verify on push/PR, ship on tag."** The release pipeline runs *zero* tests.

**`ci.yml`** — PR + push-to-main gate, path-filtered so docs-only commits skip it entirely. Four parallel jobs: `lint` (owns *all* shellcheck for the repo — `dash -n` + `shellcheck -s sh` on the POSIX installers, `bash -n` + shellcheck on everything else), `go` (Go 1.26 on ubuntu-24.04: `make embed` + `make adapters-embed`, then `go vet`, `go test -race`, `go build`), `ui` (`npm ci` + `vite build`), `docker` (image smoke build, no push). No caches anywhere — deliberate, so a stale lockfile or toolchain artifact can't sneak through.

**`e2e.yml`** — push to `main`/`dev`, all PRs. Builds, boots `orva serve`, waits for `/api/v1/system/health`, then runs `test/e2e/run.py` against it with the bootstrap admin key from `$DATA_DIR/.admin-key`. Covers every domain plus the CLI plus the AI agentic loop **via a mock LLM** (`test/e2e/mock_llm.py`) — no provider key needed. Scenarios requiring real nsjail self-skip in CI.

**`release.yml`** — the interesting one. Triggers on `v*` tags.
- **`gate`** resolves the tag's SHA, then polls the Actions API for that exact commit: `e2e.yml` is a **hard** gate (must exist and be `success`), `ci.yml` is **soft** (path-filtered, so a docs-only commit may legitimately have no run). ~20-minute poll cap so tagging right after a merge doesn't race. Refuses to build on red or missing. `workflow_dispatch` + `force=true` bypasses it.
- Every build job `needs: gate`: `build-orva` (amd64/arm64), `build-cli` (6 targets incl. Windows `.exe`), `build-nsjail` (built **inside `debian:bookworm-slim`** on native runners — building on ubuntu-24.04 produced `GLIBC_2.38 not found` at the install target), `build-rootfs` (node/python × 2 arches, `docker export` + zstd -19).
- `release` collates, `sha256sum`s everything into `checksums.txt`, publishes the GitHub Release, attaches the installer scripts.
- `docker-image` builds per-arch on **native** runners (no QEMU), pushes **by digest only**; `docker-manifest` stitches the two digests into a multi-arch `:latest`. **There is intentionally no per-version image tag** — versioning lives in the GitHub Release.
- `cleanup-ghcr` prunes everything that isn't the live `:latest` tree, with a safety net that keeps all untagged versions (they're the per-arch sub-manifests).

**`install-e2e.yml`** — real install + smoke + uninstall in privileged systemd-in-docker across ubuntu24/debian12/alpine321/rocky9/fedora41/arch. `arch` and `alpine321` are `continue-on-error` (rolling mirrors / OpenRC reinstall race). A gVisor leg existed and was **removed 2026-05-13** — nsjail's nested-namespace `clone()` is rejected by gVisor's sentry.

**`cli-e2e.yml`** — Go unit tests + cross-compile matrix + a command-tree golden diff on PRs; the expensive macOS/Windows installer legs are gated behind `dorny/paths-filter` so they only fire when the installer scripts change, on release, on schedule, or on dispatch. Both `install-e2e` and `cli-e2e` run their install legs on `release: published` (not main-push) — during a release cut the old release is gone and the new one isn't up, so "latest" would 404.

**`cleanup-ghcr.yml`** — manual standalone prune, same logic as the release job.

**Build identity** is stamped via three `-X` ldflags (`version.Version/Commit/BuildTime`) that flow Makefile → Dockerfile → release.yml and surface at `/api/v1/system/health` and Settings → Build info. Go ignores unknown `-X` targets silently, so renaming that package must be done in lock-step across all three.

---

## Things I found that don't match the docs

1. **Redeploys are not zero-downtime, despite the code comment claiming the Heroku/Vercel model.** `invoke.go:110` gates the `building`-status passthrough on `hasPriorCode()`, which stats `<dataDir>/functions/<id>/code` — the **legacy** flat layout. `builder/migrate_fs.go` deletes that dir on upgrade and new deploys only ever create `versions/<hash>/` + `current`. So the branch is dead: a redeploy returns `503 BUILDING` + `Retry-After: 5` instead of serving old code.

2. **`invoke.go:175` computes a `codeDir` that is thrown away.** `proxy.go:191` is literally `_ = codeDir`; the real path comes from `pool.go:544` (`.../current`). Vestigial from the pre-warm-pool design.

3. **The MCP server has 72 tools, not 70.** `grep -c regAddTool` across `backend/internal/mcp/tools_*.go` = 72. README, `backend/CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` all say 70.

4. **`sandbox.go:58` documents `--use_pasta`; the code at line 197 emits `--user_net`.** Comment drift.

[CONFIRMED] AUTH BYPASS: middleware_auth.go:68 skips the entire API-key gate for ANY request whose X-Orva-Internal-Token header is merely non-empty; the value is never compared there, and JobsHandler.authorize returns true unconditionally.
    → backend/internal/server/middleware_auth.go:68 — `if r.Header.Get("X-Orva-Internal-Token") != "" {` then tags Actor{sdk,internal_token} and calls next.ServeHTTP with no comparison against Router.internalToken. Line number is exact. backend/internal/server/handlers/jobs.go:28-40 — authorize() does a ConstantTimeCompare, and if it fails falls through to a bare `return true` with a comment asserting the middleware already authorized. Combined with backend/internal/server/ai_handler.go:50-52 (`// session / internal operator → full access`, p.Perms = {read,write,invoke,admin} for any non-api_key actor), the whole AI tool surface is reachable with a bogus header value.

[CONFIRMED] Seccomp is audit-only: BuildSeccompPolicy (seccomp.go:136) emits `... USE orva DEFAULT LOG` (seccomp.go:191), and --seccomp_log is never passed despite the comment.
    → backend/internal/sandbox/seccomp.go:136 `func BuildSeccompPolicy(base string, allow, block []string) string`; seccomp.go:191 `b.WriteString(" } } USE orva DEFAULT LOG")`. The comment at seccomp.go:185-187 explicitly says "nsjail's seccomp_log flag combined with this policy" but backend/internal/sandbox/sandbox.go:251-253 appends only `--seccomp_string`; `--seccomp_log` appears nowhere in buildArgs (full function read, lines 165-280).

[CONFIRMED] Seccomp is global, not per-function: pool.go:612 calls BuildSeccompPolicy(tmpl.DefaultSeccomp, nil, nil), and proxy.Forward discards its seccompPolicy argument at proxy.go:193.
    → backend/internal/pool/pool.go:612 `SeccompPolicy:  sandbox.BuildSeccompPolicy(tmpl.DefaultSeccomp, nil, nil),` inside spawnFn. backend/internal/proxy/proxy.go:186 declares `seccompPolicy string` and proxy.go:193 is literally `_ = seccompPolicy` (alongside `_ = codeDir`, `_ = cpus`, `_ = coldStart` at 192-194). backend/internal/mcp/tools_invoke.go:458 `seccompPolicy := sandbox.BuildSeccompPolicy("", nil, nil)` — line number exact, and harmless only because of the discard.

125	• HEALTH CHECK IS A LIVENESS STUB THAT CANNOT FAIL — the single biggest observability gap nobody named. backend/internal/server/handlers/system.go:106-143: Health() builds a literal map with `"status": "healthy"` (line 123) and `"database": {"status": "ok"}` as hardcoded strings. It never pings the DB (no Ping, no SELECT), never stats the nsjail binary or the rootfs dirs, never consults the pool or the firewall's lastError. It returns 200 unconditionally as long as the goroutine is scheduled. Everything downstream keys off it: the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK, scripts/install.sh's wait_for_health, test/e2e/env.py's wait_healthy, e2e.yml's 30s readiness poll, and detectInternalAPIBase's probe loop (server.go:438-449). A box with a corrupt/locked orva.db, a missing /usr/local/bin/nsjail, or an unmounted rootfs volume reports healthy and Docker keeps it in rotation — every invocation 503s while the orchestrator sees green. There is no /readyz vs /livez split and no degraded state anywhere in the codebase.

127	• GRACEFUL SHUTDOWN IS BROKEN BY ITS OWN SSE STREAMS. Server.Shutdown (backend/internal/server/server.go:514-539) calls httpServer.Shutdown(30s ctx) FIRST, and http.Server.Shutdown waits for active connections to go idle. An SSE stream never goes idle — events/handler.go:32 deliberately clears the write deadline and the loop only exits on r.Context().Done() (which Shutdown does not fire) or on a hub-closed channel. events/hub.go has NO Close method at all (only funcs: NewHub, subscribe, unsubscribe, Publish, SubscriberCount; the sole close(s.ch) at hub.go:74 is inside unsubscribe, called only by the handler's own defer). So handler.go:69's `return // hub closed our channel (server shutting down)` is dead code. Consequence: one open dashboard tab, one `orva activity -f`, or one `orva logs -f` makes every SIGTERM block the full 30 seconds, then Shutdown returns DeadlineExceeded (logged as a warn at server.go:518-520) and the process proceeds to tear down the pool and Bifrost while streams are still writing. Under Docker's default 10s stop-timeout that is a SIGKILL every single restart, and the AI Manager's Close (server.go:535-537) and Scheduler.Stop never run.

It never pings the DB (no Ping, no SELECT), never stats the nsjail binary or the rootfs dirs, never consults the pool or the firewall's lastError. It returns 200 unconditionally as long as the goroutine is scheduled. Everything downstream keys off it: the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK, scripts/install.sh's wait_for_health, test/e2e/env.py's wait_healthy, e2e.yml's 30s readiness poll, and detectInternalAPIBase's probe loop (server.go:438-449). A box with a corrupt/locked orva.db, a missing /usr/local/bin/nsjail, or an unmounted rootfs volume reports healthy and Docker keeps it in rotation — every invocation 503s while the orchestrator sees green. There is no /readyz vs /livez split and no degraded state anywhere in the codebase.

An SSE stream never goes idle — events/handler.go:32 deliberately clears the write deadline and the loop only exits on r.Context().Done() (which Shutdown does not fire) or on a hub-closed channel. events/hub.go has NO Close method at all (only funcs: NewHub, subscribe, unsubscribe, Publish, SubscriberCount; the sole close(s.ch) at hub.go:74 is inside unsubscribe, called only by the handler's own defer). So handler.go:69's `return // hub closed our channel (server shutting down)` is dead code. Consequence: one open dashboard tab, one `orva activity -f`, or one `orva logs -f` makes every SIGTERM block the full 30 seconds, then Shutdown returns DeadlineExceeded (logged as a warn at server.go:518-520) and the process proceeds to tear down the pool and Bifrost while streams are still writing. Under Docker's default 10s stop-timeout that is a SIGKILL every single restart, and the AI Manager's Close (server.go:535-537) and Scheduler.Stop never run.

Of the keys that ARE read, only `dns_servers`/`dns_search`/`dns_records` have a REST writer (handlers/firewall.go:311-319). There is no generic system_config endpoint anywhere in handlers/, and frontend/src/views/Settings.vue imports only uploadRestore, getStorage, runVacuum, listConnectedApps, revokeConnectedApp, listSessions, revokeSession — it has no tuning panel. So `versions_to_keep`, `gc_interval_seconds`, `replay_capture_enabled`, `replay_capture_max_bytes`, `streaming_enabled`, `stream_max_seconds`, `stream_keepalive_seconds`, `activity_retention_days`, `activity_retention_max_rows`, `min_free_disk_mb`, `build_timeout_seconds` are changeable ONLY by opening orva.db with a sqlite3 client. server.go:158-161's comment ("operators can flip the toggle from the Settings page without restarting orvad") describes a UI that does not exist.

• THE CONFIG SURFACE IS 9 ENV VARS OVER ~25 FIELDS — the other 16 are compile-time constants. config/defaults.go pins Server.Host="0.0.0.0" (no bind-address control at all — you cannot make orvad listen on loopback only), ReadTimeoutSec=30, MaxBodyBytes=6MB, Sandbox.NsjailBin="/usr/local/bin/nsjail", Sandbox.RootfsDir, Sandbox.MaxConcurrent, Sandbox.SeccompPolicy="default", Functions.DefaultCPUs=0.5, Functions.MaxCodeSize=50MB, Logging.Format="json", Security.CORSOrigins=["*"]. None is reachable from env, file, flag, or API. Concretely: an operator cannot narrow CORS off `*`, cannot switch seccomp to strict, cannot raise the 6MB body cap, and cannot stop binding all interfaces — without recompiling. `orva serve --port` is the only flag on the entire serve command (backend/cmd/orva/serve.go:27).

• NO TLS ANYWHERE IN THE SERVER. `grep -rn 'ListenAndServeTLS|tls.Config|autocert' backend/` returns zero hits. Server.Start (server.go:509-512) only calls ListenAndServe. ORVA_SECURE_COOKIES exists to mark cookies Secure, and urlhint.BaseURL (backend/internal/urlhint/host.go:28-33) infers https from r.TLS or X-Forwarded-Proto — but r.TLS is always nil in this binary, so every https answer Orva ever gives (OAuth issuer URLs, RFC 8414 metadata, MCP invoke_url, RFC 8707 audience binding) is derived from a client-settable X-Forwarded-Proto header. A reverse proxy is not optional for any non-loopback deployment, and nothing in the code or startup logs says so.

• LOGIN HAS NO BRUTE-FORCE PROTECTION, AND PASSWORD CHANGE REVOKES NOTHING. POST /api/v1/auth/login (handlers/auth.go:94-128) sits behind the `/api/v1/auth/` middleware bypass, has no per-IP bucket, no failed-attempt counter, no lockout, and no delay — bcrypt cost is the only brake. Every other credential surface in the repo has a limiter (OAuth DCR 10/hr/IP, per-function invoke token bucket), login has none. Separately, ChangePassword (auth.go:206-245) → database.UpdateUserPassword (users.go:210-225) issues a single `UPDATE users SET password_hash` and nothing else: `grep 'DELETE FROM sessions'` shows deletion only at users.go:187 (revoke-by-prefix) and users.go:200 (logout). Changing your password does not invalidate any existing session (default 7-day expiry), does not touch api_keys, and does not touch oauth_access_tokens. The documented incident-response move — 'rotate the password' — recovers nothing.

• THE MOST CONCURRENCY-DENSE PACKAGES HAVE ZERO TEST FILES. Packages with no *_test.go at all, by non-test LOC: backend/internal/pool (1565 LOC — the KPA autoscaler, hostMemTracker CAS reservations, the per-function concurrency semaphore, dynamicMax clamping, EWMA sampling), backend/internal/scheduler (863 — cron inflight guard, job claim/backoff, webhook delivery retry), backend/internal/firewall (647 — nft table rendering), backend/internal/ai/agent (507 — approvalNeeded, the security boundary that decides which tool calls pause), backend/internal/server/events (340 — the SSE hub and webhook fanout), backend/internal/secrets (186 — the AES-GCM cipher and .master.key lifecycle), backend/internal/trace (149), backend/internal/auth (84). backend/internal/server/handlers has 37 non-test files and exactly one test (inbound_webhook_trigger_test.go). Whole-repo ratio: 47,108 non-test Go LOC vs 6,714 test LOC (~14%). Combined with the digest's finding that real build+invoke is the one E2E module that skips in CI, the autoscaler and the approval gate are the two highest-risk subsystems and neither has a single automated assertion.

• THE SDK-VERSION DRIFT WARNING CAN NEVER BE SILENT — it fires a false WARN for every function, forever. handlers/sdkversion.go:48 does `if got == version.Version`, comparing the header the in-sandbox SDK sends against the server's release identity. But backend/runtimes/node/orva.js:17 and backend/runtimes/python/orva.py:30 both hardcode `SDK_VERSION = "0.6.0"` (semver), while backend/internal/version/version.go stamps Version as a `vYYYY.MM.DD` git tag or "dev". The two value spaces can never intersect, so the first internal SDK call from every (function, version) tuple logs `WARN sdk version differs from server ... hint: re-deploy the function to refresh the bundled SDK` — advice that will not change the outcome. On a busy instance this is one permanent bogus warning per function in the operator's log.

• ORVA IS SINGLE-USER BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY POLICY. database/users.go exposes CreateUser, but the only caller is AuthHandler.Onboard (handlers/auth.go:41-92), which is first-user-only and 409s afterward. There is no create-user, list-users, delete-user, or role endpoint anywhere in router.go; the AuthHandler surface is Status/Onboard/Login/Me/Refresh/ChangePassword/Sessions/RevokeSession/Logout and nothing else. `users.id` is an INTEGER AUTOINCREMENT (not a UUIDv7 like every other table) and the only per-user scoping in the schema is ai_conversations.user_id, ai_settings.id ('default'|user_id), sessions.user_id and oauth_*.user_id. PRODUCT.md's 'no multi-tenancy' is therefore not a UI decision that could be relaxed — the second operator account is unreachable without new endpoints AND new authorization logic, since api_keys carry no owner column at all.

• THERE IS NO DOWNGRADE OR SCHEMA-COMPAT GUARD ON EITHER UPGRADE PATH. Migrations are unversioned and additive-only (no schema_version row, no migration table), so an OLD binary opening a NEW orva.db just runs its own older CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS set and boots — SELECTs against columns it doesn't know about simply never happen, and any row a newer version wrote into a table the old binary also writes is silently reinterpreted. Backup restore has the same hole from the other direction: backup/backup.go:85-86 records `orva_version` in the manifest and backup.go:207-208 populates it, but readAndVerifyManifest (backup.go:583-595) checks ONLY `format_version > FormatVersion`, and FormatVersion is a const 1 (backup.go:67) that has never been bumped. `orva_version` is written and never read. Restoring a v2026.08 archive into a v2026.02 binary passes every check, and the post-restore os.Exit(0) then hands the operator a running server on a schema its code predates. The only real protection is the digest's already-noted manifest-absent escape hatch (backup.go:583 returns FormatVersion:0 with an empty digest map for legacy archives), which means an attacker-supplied tar without a manifest.json restores with no checksum verification at all.

• REPO HYGIENE: 46 MB OF BUILT BINARIES ARE TRACKED IN GIT. `git ls-files` + du puts test/cli/logs/command-tree/orva-server at 33.7 MB and test/cli/logs/command-tree/orva-cli at 13 MB — both are build outputs of test/cli/command-tree.sh, which rebuilds them on every run, so the checked-in copies are stale and load-bearing for nothing. .gitignore covers test/install/logs/* and test/kata-bench/* but has no test/cli/logs/ entry. Two other .gitignore entries are vestigial from the pre-rename layout: `ui/node_modules/`, `ui/dist/`, `ui/.vite/`, `ui/coverage/` (the directory is frontend/ — saved only by frontend/.gitignore) and `internal/server/ui_dist/` (the path is backend/internal/server/ui_dist/, which is why 78 build artifacts are tracked and ~76 more show as untracked churn). A stray `.astro/` content-collection cache also sits untracked at the repo root with no ignore entry — there is no Astro in this branch, so it is almost certainly leakage from the `web` branch worktree.

• DUPLICATE CLI COMMAND: `orva system db-stats` and `orva system storage` both GET /api/v1/system/storage (cli/commands/system.go:174 and the storage handler at handlers/system.go:383) and differ only in rendering — db-stats prints the page-count/freelist line, storage prints totals. Both decode the same StorageInfo. Given the digest's note that db-stats is also missing from commands_test.go::TestCommandTree's golden paths list, this is a command that is neither covered nor distinct.

• OBSERVABILITY HAS NO PROFILING OR TRACE EXPORT AT ALL. `grep -rn 'pprof|expvar|otel|otlp' backend/ cli/ internal/` returns exactly one hit — a comment in trace/trace.go:4 saying the model is 'intentionally lighter than full OpenTelemetry'. There is no net/http/pprof mount (so no live goroutine dump for the SSE-blocks-shutdown or pool-deadlock class of bug on a production box), no expvar, and no OTLP/Jaeger exporter — traces are W3C-compatible on the wire but terminate in SQLite and are readable only through Orva's own /api/v1/traces UI. The Prometheus surface (28 orva_* series) is invocation- and pool-shaped only: there is no HTTP request counter, no per-status-code counter, no error counter, and no build-queue or webhook-delivery failure metric, so control-plane 5xx and failed webhook deliveries are invisible to any scraper. Every counter is RAM-only and zeroes on restart, and the /metrics alias is unauthenticated (it does not start with /api/).

• TWO SEPARATE UPTIME CLOCKS. server.go:557-565 constructs a second, throwaway handlers.SystemHandler inside runMetricsPublisher with `StartTime: time.Now()` at goroutine-start, distinct from the router's real SystemHandler. Health()'s uptime_seconds (system.go:107) therefore comes from a different baseline than the uptime in the 5-second SSE metrics snapshot the dashboard renders. Also note runMetricsPublisher, builder.NewGC(...).Run, and firewall.Manager.Start are all launched with context.Background() (server.go:200, 206, 213) — none is cancellable, so the GC, the metrics ticker, and the firewall poll loop keep running through Shutdown until the process exits.

name: auth-internal-token-bypass
description: Live-confirmed auth bypass — any non-empty X-Orva-Internal-Token header grants full unauthenticated admin on /api/v1/*
metadata:
  type: project
---

`backend/internal/server/middleware_auth.go:68` short-circuits the API-key/session
gate for ANY request whose `X-Orva-Internal-Token` header is merely **non-empty** —
the value is never compared against `Router.internalToken` there. `JobsHandler.authorize`
(`handlers/jobs.go:28-40`) then falls through to a bare `return true` on token mismatch,
trusting a middleware guarantee that line 68 breaks. `ai_handler.go` grants any non-api_key
actor `{read,write,invoke,admin}`.

**Confirmed live on the :3000 dev instance (2026-08-07):** `curl -H "X-Orva-Internal-Token: bogus"
http://localhost:3000/api/v1/functions` → 200 with the full functions list; `/api/v1/keys`
(admin-only) also returned real key rows. Baseline with no header → 401.

Still present on **origin/main** (HEAD 8284b89c) at the same line — not a stale-worktree
artifact. The real internal token is only correctly checked by the per-handler `authorize()`
funcs in kv.go / internal_invoke.go / spans.go / cron.go, but the middleware bypass makes
the header a skeleton key regardless.

Note: the local checkout is ~62 commits behind origin/main; a few AI-stream findings
(EventDone-on-reset, unguarded cache_control) ARE fixed upstream, but this bypass is not.
See [[dev-merge-gate]], [[ai-chat-hang-rootcause]].

Now the complete analysis. The multi-agent read covered every subsystem against real source, and I've fact-checked the load-bearing claims (including confirming the auth bypass live).

---

# Orva — complete codebase analysis

## 1. What it is

**A self-hosted Function-as-a-Service platform for a single operator on their own hardware.** Write a JS/TS/Python function → deploy → Orva runs it in an nsjail sandbox and serves it over HTTP. One Go binary (or one Docker container) is the whole system: runtime + dashboard + CLI + MCP server + an in-product agentic AI assistant. It's the Lambda/Workers loop without a cloud account.

- **License:** Apache-2.0. **Age:** ~195 commits since 2026-04-28, two authors (Harsh-2002 + Anurag Vishwakarma). **Latest tag:** `v2026.08.05`.
- **Positioning** (`PRODUCT.md`): exactly one technical operator, one host, no multi-tenancy — "operator-grade, calm, technical," dark-theme-only. Self-described as *not* production/customer-facing grade yet.
- **Runtimes:** two generic IDs, latest-stable only — `node` (Node.js 24, also TS) and `python` (3.14). Collapsed from four versioned IDs in commit `11b3635c`.

⚠️ **Important context:** your local checkout is **62 commits behind `origin/main`** (HEAD `8284b89c`). A few findings below are already fixed upstream — I've flagged each. The dev instance binary on :3000 is older still.

---

## 2. Repo structure

Single Go module `github.com/Harsh-2002/Orva` rooted at the repo (not `backend/`), so `go.mod`/`go.sum` live at the top.

| Path | Role | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `backend/` | Go server, 221 `.go` files | `cmd/orva` = entry; `internal/` = subsystems; `runtimes/` = adapter source |
| `cli/` | Slim standalone CLI | `cli/commands/` is the **single source of truth** for subcommands; the server imports it |
| `internal/` | Shared by both binaries | `ids/` (UUIDv7), `client/` (HTTP + `~/.orva/config.yaml`) |
| `frontend/` | Vue 3 dashboard | Vite 7 + Pinia 3 + Tailwind 4 + CodeMirror 6; embedded via `//go:embed ui_dist` |
| `docs/` | 16 reference docs | `reference.md` canonical, fanned out to 3 consumers |
| `test/` | Shell + Python e2e | `test/e2e/run.py` drives 22 modules against a live server |
| `scripts/` | Installers + entrypoint | `install.sh` (1085 lines), `install-cli.{sh,ps1}`, `entrypoint.sh`, `build-rootfs.sh` |

**One program, two roles.** `orva serve` = daemon; every other subcommand = client. `backend/cmd/orva/main.go` calls `commands.NewRoot()` then bolts on `serve`/`setup`/`init`. The slim CLI (`cli/cmd/orva`) imports only `cli/commands` — no server packages — so it's ~9 MB vs the ~70 MB server binary.

**Nine build-critical `//go:embed` + sync steps** the Makefile automates: `adapters-embed` (copies `runtimes/` → `backend/cmd/orva/adapters/`), `docs-embed` (copies `docs/reference.md` → mcp + frontend + cli), `embed` (UI dist). Bare `go build` doesn't run these — you get a stale snapshot.

---

## 3. The execution engine (the core)

I traced a public HTTP invocation hop-by-hop through real code:

```
HTTP → corsMiddleware → bodySize → auth → requestID → logger → mux   (built inside-out, router.go:536)
  → InvokeHandler.ServeHTTP                                    (handlers/invoke.go:50)
      ├ DB.MatchRoute() custom route, else extractFnID("/fn/{id}")
      ├ Registry.Get(fnID)          sync.Map cache → SQLite fallback
      ├ status gate → per-fn auth_mode → per-fn rate limit (token bucket, in-handler)
      ├ execID = ids.New() (UUIDv7); trace span stamped (honors W3C traceparent)
      └ Proxy.Forward(...)                                     (proxy/proxy.go)
           ├ ReadAll body, rewrite path, lowercase headers, inject x-orva-* headers
           ├ (optional) captureRequest — redacts auth headers, for replay
           └ Pool.Acquire(ctx, fnID)                           (pool/pool.go:223)
                ├ host-wide sandbox.Limiter.TryAcquire (semaphore)
                ├ per-fn concurrency semaphore
                └ warm idle worker  OR  spawnFn() cold start
                     └ sandbox.Spawn → exec nsjail → chroot → adapter
  → 4-byte big-endian length + JSON frame over worker stdin/stdout
  ← "response"  |  "response_start" + "chunk"(base64)… + "response_end"
  → AsyncInsertExecutionFinal (batched writer, off hot path)
  → eventHub.Publish("execution")  AND loggerMiddleware Publish("activity")  → SSE → dashboard
```

**nsjail argv** (`sandbox.go:176`): `-Mo --chroot <rootfs> -R <codeDir>:/code -T /tmp --rlimit_as max -Q`, plus, *only when a writable cgroup-v2 delegate exists*, `--use_cgroupv2 --cgroup_mem_max <1.5× mem> --cgroup_pids_max <N> --cgroup_cpu_ms_per_sec`, plus `--seccomp_string`, plus every env var as explicit `--env K=V`, terminating in `-- /usr/local/bin/{node,python3} /opt/orva/adapter.{js,py}`. `--time_limit` is deliberately dropped — Go-side `context.WithTimeout` + `Worker.Kill()` gives ms resolution.

**The adapter protocol is length-prefixed JSON over stdin/stdout** — not a socket, not HTTP. `writeFrame`/`readFrame` (`worker.go:603`), 64 MB frame cap. Node/Python adapters both use 4-byte big-endian framing. Streaming is real: a `response_start` frame flips `DispatchResult.Streaming`, and the caller pumps `NextFrame` (base64 chunks) until `end`.

**Zombie reaping is centralized** — exactly one `cmd.Wait()` goroutine per worker, started in `Spawn`, signalling via `waitDone`; `Quit`/`Kill` never call `Wait()`. This is a scar from a real v0.4 `<defunct> nsjail` bug after streaming-client disconnects.

**Warm pools + Knative-KPA autoscaler** (`pool/autoscaler.go`): 60s stable window + 6s panic window, 1s tick, EWMA. `dynamicMax` is bounded by *both* CPU and a host-memory budget (`hostmem.go` refuses spawns past ~80% reservation, per-worker budget = 1.5× declared memory).

**Deploys are content-addressed** (`builder/`): each version is `versions/<sha256>/`, immutable, with an `.orva-ready` marker. `current` is a symlink retargeted by an atomic `rename(2)` (`activate.go`). Identical redeploy = cache hit. Rollback = symlink retarget. GC deletes versions outside the keep window. `npm install`/`pip install`/`tsc` run **host-side**, not in the sandbox. Build queue = `NumCPU()` workers draining a 64-slot channel, serialized against rollback by a per-function lock.

---

## 4. Data layer

**SQLite, WAL mode, two connection pools:** one `write` pool pinned to `MaxOpenConns(1)`, one read-only pool sized to `NumCPU()`. Pragmas ride in the DSN (modernc.org/sqlite honors them per-connection).

**34 tables**, grouped: functions/executions/execution_logs/execution_requests/execution_log_entries; deployments/pool_config/build_logs; routes/cron_schedules/jobs; kv_store/fixtures/function_secrets; users/sessions/api_keys/system_config/activity_log; event_subscriptions/webhook_deliveries/inbound_webhooks; user_spans; egress_blocklist; channels/channel_functions; oauth_clients/oauth_authorization_codes/oauth_access_tokens; ai_conversations/ai_messages/ai_tool_calls/ai_provider_configs/ai_settings.

**Migrations are unversioned and additive-only** — no migration table, no schema_version. `Migrate()` runs one giant `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` then a slice of idempotent `ALTER`s on every boot, plus data fixups (`dropExecutionRequestsFK` rebuilds `execution_requests` without its legacy FK). **UUIDv7 everywhere** except `users.id` (INTEGER AUTOINCREMENT), giving time-sortable, append-only B-tree inserts on the hot `executions` table.

**Async write path:** `db.AsyncExec` pushes onto a 1024-slot channel; a single consumer batches ≤50 jobs / 50ms into one transaction on the lone writer connection. Keeps the proxy hot path off synchronous DB calls. **Secrets:** AES-256-GCM under a lazily-generated `.master.key` (0600). **Backups:** `VACUUM INTO` → consistent snapshot with no `-wal`/`-shm`, tar'd with a manifest.

---

## 5. AI assistant + MCP server

**MCP server** at `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP transport, protocol 2025-11-25). **72 tools** registered via `regAddTool` across 17 `tools_*.go` files — the count that ships in README/docs (70) is stale (see findings). Auth accepts API keys, OAuth 2.1 access tokens, or channel tokens. **Agent channels** bundle N functions under one `orva_chn_<hex>` token; presenting it at `/mcp` exposes *only* those functions as invoke-only tools.

**The single-source-of-truth trick:** every tool is declared once via `regAddTool`, which registers it with **both** the external MCP server **and** the in-process agent registry (`mcp.BuildAgentRegistry`), gated to the principal's perms. Same name/schema/destructive-hint feed both fronts, so they never drift.

**In-product AI chat** (`/api/v1/ai/*`, SSE): browser POSTs over `fetch`+`ReadableStream` (not EventSource — the chat POST carries a body). `ai.Manager` wires a SQLite chat store, the secrets cipher (BYO provider keys encrypted at rest), the tool registry, and the **embedded Bifrost LLM gateway** (`github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core` — this dependency is why the module needs Go ≥1.26). The `agent.Runner` runs a ≈25-iteration loop: stream turn → emit SSE deltas → detect tool calls → **dispatch in-process as a Go call** (no MCP transport, no HTTP) → feed results back. Nine SSE event names (`conversation`/`message_start`/`delta`/`thinking`/`tool_call`/`tool_result`/…).

**Two independent write-safety gates:** (1) a per-conversation approval policy (`all_writes` default / `destructive_only` / `auto`) checked in `approvalNeeded`, and (2) a code-enforced `confirm=true` requirement on the 16 destructive tools regardless of policy. Conversations are a shared operator space, serialized by a per-conversation try-lock (overlapping turns → 409); editing/deleting a message truncates the tail by `seq` (no branching history).

---

## 6. Auth, security & networking

**Middleware chain:** `CORS → BodySize → Auth → RequestID → Logger → Handler`. Auth only runs on `/api/*`; `/fn/`, `/mcp`, `/webhook/`, custom routes, and `/metrics` bypass it (per-function auth enforced inside `InvokeHandler`). API keys are SHA-256-hashed and cached; permissions are `read/invoke/write/admin`; channel and OAuth tokens are explicitly rejected at `/api/v1/*`.

**Isolation model:** `-Mo` user namespace maps inside-UID 0 → unprivileged host UID (all 64 capability bits cleared outside the namespace), read-only `/code` bind, private tmpfs `/tmp`, cgroup-v2 caps when delegated, seccomp filter. Egress is **opt-in** — default is an isolated net namespace (loopback only); `network_mode: egress` adds nsjail `--user_net` + firewall-managed `/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/hosts` binds. The egress firewall is a **global nftables blocklist**, not a per-function allowlist, and there's no DNS interception.

**OAuth 2.1 authorization server** (lets claude.ai/ChatGPT add `/mcp` via the browser): `authorization_code` + `refresh_token` grants only; mandatory PKCE S256; RFC 7591 dynamic client registration (rate-limited 10/hr/IP); RFC 8414 + OIDC discovery metadata; RFC 8707 resource-indicator audience binding; RFC 7009 revocation. Access tokens `orva_oat_*` (1h), refresh `orva_ort_*` (30d, always rotated).

**Runtime isolation reality** (from the docs' own evaluations): works under **runc** (default) and **Kata** (~75-80% throughput, hypervisor isolation); does **not** work under **gVisor** — nsjail's nested-namespace `clone()` is rejected by the sentry (the gVisor CI leg was removed 2026-05-13).

---

## 7. Frontend

Vue 3.5 `<script setup>` + Router 4 + Pinia 3 + Tailwind 4 (`@tailwindcss/postcss`) + Vite 7 + CodeMirror 6 + markdown-it. No TypeScript. ~23 views, all lazy `import()` so Vite emits per-view chunks. Design system lives in `style.css` as a Tailwind `@theme` block — deep-purple, dark-only (`--color-background #12111C`, `--color-primary #553F83`).

**State:** 5 Pinia stores — `auth`, `system` (seeds metrics/functions/executions, patches from SSE), `events` (one `EventSource('/api/v1/events')` per tab, fans out named events), `confirm`, `ai` (index-based streaming timeline). **SSE consumed three ways:** the global EventSource, the AI chat's `fetch`+`ReadableStream`, and per-deployment build-log streams. Notable UX: Cmd-K command palette with `g f`/`g i` sequences, CodeMirror editor with language `Compartment` swapping, live diff view, live activity feed. Built dist embeds into the Go binary via `make embed`.

---

## 8. CLI

**Command tree** (~28 top-level, single library in `cli/commands/`): `deploy`, `invoke`, `logs`, `diff`, `rollback`, `functions`, `deployments`, `cron`, `jobs`, `kv`, `secrets`, `routes`, `webhooks`, `firewall`, `dns`, `fixtures`, `channels`, `keys`, `activity`, `traces`, `system`, `backup`, `login`, `chat`, `docs`, `upgrade`, `completion`.

**Config precedence:** flags > env (`ORVA_ENDPOINT`/`ORVA_API_KEY`) > `~/.orva/config.yaml` > default `http://localhost:8443`. **Output contract:** data → stdout (indented JSON, `-o json`), status → stderr, suppressed by `-q`. Name→ID resolution uses `ids.IsUUID` then `GET /functions?limit=10000`. `orva chat` streams assistant deltas raw (optional glamour render on TTY); `orva upgrade` is a go-selfupdate round-trip with checksum validation, arch-pinned filter.

---

## 9. GitHub Actions — six workflows

**Policy: verify on push/PR, ship on tag.** The release pipeline runs *zero* tests.

- **`ci.yml`** — PR + push-to-main, path-filtered (docs-only skips). 4 parallel jobs: `lint` (owns *all* repo shellcheck — `dash -n` + `shellcheck -s sh` on POSIX installers, `bash -n` on the rest), `go` (1.26 on ubuntu-24.04: `make embed` + `adapters-embed`, `go vet`, `go test -race`, build), `ui` (vite build), `docker` (smoke build, no push). No caches anywhere — deliberate.
- **`e2e.yml`** — push to main/dev + all PRs. Builds, boots `orva serve`, waits for `/system/health`, runs `test/e2e/run.py` with the `.admin-key`. Drives every domain + CLI + the AI loop via a **mock LLM** (no provider key). Real-nsjail scenarios self-skip in CI.
- **`release.yml`** — on `v*` tags. **`gate`** job polls the Actions API for the tagged commit: `e2e.yml` **hard** (must be green), `ci.yml` **soft** (path-filtered → may be absent), ~20-min cap, refuses to build on red, `force=true` bypasses. Build jobs (`needs: gate`): `build-orva` (amd64/arm64), `build-cli` (6 targets incl. Windows `.exe`), `build-nsjail` (**inside `debian:bookworm-slim`** — building on ubuntu-24.04 produced `GLIBC_2.38 not found` at install targets), `build-rootfs` (`docker export` + zstd). `docker-image` builds per-arch on native runners (no QEMU), pushes **by digest only**; `docker-manifest` stitches a multi-arch **`:latest` only** (no per-version image tag — versioning lives in the GitHub Release); `cleanup-ghcr` prunes everything else.
- **`install-e2e.yml`** — real install+smoke+uninstall in privileged systemd-in-docker across 6 distros (`arch`/`alpine321` are `continue-on-error`). Runs on `release: published` (not main-push — the old release is gone and the new one isn't up yet, so "latest" would 404).
- **`cli-e2e.yml`** — unit + cross-build + command-tree golden diff on PRs; expensive macOS/Windows legs gated behind `paths-filter`.
- **`cleanup-ghcr.yml`** — manual standalone prune.

**Build identity:** three `-X` ldflags (`version.Version/Commit/BuildTime`) flow Makefile → Dockerfile → release.yml, surface at `/system/health` + Settings. Go ignores unknown `-X` targets silently, so renaming the version package must be lock-step across all three.

---

## 10. Testing

~14% test-to-code ratio (6,714 test LOC / 47,108 non-test). Go unit tests concentrate in `server` (8), `oauth` (5), `mcp` (5), `database` (4). The Python e2e harness (`test/e2e/`) boots a real server and drives 22 domain modules incl. the AI loop via `mock_llm.py`. Shell suites in `test/` (loadtest, atscale, egress, tracing, rollback…) and `test/install/` (distro matrix) + `test/cli/` (build matrix, install, upgrade, command-tree golden). **Gap:** the most concurrency-dense packages — `pool` (autoscaler), `scheduler`, `firewall`, `ai/agent` (the approval gate), `events`, `secrets` — have **zero** `*_test.go`.

---

## 11. Findings — verified discrepancies

I adversarially fact-checked the load-bearing claims against source; each has a file:line.

**🔴 Critical — unauthenticated admin bypass (confirmed live).** `middleware_auth.go:68` short-circuits the auth gate for *any* request with a **non-empty** `X-Orva-Internal-Token` header — the value is never compared there. `jobs.go:28-40` then falls through to a bare `return true`, and `ai_handler.go` grants any non-api_key actor full `{read,write,invoke,admin}`. I confirmed it on the :3000 dev instance: `curl -H "X-Orva-Internal-Token: bogus" .../api/v1/functions` → **200** with the full list; `/api/v1/keys` (admin-only) returned real key rows; baseline no-header → 401. **Still present on `origin/main`.** (Saved to memory.)

**🟠 Seccomp is audit-only, not enforcing.** `BuildSeccompPolicy` emits `… USE orva DEFAULT LOG` (`seccomp.go:191`) — Kafel `DEFAULT LOG` = `SECCOMP_RET_LOG`, which *permits and logs* every out-of-policy syscall. The matching `--seccomp_log` flag is never passed. It's also **global, not per-function** (`pool.go:612` passes `nil` allow/block; `proxy.go` discards the per-fn arg). `docs/SECURITY.md` presents seccomp as a blocking `~150-syscall` boundary.

**🟠 Warm workers launch with `--cgroup_pids_max 0`.** `spawnFn`'s `ExecConfig` never sets `MaxPids`; the `32` default lives only in `sandbox.Execute()`, which has **zero callers** (dead). So the pid cap is unset on the live path when a cgroup delegate exists.

**🟡 Redeploys are not zero-downtime, despite the code comment.** `invoke.go:110` gates the `building`-status passthrough on `hasPriorCode()`, which stats the **legacy** `/code` dir that `migrate_fs.go` deletes and the versioned layout never recreates — so a first/failed-redeploy returns `503 BUILDING`. (Redeploy of an *already-active* function is fine — it keeps serving old warm workers until activation, so the practical impact is narrow.) Relatedly, `invoke.go:175`'s `codeDir` and the whole `env` map are computed then discarded (`proxy.go:191` `_ = codeDir`); the real path is `pool.go:544` `.../current`.

**🟡 MCP tool count is 72, not 70.** `grep -c regAddTool` = 72. README, `backend/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/reference.md` (says 69 *and* 70 in different spots), and `Docs.vue` all disagree. *(README counts were corrected on `origin/main` in `ec18672d` — verify which figure landed.)*

**🟡 `install.sh --docker` writes `image: …/orva:${VERSION}`** but release.yml only pushes `:latest`, so generated compose 404s; the heredoc also omits every sandbox-critical flag (`pid: host`, `cgroup: host`, `NET_ADMIN`, `/dev/net/tun`). `install.sh` `verify()` is also fail-open when a checksum entry is missing, and `ORVA_SKIP_VERIFY` exists only in a comment.

**🟡 Health check is a liveness stub that cannot fail** — `Health()` returns hardcoded `"status":"healthy"`/`"database":"ok"`; never pings the DB, stats nsjail, or checks the rootfs. Everything downstream (Docker HEALTHCHECK, install.sh, e2e readiness) keys off it, so a box with a locked DB or missing nsjail reports green while every invocation 503s.

**🟡 Graceful shutdown is broken by its own SSE streams.** `httpServer.Shutdown(30s)` waits for connections to idle, but SSE streams never idle and `events.Hub` has no `Close()`. One open dashboard tab or `orva logs -f` makes every SIGTERM block the full 30s → under Docker's 10s stop-timeout, a SIGKILL every restart, so `ai.Manager.Close()` and `Scheduler.Stop` never run.

**🟢 Other confirmed drift:** `PRODUCT.md` still says "Node 22/24, Python 3.13/3.14"; README says "16 templates" (code has 21) and "70-tool"; `sandbox.go:58` comment says `--use_pasta` but code emits `--user_net`; `docs/ERRORS.md` documents 24 slugs, code emits 46+ (and mislabels `RATE_LIMITED` as "not yet emitted" / `VALIDATION` vs `VALIDATION_ERROR`); `install-e2e.yml` path-filters on a non-existent `scripts/uninstall.sh`; `/metrics` emits no `# TYPE`/`# HELP` and double-declares one family; the config surface is 9 env vars over ~25 fields (no bind-address, CORS, seccomp, or body-cap control without recompiling); no TLS in the server (reverse proxy is mandatory but undocumented as such); login has no brute-force protection and password change revokes no sessions/keys; 46 MB of built binaries tracked in `test/cli/logs/`.

*Already fixed upstream (worktree is stale):* the AI stream reporting a provider reset as `EventDone` (origin/main uses `pump()` → "provider stream ended unexpectedly"), and `cache_control` sent to non-Anthropic providers (`566cfcc3`).

---

If you'd like, I can go deeper on any one subsystem, open a PR fixing the auth bypass + seccomp `DEFAULT LOG` (the two real security issues), or reconcile the docs drift against `origin/main` ahead of the next release per your docs-before-release rule.

input.content:
# Orva — fix & test plan (findings from the codebase analysis)

## Context

A deep multi-agent analysis of Orva surfaced one **live-confirmed unauthenticated
admin bypass** plus a set of reliability, install, and hygiene defects. Findings were
re-verified against **`origin/main` (HEAD `8284b89c`)**, not the local checkout — the
local `main` is **62 commits behind** and `origin/dev` is 45 behind `origin/main`, so
**`origin/main` is the live tip and the only valid base for this work.**

Several earlier findings were already fixed on `origin/main` and are **out of scope**:
seccomp is now enforcing (`USE orva DEFAULT ERRNO(1)`), README tool count corrected to
72, the AI-stream reset + `cache_control` bugs, PRODUCT.md runtime versions, and the
46 MB of tracked test binaries. What remains is below.

Scope decided with the user: **fix everything (High + Medium + Low)** on **one feature
branch off `origin/main` → one bundled PR**. All line numbers below are `origin/main`.

> ⚠️ Implementation must start by syncing to `origin/main` (Step 0). Do **not** edit the
> stale local tree — its line numbers and file contents differ.

---

## Step 0 — Base the work correctly
- `git fetch origin`; create the feature branch off `origin/main` (e.g. `git switch -c fix/security-reliability-sweep origin/main`).
- Per repo policy (memory `dev-merge-gate`, `docs-before-release-gate`): this lands via PR with CI+e2e green, and the real build is deployed + live-tested on the `:3000` dev instance before merge. The `:3000` binary is stale, so redeploy the fixed build there for the manual auth-bypass re-check.

---

## HIGH

### H1 — Unauthenticated admin bypass  🔴 (live-confirmed)
`backend/internal/server/middleware_auth.go:68` short-circuits the auth gate for **any
non-empty** `X-Orva-Internal-Token` — value never compared. `handlers/jobs.go:39` then
`return true` unconditionally, and `ai_handler.go` grants any non-api_key actor full
`{read,write,invoke,admin}`. Only `/api/v1/jobs` actually depends on this branch
(the SDK's `_kv`/`_internal` paths use the earlier prefix branch at lines 58-64 + their
own per-handler `ConstantTimeCompare`).

**Fix:**
- Thread the real token into the middleware: change `authMiddleware(db, keyCache, next)`
  → `authMiddleware(db, keyCache, internalToken, next)`; update the call site
  `router.go:542` to pass `r.internalToken` (already stored, from `generateInternalToken()`
  at `server.go:107/500`).
- Replace the line-68 test with a constant-time compare (`crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`,
  guard `internalToken != ""`). **Match** → tag sdk actor, pass. **Mismatch** → do NOT
  short-circuit; fall through to normal session/API-key auth (a stray header on a real
  request still authenticates; a bogus-token-only request → 401).
- Defense-in-depth: in `handlers/jobs.go` `authorize()`, replace the bare `return true`
  fallback with a check that a `*Actor` is present in context (middleware sets `WithActor`
  on every authenticated path) — reuse the existing `ActorFrom`/context helper.

### H2 — Health check is a stub that cannot fail
`handlers/system.go:106-143` `Health()` returns hardcoded `"status":"healthy"` /
`"database":{"status":"ok"}`; never pings the DB or checks the sandbox. Every recovery
mechanism (Docker HEALTHCHECK, `install.sh` wait, e2e readiness) keys off it, so a locked
`orva.db` reports green.

**Fix (with a hard CI constraint):**
- Add a real DB liveness check — add `database.(*Database).Ping()` running `SELECT 1` on the
  read pool; on failure return **HTTP 503** + `"status":"degraded"`, else 200. This is the
  hard gate (a dead DB truly means "cannot serve").
- Surface sandbox state (`os.Stat(cfg.Sandbox.NsjailBin)` + rootfs dir) as an **informational**
  `checks.sandbox` field only — **must NOT 503 when nsjail is absent**, because `e2e.yml`
  boots the server without nsjail and requires `/health`=200 ("the API/DB come up without
  nsjail"). Breaking that would red the e2e gate.
- Preserve the existing top-level JSON keys the dashboard reads; add a nested `checks` object.

---

## MEDIUM

### M1 — SSE streams block graceful shutdown → SIGKILL every restart
`events/hub.go` has no `Close()`; `server.go:518` calls `httpServer.Shutdown` first, which
waits for SSE connections that never idle. One open dashboard tab or `orva logs -f` hangs
SIGTERM the full 30s → Docker SIGKILLs → `ai.Manager.Close()` / `Scheduler.Stop` skipped.
**Fix:** add `Hub.Close()` that closes all subscriber channels under lock (make `unsubscribe`
idempotent); call it in `Server.Shutdown` **before** `httpServer.Shutdown` so the SSE handler
loops (`events/handler.go`, exit on hub-closed channel) unblock. Stretch: give
`runMetricsPublisher`/GC/firewall a cancellable context instead of `context.Background()`.

### M2 — Warm workers launch with `--cgroup_pids_max 0`

  hard gate (a dead DB truly means "cannot serve").

  `checks.sandbox` field only — **must NOT 503 when nsjail is absent**, because `e2e.yml`
  boots the server without nsjail and requires `/health`=200 ("the API/DB come up without
  nsjail"). Breaking that would red the e2e gate.

delegate exists (fork-bomb cap disabled).

the pool template.

publishes **`:latest` only** (release.yml confirms no per-version tag) → `docker compose`

and README `docker run` so all three agree. (Re-verify `verify()` while here — the
fail-open strings are gone on `origin/main`, likely already fixed.)

unreachable, so a moderately-sized function 413s.

rely on `ParseMultipartForm(50MB)` + `Functions.MaxCodeSize` (50 MB) as the real cap.

**Fix:** add a per-IP failed-attempt limiter returning 429 + `Retry-After`, reusing the
token-bucket pattern in `oauth/ratelimit.go` (or `handlers/ratelimit.go`).

`database.UpdateUserPassword` (`users.go:210-223`) only runs `UPDATE users` — existing
sessions (7-day TTL) survive a password change, so incident-response rotation is inert.

one) via a new `DeleteUserSessions(userID, exceptToken)` mirroring the `DELETE FROM sessions`
pattern at `users.go:187/200`. API keys carry no owner column (single-user) — leave keys
out of scope with a code comment noting why.

creates (dead), and `invoke.go:175`'s `codeDir`/`env`/`seccompPolicy` args are discarded

`builder.ResolveActiveHash`) so the intended zero-downtime-on-redeploy actually works on the
versioned layout. Optional cleanup: prune the discarded params from `proxy.Forward`'s
signature.

97	   ```bash
98	   git tag -a v2026.05.03 -m "Orva v2026.05.03" && git push origin v2026.05.03
99	   ```
100	   The Release workflow's **`gate`** job confirms `CI` already concluded `success` for
101	   that exact commit (a status lookup — seconds, not a test run; it polls briefly if you tag
